# Pulp Wars Ruleset 7: current rules

**Status:** authoritative description of the current Ruleset 7 runtime,
`pulp-wars-poc-7r110`, for all nine offered factions, Human (`ORIGINAL`),
Undead (`UNDEAD`), Goblin (`GOBLIN`), Dinosaur (`DINOSAUR`), Martian
(`MARTIAN`), Ice Folk (`ICE_FOLK`), Dwarf (`DWARF`), Candy (`CANDY`), and
the Cultists (`CULT`). The ninth faction, the Cultists of the Ancient Ones,
is folded in by `pulp_wars-mch9.21`: its rules (Favour with Sacrifice,
Seize, and Offering; the daemons and the channel that holds them;
Unbound, the rampage, and Bind again; the rituals Star-fall and the Great
Summoning, and the Herald; the hexes and tricks) are
[section 26](#26-cultist-faction-rules), its roster is in
[section 11](#11-unit-roster), its technology in
[section 6.2](#62-technology-tree), and its Normal AI in
[section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary); [its spec](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md) is
kept as the design record, and the notes of its six engine steps are in
[section 1](#1-identity-and-compatibility). The Cult redesign
([its design](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md), approved by the user on
2026-10-16) is built: each step folded its part into section 26 as it
landed (`7r85`: the roster step; `7r88`: Star-fall alone with Join the
chant, Switcheroo at 4, the daemons' advance after a kill, and the Unbound
target order; `7r89`: the Favour economy and the warden; `7r90`: the Imp;
`7r91`: the Gibbering Mass; then, with no identity change, the Normal AI,
the interface, the art, and campaign mission 10), and section 26 describes
the Cult as it now plays (`pulp_wars-mch9.47`). It
folds in
revision 12 (free opening technology, Fruit visible from the start, Fertile
Ground revealed by Gathering, resources kept under improvements, Normal AI
opening research, and Raider Escape; no separate overlay document) and the
overlays of revisions [13](RULESET_7_REVISION_13_UNDEAD.md) (the Undead
faction), [14](RULESET_7_REVISION_14_BALANCE.md) (Plague, Bitten, the
unanswered Vampire, villages, and income caps),
[15](RULESET_7_REVISION_15_BALANCE.md) (three-turn Plague, 18-HP Zombie),
[16](RULESET_7_REVISION_16.md) (16a: orthogonal Shallow Water and the capital
growth guarantee; 16b: 2-tile boats and landing; 16c: economy deflation),
[17](RULESET_7_REVISION_17_GOBLINS.md) (the Goblin faction, with the
`pulp_wars-0ao.7` tuned numbers), [18](RULESET_7_REVISION_18.md) (friendly
pass-through, the Road half cost by origin, and the fixed Showcase setup),
[19](RULESET_7_REVISION_19_DINOSAURS.md) (the Dinosaur faction) as amended by
[20](RULESET_7_REVISION_20.md) (the Triceratops's Charge! replacing
Stampede, the T-Rex cost and hatch time, Nesting's city slot, Wallbreaker,
and the full heal of a Promotion or growth stage),
[21](RULESET_7_REVISION_21_ACHIEVEMENTS.md) (the Conqueror, Land Baron, Sea
Dog, and Slayer achievements), the `pulp_wars-0hi.3` coarse balance
numbers of `pulp-wars-poc-7r23`
([revision 20 section 6.3](RULESET_7_REVISION_20.md#63-tuning-record): Human
Fighter, Raider, and Marksman 12 HP, Guard 17, Caveman 10), the
[Martian overlay](RULESET_7_MARTIANS.md) (the Martian faction: engine
`pulp_wars-t6s.2` at `pulp-wars-poc-7r22`, Normal AI `pulp_wars-t6s.3`, UI
`pulp_wars-t6s.4` with the production art of `pulp_wars-t6s.6`, and the
`pulp_wars-t6s.5` coarse balance number of `pulp-wars-poc-7r25`, Colossus
Defense 2.5, from its
[tuning record](RULESET_7_MARTIANS.md#165-tuning-record) and its
implementation notes in
[section 19](RULESET_7_MARTIANS.md#19-implementation-notes-pulp_wars-t6s2)),
the [Ice Folk overlay](RULESET_7_ICE_FOLK.md) (the Ice Folk faction:
engine `pulp_wars-7g3.3` at `pulp-wars-poc-7r24`, Normal AI

`pulp_wars-jdb.7` coarse balance, closed on a small sample with no number
changed

with its Normal AI notes in
[section 14.1](RULESET_7_CANDY.md#141-implementation-status-pulp_wars-jdb4),
its engine notes in
[section 23](RULESET_7_CANDY.md#23-implementation-notes-pulp_wars-jdb3),

The Undead, the Goblins, the Dinosaurs, the Martians, the Ice Folk, the
Dwarves, the Candy, and the Cultists are part of the ordinary game: faction choice is offered in every
match setup, with no development flag. The numbers of the Cultists were
checked against the engine code at `pulp-wars-poc-7r78`
(`pulp_wars-mch9.21`) and again, after the Cult redesign, at
`pulp-wars-poc-7r91` (`pulp_wars-mch9.47`). The numbers of the first five
factions were checked against the engine code at `pulp-wars-poc-7r25`, those
of the Ice Folk at `pulp-wars-poc-7r30` (`pulp_wars-7g3.8`), those of
the Dwarves at `pulp-wars-poc-7r31` (`pulp_wars-78i.8`), and those of the
Candy at `pulp-wars-poc-7r38` (`pulp_wars-jdb.3`) and again at
`pulp-wars-poc-7r41` (`pulp_wars-jdb.8`); `pulp-wars-poc-7r24`
(`pulp_wars-7g3.3`) registers the Ice Folk and changes no rule of the other
factions, `pulp-wars-poc-7r26` (`pulp_wars-9s0.2`) changes only Pangea map
generation (the coast ring, [section 2.3](#23-map-types)),
`pulp-wars-poc-7r27` (`pulp_wars-7g3.7`) changes only the Ice Folk Yeti (9
HP, Defense 1.5), `pulp-wars-poc-7r28` (`pulp_wars-9s0.5`) adds the **Rift**
terrain, folded in directly here (sections [2.3](#23-map-types),
[2.4](#24-biomes-terrain-and-resources), [8.1](#81-common-placement-gates),
[12.1](#121-movement), and [13.4](#134-after-combat)); its full ruling of
every interaction is the [Rift overlay](RULESET_7_RIFT.md),
`pulp-wars-poc-7r29` (`pulp_wars-w5j.1`) makes every player play a
different faction, folded in directly in [section 2.1](#21-match-setup)
from the [unique-factions overlay](RULESET_7_UNIQUE_FACTIONS.md), and
`pulp-wars-poc-7r30` (`pulp_wars-78i.3`) registers the Dwarves and changes
no rule of the other factions (the per-unit living test, the one occupancy
predicate, and the board-or-all-units accessors it introduced return what
the former rules returned in a match without a Dwarf seat), and
`pulp-wars-poc-7r31` (`pulp_wars-78i.7`) changes only the Dwarf
Gyrocopter's bomb (5, and 6 with Dive), `pulp-wars-poc-7r32`
(`pulp_wars-b5f.2`) gives the Martian Grunt a ray pistol (range 1–2, Attack
1.5, 3 Coins) and the Tripod range 2 only with Sight 2
([section 11](#11-unit-roster), [section 20](#20-martian-faction-rules)),
`pulp-wars-poc-7r33` (`pulp_wars-b5f.3`, the engine step of the
[Mind Control overlay](RULESET_7_MIND_CONTROL.md)) makes a mind-controlled
unit keep its type and abilities under the Brain's owner, one per Brain,
released to its owner when the Brain is lost
([section 20.8](#208-mind-control),
[section 20.9](#209-mind-controlled-units)); matches without a Martian seat
are unchanged, `pulp-wars-poc-7r34` (`pulp_wars-68k.2`, the engine step
of the [campaign design](CAMPAIGN.md)) adds the `MISSION` setup, a
hand-authored board built from a registered mission, and mission-forbidden
technologies ([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup),
[section 6.1](#61-research-cost)); every other match is unchanged,
`pulp-wars-poc-7r35` (`pulp_wars-737.2`, engine step I of the
[map curiosities spec](RULESET_7_MAP_CURIOSITIES.md)) adds the
Curiosities setup option (on by default) and the rare Fountain of Youth,
Shrine, and Sunken Wreck ([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)); with the
option off, a match is the `7r34` match, `pulp-wars-poc-7r36`
(`pulp_wars-737.3`, engine step II) adds the Giant Spider, a unit owned by
the neutral owner that acts in a neutral turn after every round
([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)); a match without a Spider plays as
before, and `pulp-wars-poc-7r37` (`pulp_wars-1wy.3`, the engine step of the
[Martian and Ice Folk balance design](RULESET_7_BALANCE_MARTIAN_ICE.md))
makes the Martians win by mobility and tones the Ice Folk down: Beam Down
after a Move, with a pick-up within two tiles and a passenger that counts
as moved ([section 20.7](#207-beam-down)); the Tractor Beam on the Saucer
and the Mothership's free Heavy Tractor Beam
([section 20.10](#2010-tractor-beam)); the Mothership at 8 Coins with Beam
Down and the Grunt at Attack 2 and 9 HP ([section 11](#11-unit-roster));
Glide only from Snow onto Snow and Snow cover × 1.25
([section 21.5](#215-snow)). A match without a Martian or Ice Folk seat
plays as before, and `pulp-wars-poc-7r38` (`pulp_wars-jdb.3`, the engine
step of the [Candy overlay](RULESET_7_CANDY.md)) registers the Candy, the
eighth faction: Sugar Rush and the Crash, Crumbs and Re-bake, Splat, Bounce,
Frosting, and Sugar Toss ([section 23](#23-candy-faction-rules)). A match
without a Candy seat plays as before: its four new state lists stay empty
and its four new combat-preview fields neutral, and `pulp-wars-poc-7r39`
(`pulp_wars-1wy.6`, the measurement of the balance design) gives the Martian
Grunt 8 HP (was 9), the first step of the design's fallback ladder
([section 11](#11-unit-roster)). A match without a Martian seat plays as
before, and `pulp-wars-poc-7r40` (`pulp_wars-ykw.2`, engine step I of the
[map scale design](RULESET_7_MAP_SCALE.md)) replaces the fixed village
table with a **village density** per map type: the settlements of a board
follow its land, villages may stand one tile from the edge, and Dry Land,
Pangea, and Lakes keep a wild reserve for curiosities and Rifts
([section 2.2](#22-settlements-and-treasures)). Every generated board
changed (map revision `REGIONAL_BIOMES_NAVAL_V3`); the Showcase, the
missions, and every other rule did not, and `pulp-wars-poc-7r41`
(`pulp_wars-if6`, an early economy tweak) starts every seat with 3 Coins
(was 5), so a first turn has 5 Coins in hand
([section 3](#3-players-turns-and-victory)), and lowers the tier 3
technology base cost to 9 (was 12), so the one-city costs read 5, 7, and 9
([section 6.1](#61-research-cost)). The per-city steps, the missions' own
Coins, and every other rule did not change. `pulp-wars-poc-7r42`
(`pulp_wars-ykw.3`, engine step II of the
[map scale design](RULESET_7_MAP_SCALE.md)) allows **2 to 8 players** (as
many as there are factions) on every width that holds them, places capitals
in domains with room and village balance, and gives Continents and
Archipelago layouts for many seats
([sections 2.1 to 2.3](#21-match-setup)). Every generated board changed
again (map revision `REGIONAL_BIOMES_NAVAL_V4`); the Showcase, the missions,
and every rule of play did not.

**The naval branch overlay is folded.** `pulp_wars-5ti.9` folded the
[naval branch overlay](RULESET_7_NAVAL_BRANCH.md) as built.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r43` (`pulp_wars-5ti.2`, engine step I) gives the Naval
branch five technologies in all eight trees (Seamanship, tier 2 under
Shorecraft: **Ram** and **Board**; Submersibles, tier 3 under Seamanship:
the **Submarine** and **Harbours**). `pulp-wars-poc-7r44`
(`pulp_wars-5ti.3`, engine step II) is **the Ice Folk frozen sea**: the Ice
Folk have no ships and never embark; their five Naval technologies (shown
as Rime, Pack Ice, Icebound, Black Ice, and Glacier) let their land units
**Freeze** water into ice that every faction's land units can stand on, on
which Ice Folk units **slide** and others slip, which locks ships in
(**Icebound**, with the crush), freezes enemies standing on it (**Black
Ice**; it Chilled them before `pulp_wars-w49.37`), and thaws outside its owner's territory. The art (`pulp_wars-5ti.6`)
and the interface (`pulp_wars-5ti.7`) are live with no identity change. The
rules are in [section 6.2](#62-technology-tree) (the tree),
[section 11](#11-unit-roster) (the Submarine),
[section 14](#14-naval-rules) (ships, [the Ram](#141-the-ram-bow-ram),
[Board](#142-board), [the Submarine](#143-the-submarine-submerged-and-torpedo),
and [Harbours](#144-harbours)), and
[section 21.16](#2116-the-frozen-sea) (the frozen sea), with the shared
sections changed where a shared rule reads differently
([sections 2.5](#25-showcase-setup), [2.6](#26-mission-setup),
[3](#3-players-turns-and-victory), [5](#5-achievements-and-monuments),
[12](#12-movement-and-unit-actions), [13](#13-combat-and-fortification),
[15](#15-fog-and-observation), and [16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). A match on
Dry Land plays as before (the whole branch is forbidden there), and a match
without an Ice Folk seat has no ice. What is still open (the coarse
balance on water maps, `pulp_wars-5ti.8`, and the polish items of
`pulp_wars-5ti.10`) is in [section 25](#25-known-discrepancies).
`pulp-wars-poc-7r45` (`pulp_wars-5ti.11`) fixes one rule of the frozen sea:
a unit on ice has no fortification, so a Dwarf Hammerer or Steam Mole is
never dug in on an ice tile ([section 22.7](#227-dig-in)). No shape changed,
and a match without both a Dwarf and an Ice Folk seat plays as at `7r44`.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r59` (`pulp_wars-w49.27`) is
[step two of the Ice Folk pass](RULESET_7_TUNING_ICE_FOLK.md): **an Ice
Folk city's level-2 Survey is Scouts, with a free Sled**, as the Humans',
the Goblins', the Undead's, the Martians', and the Dinosaurs' is
([section 4.8](#48-city-rewards)), and nothing else in the rules changed.
An Ice Folk seat of the Normal AI plays the army rules in a match of
Humans, Undead, Goblins, Martians, Dinosaurs, and Ice Folk
([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)), and the lab `LAB_ICE_FOLK_MID`
stages the Ice Folk for a hand player ([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup)).
No command, event, state, or view shape changed. A save, replay, or setup
of `7r58` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. A match
without an Ice Folk seat plays as at `7r58`.
[Step two of the Dwarf pass](RULESET_7_TUNING_DWARF.md) (`pulp_wars-w49.28`)
changed no rule and kept the identity `7r59`: a Dwarf seat of the Normal
AI plays the army rules in a match without a Candy seat
([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)), and the lab `LAB_DWARF_MID` stages
the Dwarves for a hand player ([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup)).
`pulp-wars-poc-7r60` (`pulp_wars-w49.33`) is **Dwarf crowd control**: the
Whirligig's **Whirl** replaces Three Hammers
([section 22.15](#2215-the-whirligig-whirl)), the Engineer builds
**Barricades** ([section 22.8](#228-engineer-repair-and-assemble)), and a
**bombing run lands up to 2 tiles** from its target
([section 22.5](#225-gyrocopters-and-the-bombing-run)). The state gains
`barricades` and loses `ninthUnit.struckThisTurn`; the commands `WHIRL`,
`BUILD_BARRICADE`, and `ATTACK_BARRICADE` and four events are new. A save,
replay, or setup of `7r59` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new
key. A match without a Dwarf seat plays as at `7r59`.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r61` (`pulp_wars-w49.35`) is **Goblin explosions and
Berserk**: every Goblin death blast is 3 harder (Bomb Chucker 5, Rocket Cart
7, Scrap Buggy 7; [section 18.5](#185-death-blasts)), the Goblin's Kaboom is
6 ([section 18.4](#184-kaboom)), and the Orc Warboss's **Berserk** replaces
WAAAGH!: its `RALLY` gives the own unmoved land units within 2 +1 Move and
no stop in enemy zones of control until the end of the turn
([section 18.10](#1810-berserk-ram-and-troll-regeneration)). The state and
view gain `berserkThisTurn`, and the Administration unlock is
`BERSERK_SUPPORT`; no command or event is new. A save, replay, or setup of
`7r60` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. A match without
a Goblin seat plays as at `7r60`.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r62` (`pulp_wars-w49.30`) is **the giants' signatures**
([section 11.1](#111-the-giants-signatures)): every faction's reward giant
has one signature ability (Crushing Shove, Swallow, Goblin Toss, Thunder
Stomp, Overstride, Glacial Smash, Siege Hammer, Break Off), Push stays only
on the Human Juggernaut, the Colossus has Move 2, and the Frost Giant never
advances. The state gains the `giants` block (held victims), a city may
carry `wallsRazed`, and a unit may carry `variant`; the commands `SWALLOW`,
`TOSS`, `STOMP`, and `BREAK_OFF` and ten events are new. A save, replay, or
setup of `7r61` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r63` (`pulp_wars-zypi`) is **the reward ladder rework**,
which changes the city level
rewards of every faction ([section 4.8](#48-city-rewards)): **level 2
Stockpile (+4 Coins) or Militia; level 3 Scouts (the radius-3 reveal and
the faction's free `RAIDER`-role unit, now also the Dwarf Gyrocopter and
the Candy Donut Racer) or Walls; level 4 Population Boom (+3 permanent
population) or the new Economic Miracle (+1 Coin of the city's income
every turn); level 5 and every later level the faction's giant or the
Treasury (+10 Coins)**, with no once-per-city limit on the giant.
Barracks and the 6-Coin level-4 Treasury are no longer offered; a city
whose history holds one keeps its effect. The Showcase records follow
the new ladder ([section 2.5](#25-showcase-setup)), and the Normal AI
chooses among the new rewards ([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). One
reward ID was added, `ECONOMIC_MIRACLE`; no state, view, command, or
event key changed. **Where another passage of this document, the economy
rejig record, a tuning document, or a faction's document still gives
another reward ladder, a giant once per city or from level 6, a Treasury
of 6 Coins, or a Survey without a unit, section 4.8 is the rule.** A
save, replay, or setup of `7r62` is rejected, and the browser autosave
has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r64` (`pulp_wars-ke95`) is **any unit can capture**
([section 4.7](#47-siege-and-capture)): every land unit of every faction
has `CAPTURE` (support, siege, Knight-role, and heavy line units, the
flyers, and the Sabretooth included); boats, Eggs, embarked and burrowed
units, and the neutral Giant Spider never capture. A flyer (Saucer,
Mothership, Gyrocopter) and the Sabretooth may now end a Move, land, or
advance on a village or a foreign center, so they besiege and capture
there; only a Dwarf rider on its surfacing turn still keeps off foreign
centers. "Can't capture" is gone from every recruit card and glossary.
The Normal AI plans captures with every land unit but the flyers
([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). No state, view, command, or event
key changed. A save, replay, or setup of `7r63` is rejected, and the
browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r65` (`pulp_wars-kaw6.2`) is **score and modes**
([section 3.1](#31-score-play-modes-and-stars)): every player has a running
battle score (territory, city levels, technology tiers, achievements, army,
and kills, minus losses and damage taken, the penalty capped at half), kept
in the new state list `scoreLedger` and shown as a public total in every
leaderboard entry and as the viewer's breakdown in the view's `score`
block; the optional setup key `gameMode` chooses Domination (the default,
today's game) or the new Perfection (30 rounds, the highest score wins,
with `decidedBy: "SCORE"` and the `ranking` on the outcome); the end of a
match carries the human seat's star grade. The Normal AI never reads the
mode or the score. A save, replay, or setup of `7r64` is rejected, and the
browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r66` (`pulp_wars-737.14`) is **map curiosities round 2**
([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)): with the Curiosities option on, a
board may draw a Downed Saucer camp (no Martian seat) or a Graveyard camp
(no Undead seat) guarded by neutral units, a pair of Dimensional Gates
(20 x 20 and up; a gate ends every Move, and stepping on one carries the
unit to the other, displacing its occupant), Bigfoot, or the Wishing Well
and its new command `TOSS_COIN`; the state gains the neutral breeds
(`monsters[].breed`), the gate and Well markers, and four events. The
option off plays as at `7r65`. A save, replay, or setup of `7r65` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r67` (`pulp_wars-w49.37`) is **Ice Folk Freeze**, which
replaces Chill and Sluggish with one status, **Frozen**: a
Frozen unit cannot move or act on its owner's next turn and does not
retaliate, and thaws at the end of that turn
([sections 21.2](#212-frozen) and [21.3](#213-what-a-frozen-unit-cannot-do)).
The Ice Witch's Cold Snap reaches the eight tiles around her and she gains
**Frost Bolt** ([section 21.6](#216-the-blizzard-cold-snap-and-frost-bolt)),
the Frost Giant's Cold Aura acts after its own Move
([section 21.12](#2112-prowl-and-the-cold-aura)), Glacier gives +1 Move
across ice ([section 21.16](#2116-the-frozen-sea)), the Mammoth gains
**Stampede** ([section 21.18](#2118-the-mammoths-stampede)), and five Ice
Folk numbers changed ([section 11](#11-unit-roster)). The state and view
list `chilled` is now `frozen`, the event `UNITS_CHILLED` is now
`UNITS_FROZEN`, and the commands `FROST_BOLT` and `STAMPEDE` and the event
`MAMMOTH_STAMPEDED` are new. A match without an Ice Folk seat plays as at
`7r66` except for the renamed empty list. A save, replay, or setup of
`7r66` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r68` (`pulp_wars-jdb.12`) is **the Candy redesign**
([section 23](#23-candy-faction-rules)): every Candy land unit has an
ability of its own (Sticky Toffee, Glaze Trail, Ricochet, Bunny Hop and
Thump, Toothache, and the Confectioner's Top-Up in place of Frosting), the
Rush perks are gone, Crumbs lie on settlement sites, and Re-bake reaches 2,
scoops from under any unit, bakes beside the Confectioner, and may go one
unit over capacity. The state gains `stuck`, `toothache`, and
`glazedThisTurn`; the command `TOP_UP` and six events are new, and
`REBAKE` gains `from`. A match without a Candy seat plays as at `7r67`
except for the three new empty lists. A save, replay, or setup of `7r67` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r69` (`pulp_wars-eu3r.3`) is **the Monument skin rule**
([section 5](#5-achievements-and-monuments)): a Monument keeps the look of
the faction that built it when another faction captures its city. A
Monument's population contribution gains the optional `builderFaction`, set
by every `BUILD_MONUMENT` and published to every viewer; no rule, price,
population, command, or event changed. A save, replay, or setup of `7r68`
is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r70` (`pulp_wars-ty6i`) is **the Vampire and Banshee
rework** ([section 17.12](#1712-the-vampire-and-banshee-rework)): the
Vampire has 13 HP, Feast, and Bat Escape; the Banshee's Wail hits at
Attack 1.5, with Terror, and the Banshee is Ethereal. The state and view
gain `terrorThisTurn` and `feastedThisTurn`, the combat preview `feast`
and the no-retaliation reason `TERROR`, `WAIL_RESOLVED` its `terrified`
list, and `MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL` the reason `BAT_ESCAPE_LANDING`. A save,
replay, or setup of `7r69` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new
key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r71` (`pulp_wars-mch9.3`) is **the Cult registration**
([section 1](#1-identity-and-compatibility)), the first engine step of
[the Cultists of the Ancient Ones](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md): the ninth faction
ID `CULT` with its tree `CULT_BASELINE_V1`, its nine land units and their
numbers, the registered numbers of its three summoned units, its technology
names, its start, and its rewards. `F` is 9, so a headless or test match
seats 2 to 9 players ([section 2.1](#21-match-setup)). The browser offers
neither the Cult nor a ninth seat. No rule of the eight offered factions
changed, and none of the Cult's own rules (Favour, Sacrifice, the channel,
the rituals, the hexes) exists yet. A save, replay, or setup of `7r70` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r72` (`pulp_wars-mch9.4`) is **the Cult's Favour**
([section 1](#1-identity-and-compatibility)), the second engine step of the
Cultists: every Cult seat has a public pool of Favour; a Summoner
**Sacrifices** an own unit beside it for its value or **Seizes** a broken
enemy (5 HP or less) that a second robed cultist holds down, for twice its
value; a Cult city with Harvest Rites makes an **Offering** of 2 population
for 3 Favour; a Chosen's death pays 6 (**Martyr**). Nothing spends Favour
yet. The state gains the `cult` block and a city the optional
`offeredPopulation`; the commands `SACRIFICE`, `SEIZE`, and `OFFERING`, the
events `UNIT_SACRIFICED`, `UNIT_SEIZED`, `OFFERING_MADE`, and
`FAVOUR_GAINED`, and the death cause `SACRIFICED` are new. No rule of the
eight offered factions changed. A save, replay, or setup of `7r71` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r73` (`pulp_wars-w49.39`) is **the AI head start**
([section 2.1](#21-match-setup)), the first difficulty control (the user,
2026-10-10): the optional setup key `aiHeadStart: { coins }` gives every AI
seat 5, 10, or 20 extra starting Coins; the human seat keeps its 3. The
new-game screen offers it as "AI head start" (None by default), the
headless CLI and the text harness as `--ai-head-start`. A setup without the
key plays exactly as before, and no other rule changed. A save, replay, or
setup of `7r72` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r74` (`pulp_wars-mch9.5`) is **the Cult's channel**
([section 1](#1-identity-and-compatibility)), the third engine step of the
Cultists: a Summoner and a robed cultist beside it **Summon** a Horror for 5
Favour; a robed cultist **Channels** a daemon within 3 tiles and holds a
strand to it; a cultist that loses Hit Points, is moved, gets a status,
changes owner, or leaves the board is **disrupted** and its strand breaks;
at its seat's Start Turn a daemon with fewer holding strands than its
Control is **Unbound** (for now it leaves the board); an Idol Bearer's
**Behold!** keeps its neighbours' strands through a loss of Hit Points; the
Thing's **Anchor** makes one channeller's strand count three; and a
Horror's **Boo!** makes every living unit beside it jump one tile away. A
unit gains the optional `summoned` and the `cult` block the lists `strands`,
`grips`, and `idols`; the commands `SUMMON`, `CHANNEL`, `BEHOLD`, `ANCHOR`,
and `BOO`, ten events, and the death cause `UNBOUND` are new. No rule of the
eight offered factions changed. A save, replay, or setup of `7r73` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r75` (`pulp_wars-mch9.6`) is **the Cult's Unbound**
([section 1](#1-identity-and-compatibility)), the fourth engine step of the
Cultists: a daemon that fails its check no longer leaves the board. It
**belongs to nobody**, as a neutral unit of its own breed, **rampages** at
once and after every round (it walks to the nearest unit of any player and
attacks it), is **Furious** until that turn ends (nobody may channel it),
and is **bound again** by a Cult seat whose strands on it reach its Control
in one turn. A bound daemon's kills pay its seat the victim's value in
Favour; a Chosen killed by a wild unit's attack is no Martyr; an eliminated
Cult seat's bound daemons are Unbound and stay. The neutral registration
gains the breeds `HORROR` and `HERALD` and a `monsters` entry the optional
`unbound`; the event `DAEMON_BOUND`, the Favour source `DAEMON_KILL`, and
the `CHANNEL_NOT_LEGAL` reason `FURIOUS` are new, and the death cause
`UNBOUND` is gone. One rule reaches every faction: a neutral unit on a city
center besieges nothing. A save, replay, or setup of `7r74` is rejected, and
the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r76` (`pulp_wars-5ti.12`) is **Ports join the Road
network** ([section 9](#9-roads-trade-and-market); the user, 2026-10-10:
"the ports are supposed to connect cities the same way roads do ... as if
every port and every city tile automatically had a road built on it"). A
player has one connection network: Road tiles, every own city center, every
own active Port or Shipyard, and the **sea links** between active docks of
two own cities at most five water steps apart. A city joined to the
original capital by any mix of them gets the link once: +1 population for
it and +1 for the capital. **Sea trade is gone**: Navigation's separate
Coin is removed, and Commerce's trade Coin goes to every city the network
links to another, by Road or by Port. A sea link needs only **Shorecraft**
(Navigation lets it cross Deep Water), city centers and docks count without
the Roads technology, and unexplored water no longer breaks a link. A save,
replay, or setup of `7r75` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new
key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r110` (`pulp_wars-hmyk.35`; retune 4's hand play of
GOBLIN_5: the raft crews, whose beach the fighting had reached, came in on
far islands) adds **held waves** to the mission framework
([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup), CAMPAIGN.md section 10.3). A wave's
calm search, which keeps a wave unit from arriving next to a hostile unit,
reaches only 3 tiles from its written tile; it went to the edge of the
board before. When a unit of the wave has no calm tile in that reach, the
whole wave is **held** and tried again at its seat's next Start Turn. In
the round 2 after its own it comes regardless, a unit without a calm tile
on the nearest free tile. The state gains the optional `heldWaves`,
absent when no wave is held, and `REINFORCEMENT_ARRIVED` gains `wave`, the
wave's index, so a held wave's banner keeps its story line. A match that
is not a mission is unchanged; GOBLIN_5, whose waves have no calm ground
in reach on its starting board, is revision 5. A save, replay, or setup of
`7r109` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. Boards are
unchanged.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r109` (`pulp_wars-5ti.31`; the user, 2026-10-24: "when
doing land grant and city boundaries expand any water within city
boundaries (including water within the original boundaries) should get
covered with ice IF you have the relevant technology") adds **the border
freeze** for the Ice Folk ([section 21.16](#2116-the-frozen-sea)): with
Rime, a **Land Grant** of an Ice Folk city freezes every freezable water
tile of the city's whole territory, the old footprint's included; so does
a **capture** (a village captured into a city, or a city taken) for that
city's territory; and a **research** that widens what the seat freezes
(Rime, Pack Ice, Icebound) freezes the territory of every own city. Each
tile follows the Freeze table on its own (Deep Water needs Pack Ice, a
hostile ship is locked in only with Icebound, another seat's ice is
taken, own cracks are mended, an own dock becomes an Ice Harbour). The
event is one `WATER_FROZEN` with `unitId` null. City levels grow no
borders, so they freeze nothing. The Normal AI values an Ice Folk Land
Grant more for the water it freezes. A save, replay, or setup of `7r108`
is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. Boards are
unchanged.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r108` (`pulp_wars-ewpj`; the user, 2026-10-24: "the
mothership unit is lame and doesn't have a purpose ... its supposed to be
in the same class as knight and vampire") redesigns the **Mothership** as
the Martian army-mover and anchor
([section 20.7.1](#2071-mass-beam-down),
[section 20.3](#203-force-field-and-force-fields)): it costs 9 Coins (8)
and has 20 HP (16), Attack 3 (2.5), Defense 3 (2), and Sight 2 (1). Its
single Beam Down (the Saucer keeps it) becomes **Mass Beam Down**
(`MASS_BEAM_DOWN`, its primary action): up to three own units from within
two tiles of it are set down around an explored tile within three tiles,
each on the nearest free tile, and may still attack. Its **Shield
Canopy** covers the own units beside it like a Force Field at every
recharge, the End Turn one included, with no technology. The Heavy
Tractor Beam is unchanged (it already pulls an enemy into the army, so
there is no separate Abduct). A save, replay, or setup of `7r107` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. Boards are unchanged.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r107` (`pulp_wars-zir6`; the user, 2026-10-23: "some
actions are pointless - casting freezing spell on a unit that is already
frozen ... there should not be the option to do it") adds one general
rule, **no pointless actions**
([section 12.4](#124-no-pointless-actions), with the audit of every
ability): an ability cannot be used where it would change nothing. A
**Frost Bolt** (the Ice Witch's `FROST_BOLT` and the Sled's `THROW_BOLAS`)
at a unit that is Frozen already is refused
(`FROST_BOLT_NOT_LEGAL` / `BOLAS_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ALREADY_FROZEN" }`)
and never offered; a **Cold Snap** whose every target is Frozen already is
refused (`COLD_SNAP_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ALREADY_FROZEN" }`; one unfrozen
target keeps it legal, and the board marks only the units it changes); and
a **Thunder Stomp** that would hit nobody and smash no Field Defense is
refused (`STOMP_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NO_TARGET" }`; it was legal). Every
other ability already refused its pointless uses. A save, replay, or setup
of `7r106` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. Boards are
unchanged.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r106` (`pulp_wars-h0xx`; the user, 2026-10-23: "overall
mountains should be the toughest ... fertile ground or fruit should not be
an obstacle to building at all") rationalises **building placement**
([section 8.1](#81-common-placement-gates), with the audit of every
building before and after): nothing but the **Mine** is built on a
Mountain (a Windmill, Sawmill, Forge, Workshop, Market, or Monument was
allowed there with Engineering); **no land resource blocks a building**,
which uses it up (Fruit, Fertile Ground, or Game; the Farm keeps its
Fertile Ground and the Mine its Ore); and a building on a **Forest** needs
**Forestry**, the technology of Clear Forest, and clears it on its way
(the tile becomes Grass and pays Clear Forest's Coin; before, a Forest took
one with no technology and stayed a Forest). The Lumber Camp stays on its
Forest and Game no longer blocks it. A save, replay, or setup of `7r105`
is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. Boards are
unchanged.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r105` (`pulp_wars-737.22`; the user, 2026-10-20: "make
the tesla tower stronger") makes the **Tesla Tower**'s zap **16** (was 4)
and adds the **chain lightning**
([section 2.7, round 3](#round-3-the-tesla-tower-the-moon-gun-the-gold-claim-and-the-lost-expedition)):
the bolt then jumps from the last unit hit to a random unit next to it
that it has not hit, of any owner (the zapper included), for 8, then 4, 2,
and 1, stopping early when no such unit is next to the last one; the
draws are on the match PRNG. `TESLA_ZAPPED` is emitted once per hit and
gains `hop` and `fromAt`. A save, replay, or setup of `7r104` is rejected,
and the browser autosave has a new key. Boards are unchanged.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r104` (`pulp_wars-737.21`, map curiosities round 3, bead
B, the naval one of the user's five) adds the **Sea Serpent**
([section 2.7, round 3 B](#round-3-b-the-sea-serpent)): a neutral sea
monster afloat on Deep Water (boards 16 and up, never Dry Land) that, after
every round, swims up to 2 tiles to bite the weakest unit that came next to
it or hurt it; it regenerates 4, pays a bounty of 15, is never shoved,
boarded, frozen, or raised as a Ghost Ship, and counts as the board's one
danger. No new command or event (it acts in the neutral turn); new breed
`SEA_SERPENT`. A save, replay, or setup of `7r103` is rejected, and the
browser autosave has a new key. With curiosities off, boards and matches
are as at `7r103`.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r103` (`pulp_wars-737.20`, map curiosities round 3, bead
A; the user, 2026-10-19: "come up with and implement 5 more curiosities on
the map including 1 naval one") adds four land curiosities
([section 2.7, round 3](#round-3-the-tesla-tower-the-moon-gun-the-gold-claim-and-the-lost-expedition)):
the **Tesla Tower** (a unit on it may zap an enemy within 2 for 4, never
answered), the **Moon Gun** (a unit on it may be fired to an empty land
tile within 5, once a turn), the **Gold Claim** (staked by a Move, pays
its owner 2 Coins a turn up to 30), and the **Lost Expedition** (the first
finder's next technology is free). Boards of width 20 now get 2
curiosities and boards of width 25 get 2 or 3. New commands `ZAP` and
`FIRE_MOON_GUN`; new events `TESLA_ZAPPED`, `MOON_GUN_FIRED`,
`GOLD_CLAIM_STAKED`, `GOLD_CLAIM_PAID`, `EXPEDITION_FOUND`, and
`EXPEDITION_NOTES_USED`; new curiosity state markers. A save, replay, or
setup of `7r102` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. With
curiosities off, boards and matches are as at `7r102`.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r102` (`pulp_wars-w49.44`, the Gyrocopter pass; the user,
2026-10-19: "the dwarf gyrocopter is really weak ... the big problem with
the bomb run is that it forces you to land somewhere in enemy territory")
changes the Dwarf **Bomb Run**
([section 22.5](#225-gyrocopters-and-the-bombing-run)): the landing no
longer depends on the target (it was within 2 of the target and strictly
farther from the start, so a run always ended among the enemy); the
Gyrocopter lands **back on its own tile or on any tile an ordinary Move of
it could end on** (Move 3 under the flyer rules, from its start). The
bomb is **6** (`BOMB_DAMAGE_V7`; 5 before) and **7 with Dive**
(`DIVE_BOMB_DAMAGE_V7`; 6 before). The board picks the target, then the
landing (its own tile is "Fly back here"), and the playback flies the
Gyrocopter out over the target, drops the bomb, and flies on to the
landing. The Normal AI prefers, among runs of equal value, the landing
with the least threat and then the one nearest the start. No command,
event, state, or view shape changed. A save, replay, or setup of `7r101`
is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key. A match without a
Dwarf seat plays as at `7r101`.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r101` (`pulp_wars-w49.43`; the user, 2026-10-19: "I think
i overdid it with the gang up bonus for goblins. Make it +1 per ally
again", then "let's do +1 per ally (+2 for ogres) but up to +3") sets
**Gang Up** ([section 18.2](#182-gang-up)) to **+1 Attack** for each own
unit beside the target (`GANG_UP_ATTACK_PER_HELPER_V7` 1; 2 in `7r99` and
`7r100`) and **+2 for an Ogre** (`OGRE_GANG_UP_WEIGHT_V7`), summed and
capped at **+3** (`GANG_UP_MAX_ATTACK_V7`; the faction's `gangUpMaximum`
and the role's `gangUpLimit` are now whole Attack: Goblin 3, other roles 3,
a Rocket Cart's rocket 1, a bomb 0). It no longer stops counting at two
helpers: three allies give +3, an Ogre and an ally +3, an Ogre alone +2,
two Ogres +3, four allies still +3. The combat preview's `gangUp` (and the
attack event's) stays the whole Attack it adds, now 0 to 3. The Martian
Brain's Mind Control of `7r99` is unchanged. The Normal AI reads Gang Up
from the rule; its estimate (`gangUpForPolicyV7`) now counts an Ogre two,
as the engine does. A save, replay, or setup of `7r100` is rejected, and
the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r100` (`pulp_wars-5ti.25`, bead A of the
[frozen sea redesign](RULESET_7_ICE_REDESIGN.md); the user, 2026-10-18:
"the water freezing mechanics by the ice foik are a mess") makes **the
Ice Folk ice permanent** ([section 21.16](#2116-the-frozen-sea)): no thaw,
no countdown, no "a land unit holds the ice" (`IceTileV7` is
`{ at, ownerId, cracked }`; the view's ice entry `{ at, ownerId, cracked,
thick }`). **Crack Ice** (`CRACK_ICE { kind, unitId, at }`, a free primary
action of every land unit and ship not of the Ice Folk kind) breaks one
adjacent ice tile back into water, unless a land unit stands on it or it
is built on (`CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL`; event `ICE_CRACKED`), and frees a ship
frozen in, which may act the same turn. **Glacier** makes the ice
**thick** (capability `thickIce`, `iceTurns` gone): two Cracks break it,
and the owner's Freeze mends a crack. **Freeze** offers only what changes
something: it makes open water (the own dock included) ice, takes another
player's ice, and mends its own cracked ice, and passes over its own
sound ice (preview `{ unitId, tiles, mended, taken, icebound }`). **The
Ice Folk build on their own ice**: their Port is the **Ice Harbour**
(Shipyard: Great Harbour) on their ice or on open Shallow Water, which it
freezes (`PORT_BUILT.iceMade`); a dock on ice is blockaded by a hostile
land unit, never by a ship, and trains, embarks, and recovers nothing;
the Windmill, Sawmill, Forge, Workshop, Market, and Monument may stand on
their ice in their territory; and the new **Fishing Hole**
(`BUILD_FISHING_HOLE`, improvement `FISHING_HOLE`, Rime, 3 Coins, +1
population) counts as a Farm for mills and Markets
([sections 8.1 to 8.3](#81-common-placement-gates), [14](#14-naval-rules)).
**Black Ice** freezes an enemy **once, as it steps on** (its own `MOVE`,
a landing, or a Beam Down onto the seat's ice from off it), never at the
Start Turn. The Sled has **Runners** (role mechanic `runners`): its slide
is not stopped by zones of control. On a **capture** the former owner's
ice in the city's territory passes to the captor; on an **elimination**
the seat's icebound ships float free (`ICE_MELTED`) and its other ice
stays, one Crack from breaking. The Normal AI only stops reading the thaw
(it never picks Crack Ice yet: bead `pulp_wars-5ti.26`), and the
interface keeps its old Freeze dock without the countdown (the Crack Ice
button and the new sprites are bead `pulp_wars-5ti.27`). A save, replay,
or setup of `7r99` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r99` (`pulp_wars-w49.42`) is **bolder abilities**, the
user's ruling of 2026-10-18 ("all these abilities are too timid"). **Mind
Control** ([section 20.8](#208-mind-control)) takes **any hostile unit on
one of the eight tiles around the Brain** (`MIND_CONTROL_RANGE_V7` 1; it was 2) at any HP, of any size and form: the HP limit (6, `MIND_CONTROL_HP_V7`,
removed) and the wounded test are gone, and so is every immunity but an
Egg, a neutral unit, and a unit already controlled. A giant
(`JUGGERNAUT`), a two-slot unit, a construct, a daemon (a bound Horror,
Herald, Imp, or Gibbering Mass), a ship or a sea beast (`NAVAL`), an
embarked unit, a unit on a city or village center, and a flyer on a Rift
may all be taken; a unit afloat on Deep Water needs the Brain owner's
Navigation (`MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "DEEP_WATER" }`, the Board
rule). A Brain holds **three** units at a time (`MIND_CONTROL_LIMIT_V7` 3;
it was 1): at the limit Mind Control is not offered (`CONTROL_LIMIT`),
and a release (Disband on a controlled unit) or a controlled unit's death
frees a place; the two-turn cooldown stays. Under control a unit also
loses Swallow, Break Off, Drowned Crew, and Offerings to the Deep
(`MIND_CONTROLLED_LOST_ABILITIES_V7`: they make a unit or pay Favour), so an
Abomination taken spits out the victim it holds on the first free land
tile around it (else it is digested); a daemon taken loses its strands, is
never checked or Unbound and owes no Hunger while a Brain holds it, and
its kills feed no Favour; a ship a Brain holds that another seat boards is
the boarder's and no longer held; a unit afloat on Deep Water released to
an owner without Navigation is lost (`BRAIN_LOST`). **Gang Up** ([section
18.2](#182-gang-up)) adds **+2 Attack** for each own unit beside the
target (`GANG_UP_ATTACK_PER_HELPER_V7`; +1 before, and +1 again from
`7r101`), still counting at most two (an Ogre counts two), so up to +4; a
Rocket Cart's rocket counts one (+2) and a bomb none. The combat preview's
`gangUp` is the whole Attack (0, 2, or 4). The Normal AI takes the most valuable unit beside a ready
Brain (its kind cost, or its Score value for a unit without one: a giant
12, a Horror 6, a Herald 24), approaches any unit, no longer wounds a
target into control, and against Martians every seat keeps every unit (not
only one at 6 HP or less) out of a ready Brain's reach; its Gang Up
estimates read the rule. A save, replay, or setup of `7r98` is rejected,
and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r98` (`pulp_wars-5ti.22`, the seventh and last bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md)) is **the Deep Ones**,
the Cult fleet. The **Black Gondola** (`PATROL_BOAT`, 5 Coins) and the
**Galleon of the Eye** (`BATTLESHIP`, 16) are the Human ships' numbers under
their own names; the **Kraken** (`SUBMARINE`) is a trained sea beast for
**10 Coins** (8 at a Shipyard), 12 HP, Attack 4, Defense 2, Move 2,
Submerged and Torpedo as every Submarine, living, never a daemon, and a
**sea beast** (role mechanic `seaBeast`: never boarded, and the Cult never
boards a Submarine). The Kraken **Drags** units afloat (role mechanic
`dragsAfloat`, ability `DRAG`): a unit afloat (`NAVAL` or `EMBARKED`) of a
player hostile to the Kraken's owner that begins a `MOVE` beside a living
Kraken in `NAVAL` form that is not on ice moves one tile in it
(`MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL { reason: "DRAGGED" }`, never offered;
`draggingKrakenV7`, read by both movement validations and so by the
movement query). A landing (`DISEMBARK`), a Ram's shove, and a Tractor Beam
pull are no Moves and are never dragged. The Cult Seamanship, shown as
**Offerings to the Deep**, is the Ram and the unlock `DEEP_OFFERINGS`
(capability `deepOfferings`) in place of `COMMAND BOARD`: a hostile unit
afloat that a Cult ship in `NAVAL` form kills by its `ATTACK` or its
retaliation pays the seat `floor(value / 2)` Favour
(`DEEP_OFFERING_DIVISOR_V7`; a Patrol Boat 2, a Submarine 4, a Battleship
8, a transported Knight 4), capped at 30 as every gain, with
`FAVOUR_GAINED` source `DEEP_OFFERING` (ability literal `DEEP_OFFERING` on
the three ships). Never from splash, blasts, Plague, a bomb, the crush, or a
Tentacle, and never from a land kill. The five Cult Naval technologies are
shown as Black Gondolas, Navigation, Galleons of the Eye, Offerings to the
Deep, and The Kraken. Offerings to the Deep is private research: another
seat's preview assumes it for a Cult ship (`previewDeepOfferingsV7`). The
Normal AI counts an Offering's Favour (a Coin each, below the cap) in its
attack choice, the ram approach, the torpedo targets, and the Galleon's
station, moves a Kraken beside a hostile transport or Patrol Boat it can
hold where it is safe, and every seat reads a unit afloat beside a hostile
Kraken as moving one tile and ends no transport Move beside one it cannot
land from ([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The Kraken map sprite,
portrait, and the Offerings to the Deep card are new art, and the Kraken's
torpedo has its own sound (`attack.kraken`). A save, replay, or setup of
`7r97` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r97` (`pulp_wars-5ti.21`, the sixth bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md)) is **Sugar Sails**,
the Candy fleet. The Candy ships are the Human ships' numbers under their
own names, the **Gumdrop Tug** (`PATROL_BOAT`, 5 Coins), the **Pie
Galleon** (`BATTLESHIP`, 17), and the **Choco Sub** (`SUBMARINE`, 9), 2
less at a Shipyard. The Pie Galleon has **Splat** ([section
23.5](#235-splat)): its primary target, if it survives, joins
`splattedThisTurn` and strikes back at nothing for the rest of the turn
(splash victims are not Splatted; `attackSplatsV7` reads land or naval
form). The three ships have `SUGAR_RUSH`: the Candy Seamanship, shown as
**Sugar Sails**, is the Ram and the unlock `SUGAR_SAILS` (capability
`sugarSails`) in place of `COMMAND BOARD`, and with it a ship may Sugar
Rush afloat ([section 23.2](#232-sugar-rush-and-the-crash), row 3,
`sugarRushFormBlockV7`, read by the reducer and the command query): +1 Move
on its ordinary Move and +1 Attack on its first attack (it adds to the
Ram), then it Crashes at the End Turn as a land unit does (no primary
action on its owner's next turn; it still moves and strikes back), unless
Home Sweet Home spares it on or next to an own city center. Without Sugar
Sails a ship's Rush is `TECH_REQUIRED { tech: "SEAMANSHIP" }`; an icebound
ship's `SUGAR_RUSH_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`; an embarked unit
still never Rushes. A Pie Galleon still cannot fire after a Move, so it
Rushes to fire harder from where it stands. A ship that dies leaves no
Crumbs. The five Candy Naval technologies are shown as Gumdrop Tugs,
Navigation, Pie Galleons, Sugar Sails, and Choco Subs. Sugar Sails is
private research: the public Candy block says every Candy ship's role may
Rush, and another seat's estimate and threat reach assume it. The Normal
AI Rushes a ship for a kill the plain attack does not make (a Ram, a
torpedo, or a shot after one more tile of Move), never into visible lethal
reach for its Crashed next turn unless Home Sweet Home spares it, fires a
Pie Galleon first at the hostile unit its own units are about to attack
(the Splat value is keyed to the Splat in the preview), and every seat
counts a hostile Candy ship's Rushed reach and Attack, and reads a Crashed
one as no threat ([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The Sugar Sails
card is new art; no new sound. A save, replay, or setup of `7r96` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r96` (`pulp_wars-5ti.20`, the fifth bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md)) is **Ironclads and
Sea Tunnels**, the Dwarf fleet. The Dwarf ships are **Armoured** (the role
mechanic `armourReduction` 1, the Ankylosaurus's Armoured of
[section 19.9](#199-acid-and-armoured)): every hit of 2 or more on them
does 1 less, through `armouredDamageV7` in every form (attack,
retaliation, splash, blasts, Wail, bombs, eruptions, and Plague), never
the Ice Folk crush (3); they cost more: the **Steam Launch**
(`PATROL_BOAT`, 6 Coins), the **Ironclad** (`BATTLESHIP`, 18), and the
**Diving Bell** (`SUBMARINE`, 10), 2 less at a Shipyard, every other number
the Human ship's. The Dwarf stats block shows `armourReduction`. The Dwarf
Seamanship, shown as **Sea Tunnels**, is the Ram and the unlock
`SEA_TUNNELS` (capability `seaTunnels`) in place of `COMMAND BOARD`: a
Steam Mole whose kind's capabilities under its controller have Sea Tunnels
may tunnel under explored Shallow Water that is not ice (row 6 of
[section 22.2](#222-the-tunnel-and-burrowed-units), `seaTunnelPassableV7`,
read by the reducer and the command query); the destination and the
rider's tile stay land, the range stays 3 (a strait of one or two Shallow
tiles is crossed), and Deep Water and ice are never passed. Everything else
is the Tunnel, and it still touches no water on the board. The five Dwarf
Naval technologies are shown as Steam Launches, Navigation, Ironclads, Sea
Tunnels, and Diving Bells. Sea Tunnels is private research and is in no
public stat. The Normal AI tunnels a Mole and its rider across a strait to
the naval plan's target landmass at the priority of a planned landing
(they board at no Port), asks for Sea Tunnels when the target lies within
tunnel reach over Shallow Water and it owns a Mole, reads Armoured from the
exact previews and its threat estimate, and every seat refuses a ship's
attack on an Armoured hull that does not sink it and deals less than it
takes (a Patrol Boat's Ram on an Ironclad, 6 dealt and 7 taken)
([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The board draws a tunnel's route
under a strait while its destination is focused or chosen. The Sea Tunnels
card is new art; no new sound. A save, replay, or setup of `7r95` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r95` (`pulp_wars-5ti.19`, the fourth bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md)) is **the Martian
Hover Fleet**. The Martian ships are frail hulls behind **Shields** (the
role mechanic `shield`): the **Skimmer** (`PATROL_BOAT`, 8 HP, Shield 2),
the **Hover Cruiser** (`BATTLESHIP`, 20 HP, Shield 3), and the
**Bathysphere** (`SUBMARINE`, 10 HP, Shield 2), every other number the
Human ship's. Their Shields follow [section 20.2](#202-shields) in every
form: a ship trained with `TRAIN_NAVAL` starts with its full Shield (the
reducer now writes the entry), it recharges at its owner's Start Turn (and
End Turn with Force Fields), to 4 beside a Shield Projector, and it takes
every hit first, never Plague; a boarded Skimmer becomes its captor's ship
and loses its entry. The Martian Seamanship, shown as **Hover Pods**, is
the Ram and the unlock `HOVER_PODS` (capability `hoverPods`) in place of
`COMMAND BOARD`: a land-form Martian foot unit (the `GROUND` movement mode:
Grunt, Ray Gunner, Shield Projector, Brain, Shock Trooper) may make the
**last step** of an ordinary Move from land onto an adjacent Shallow Water
tile it knew before the command, that holds no unit and is neither ice nor
a dock; the step costs a full point, ends the Move, and the unit
**self-launches** there (it embarks, exhausted) as a machine does
(`hoverLaunchAllowedV7`, read by both movement validations and the
movement query). It never crosses water inside a Move and never launches
onto Deep Water; afloat it is an ordinary transport that keeps its Shield.
A mind-controlled unit reads its own kind's tree with its controller's
research. The five Martian Naval technologies are shown as Skimmers,
Navigation, Hover Cruisers, Hover Pods, and Bathyspheres. Another seat's
Hover Pods is private, so its public movement validation assumes them for
a visible Martian foot unit, whose launch tiles are no attack origins.
The Normal AI treats every free Shallow Water tile beside its home land as
a launch start of its naval plan once it has Hover Pods (a foot unit bound
overseas walks to the nearest one that serves the landing coast instead of
a Port, under every boarding rule of a Port), asks for Hover Pods when two
or more foot units are bound overseas, reads Shields from the exact
previews and its threat estimate, and trains the three ships by the
counter of every seat ([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The Hover
Pods card is new art; no new sound. A save, replay, or setup of `7r94` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r94` (`pulp_wars-5ti.18`, the third bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md)) is **Horned Prows
and the Plesiosaur**, the Dinosaur fleet. The Dinosaur `PATROL_BOAT` is the
**Dugout**, the Human Patrol Boat's numbers with a **Horned Prow**: its Ram
adds +1 Attack after a Move that entered one tile and **+1.5** after two or
more (the role mechanic `ramRunUpBonus2` 3, `HORNED_PROW_RAM_BONUS2_V7`;
every other Ram is +1 whatever its run); an interrupted Move counts the
tiles it entered, and the canonical estimate counts a planned path's
length. The `BATTLESHIP` is the **War Raft** (the Battleship's numbers).
The `SUBMARINE` is the **Plesiosaur**, a living sea reptile: 10 Coins (8 at
a Shipyard), 12 HP, Submerged and Torpedo, trained at a dock (never an
Egg), it **grows** from its torpedo and retaliation kills like a dinosaur
(Big 16 HP, Alpha 20 HP and +1 Attack, a full heal each; never promoted)
and is a **sea beast** (`seaBeast`, ability `SEA_BEAST`): nobody boards it,
and a Dinosaur ship never boards a `SUBMARINE`-role ship
(`BOARD_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "TARGET_IMMUNE" }`). It is not a dinosaur for
the land rules (Pack Hunt, Wallbreaker, War Drums, the Shaman's 4-HP
Tend). The Dinosaur Seamanship keeps the Ram and Board. The five Dinosaur
Naval technologies are shown as Dugouts, Navigation, War Rafts, Horned
Prows, and Plesiosaurs. Another seat's Horned Prows is private, so its
threat estimate assumes a hostile Dugout's two-tile run. The Normal AI
previews a Dugout's approach with each offered Move's real path length (a
two-tile run that sinks beats a one-tile Ram; a hostile ship's zone of
control stops a Move beside it, so the run must start at least two tiles
away), holds a plain attack while such a run kills, fires a Plesiosaur's
growing torpedo kill before a chip on a capital ship, and trains the
Plesiosaur and the Dugout by the counter of every seat
([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The Plesiosaur, the Dugout's horn,
and the Horned Prows card are new art, and the Plesiosaur's bite has its
own sound (`attack.plesiosaur`). A save, replay, or setup of `7r93` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r93` (`pulp_wars-5ti.17`, the second bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md)) is **the Undead
Drowned Fleet**. The Undead ships keep the Human numbers under their own
names, the **Ghost Ship** (`PATROL_BOAT`), the **Plague Galleon**
(`BATTLESHIP`), and the **Sunken Galley** (`SUBMARINE`), each with the
ability literal `DROWNED_CREW`, and the Galleon has `PLAGUE`: with
Pestilence its shot plagues its target and every living splash victim as a
Lich's does. The Undead Seamanship, shown as **Drowned Crews**, is the Ram
and the unlock `DROWNED_CREWS` (capability `drownedCrews`) in place of
`COMMAND BOARD`: a hostile ship that an Undead ship sinks by its `ATTACK`
or its retaliation rises at once on its tile as the killer's owner's
**Ghost Ship at 5 HP** (`DROWNED_CREW_HP_V7`; no home city, no slot,
exhausted, not capture-eligible), the Infect step pointed at the sea
(`UNIT_INFECTED`, the preview's `defenderInfected` or `attackerInfected`);
never from splash, a blast, Plague, or any other cause, never from a
transport, never on ice, and on Deep Water only when the Undead seat has
Navigation. An Undead ship never boards (other seats may board one). The
five Undead Naval technologies are shown as Ghost Ships, Navigation, Plague
Galleons, Drowned Crews, and Sunken Galleys. Another seat's Drowned Crews
is private, so its public preview of a retaliation that sinks its ship
assumes the rising. The Normal AI values the risen Ghost Ship (half the
Patrol Boat's cost, safe or doomed) in its torpedoes, rams, and Battleship
stations, sinks a ship with a rising torpedo before chipping a capital
ship when no other Submarine follows, keeps a Plague Galleon's stations by
the unplagued units in its splash, researches Pestilence for a Galleon,
and as any other seat counts a Ghost Ship it would feed the enemy
([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The Drowned Crews card is new art. A
save, replay, or setup of `7r92` is rejected, and the browser autosave has
a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r92` (`pulp_wars-5ti.16`, the first bead of the
[themed naval branches](RULESET_7_NAVAL_FACTIONS.md), approved as the
user's 2026-10-17 request) is **the Goblin Scrap Fleet** and the shared
plumbing of the themed branches. The Goblin ships are the **Fire Raft**
(the `PATROL_BOAT`: 4 Coins, 2 at a Shipyard, 8 HP, Ram, and Kaboom 5),
the **Scrap Dreadnought** (the `BATTLESHIP`: the Battleship's numbers and
a **death blast of 7** when it sinks, but not when it is boarded or
crushed by ice), and the **Diving Barrel** (the `SUBMARINE`: 8 Coins, 6 at
a Shipyard, 10 HP). The Goblin Seamanship, shown as **Powder Kegs**, is the
Ram and the unlock `FIRE_RAFTS` (capability `fireRafts`) in place of
`COMMAND BOARD`: a Fire Raft may `KABOOM` afloat (an icebound one is
refused with `KABOOM_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`, one without Powder
Kegs with `TECH_REQUIRED { tech: "SEAMANSHIP" }`), and a Goblin ship never
boards. The five Goblin Naval technologies are shown as Fire Rafts,
Navigation, Dreadnoughts, Powder Kegs, and Diving Barrels. For every
faction: a boarded prize takes its new kind's maximum HP (plus 5 for a
veteran) and `floor(max / 3) + 1` HP, and loses a Shield entry its new kind
has no Shield for; the role mechanic `seaBeast` (no role has it yet) makes
a ship unboardable (the Dinosaur Plesiosaur since `7r94`), and a seat whose own Submarine is a sea beast never
boards a Submarine (`BOARD_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "TARGET_IMMUNE" }`; ability
literal `SEA_BEAST`). The Normal AI blows a raft up where the blast is
worth its 4 Coins, kills, or the raft is lost anyway, approaches a cluster
when its blast beats its best Ram, counts the Dreadnought's blast in its
torpedoes and rams, and keeps own ships from crowding a Dreadnought a
hostile Submarine reaches ([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)). The Fire
Raft's sprite and portrait and the Powder Kegs card are new art. A save,
replay, or setup of `7r91` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new
key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r91` (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`, step E-R7 of the Cult redesign,

and a helper summon a Gibbering Mass (`SUMMON` `daemon` `MASS`, with a
`helperUnitId`) for **5 Favour** (`FAVOUR_SPENT` purpose `SUMMON_MASS`;
`DAEMON_SUMMONED` role `MASS`) with **Gibbering Masses** (the Cult's
Metallurgy now grants `SUMMON_MASS`, the capability `summonMass`; without
it `SUMMON_NOT_LEGAL` reason `TECHNOLOGY`): 30 HP, Attack 2, Defense 3,
Move 1, worth 6, Control 1, a daemon stored as a `GUARD` that is
**immovable** (a Crushing Shove crushes it), **never advances** after a
kill, and **never captures**. **Doorstep**: at the check a Mass short of
its strands stays bound on or beside an own city center or beside an own
standing idol (the view's `doorstep`). **Drag**: a hostile land-form unit
that begins a Move beside a Mass moves one tile (the movement reason
`DRAGGED`; an Unbound Mass drags every player's units). An Unbound Mass is
the neutral breed `MASS` (reach 2, one attack, no advance). The Mass's
sprite, Unbound look, and portrait join the runtime art
([section 26](#26-cultist-faction-rules)). A save, replay, or setup of
`7r90` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.

[its section 18](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md#18-implementation-beads),

summons an Imp (`SUMMON` now names its `daemon`, `IMP` or `HORROR`, and

purpose `SUMMON_IMP`; `DAEMON_SUMMONED` with a null helper and one
strand): 6 HP, Attack 2, Defense 1, Move 3, worth 2, Control 1, a daemon
stored as a `RAIDER` that **never captures**. **Brood**: at the check one
holding strand to an Imp also holds up to two other own bound Imps beside
it (the lowest IDs; a held Imp lends no Brood on; the view's `broodOf`,
`previewChannelV7`'s `brood`). **Swarm**: a unit with two or more of a
seat's bound Imps beside it does not strike back at their attacks (the
combat preview's `noRetaliationReason` `SWARMED`). An Unbound Imp is the
neutral breed `IMP` (reach 4, one attack, no Brood or Swarm). The Imp's
sprite, Unbound look, and portrait join the runtime art
([section 26](#26-cultist-faction-rules)). A save, replay, or setup of
`7r89` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.

approved by the user on 2026-10-16) is **the Cult's Favour economy and its
warden**. Favour is **capped at 30** (`FAVOUR_CAP_V7`; a gain above the cap
is lost and reported as `forfeited`, and a mission seat's Favour is
clamped); the Offering pays **6** (3 before), a Horror costs **4** (5) and
the Great Summoning **18** (20). At a Cult seat's Start Turn check each own
Summoner whose strand held, for a daemon still bound, pays a **trickle** of
1 (`FAVOUR_GAINED` source `TRICKLE`), and then each bound Herald eats 2
Favour (**Hunger**, `FAVOUR_SPENT` purpose `HUNGER`) or, unpaid, is Unbound
at once (`DAEMON_UNBOUND` reason `HUNGER`; the event's `reason` is new, with
`STRANDS` and `ELIMINATED`). The Idol Bearer's **Behold!** is a lasting aura
with no command: while the bearer has no status its idol stands, a shot of
two or more tiles on a unit of its seat beside it is **halved** (the combat
preview's `idolHalved`), and an enemy beside it may attack only an Idol
Bearer (**Awestruck**, `ATTACK_AWESTRUCK`); the `BEHOLD` command, the
`cult.idols` list, the `IDOL_RAISED` and `IDOL_DROPPED` events, the error
`BEHOLD_NOT_LEGAL`, `previewBeholdV7`, and the strand a raised idol kept
are removed ([section 26](#26-cultist-faction-rules)). A save, replay, or
setup of `7r88` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.

cultist beside it may **Join the chant** in that turn with the new command
`JOIN_CHANT` (+3 each, its primary action; event `CHANT_JOINED`, error
`JOIN_CHANT_NOT_LEGAL`, preview `previewJoinChantV7`); a star needs no
chanter and never fizzles for want of one; Switcheroo reaches 4 tiles (2
before). Every daemon now **advances after a kill**, bound or Unbound (the
Herald too, its second attack made from the victim's tile; an Unbound one
never onto a tile its walk avoids), and an **Unbound daemon** goes for a
robed cultist within 2 first, then anyone in its reach (Move + 1) who is
not a summon, then a summon in reach, else walks toward the nearest
non-summon; `previewRampageV7` names the step
([section 26](#26-cultist-faction-rules)). A save, replay, or setup of
`7r87` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r87` (`pulp_wars-ykw.8`, the user, 2026-10-15:

[map scale design](RULESET_7_MAP_SCALE.md) section 5.8): Continents

between them up to four players and islets of one to three tiles in the

campaign boards are unchanged. A save, replay, or setup of `7r86` is
rejected, and the browser autosave has a new key.

([section 26](#26-cultist-faction-rules)). Missions `FRONTIER_10`
(revision 3) and `LAB_CULT_MID` (revision 2) swap their Callers and
Chosen for Idol Bearers, Initiates, and Hexers, and mission validation

`pulp-wars-poc-7r83` (`pulp_wars-v642.5`, the campaign follow-ups) was
**waves that arrive calmly** ([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup)): a mission's
reinforcement arrives with its turn spent (it neither moves nor attacks
until its seat's next turn), and on the nearest free tile it may enter
that is not next to a unit of a seat hostile to it, searched outward to
the edge of the board instead of within two tiles. Nothing changes in a
match that is not a mission, and nothing in a mission without waves. A
save, replay, or setup of `7r82` is rejected, and the browser autosave
has a new key.
`pulp-wars-poc-7r82` (`pulp_wars-v642.1`, the campaign framework) was
**mission objectives** ([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup)): a mission's
objective may be an escort, a number of rounds to survive, places to
capture, or units to kill, with a deadline, protected places and units, and
up to two secondary goals; it decides the match after every accepted
command, and a result it decides carries its `cause`. A mission may name
**teams** (an AI seat allied to the human), bring **reinforcements** at a
seat's Start Turn of a round (the new event `REINFORCEMENT_ARRIVED`), and
forbid a seat technologies of its own. Nothing changes in a match that is
not a mission, and nothing in a mission that uses none of this. A save,
replay, or setup of `7r81` is rejected, and the browser autosave has a new
key.
