A Charge! on a Martian unit is absorbed by the Shield first and pushes and follows whatever it absorbed; Acid and Wallbreaker reach only a Martian foot unit's cover and Walls (machines have neither). An Ankylosaurus takes 1 less from every Martian hit. The two-slot Triceratops, T-Rex, and Brontosaurus are immune to the Tractor Beam; since `7r99` a Brain takes any dinosaur beside it, and it keeps growing under its controller (it has no Hatch). A Mind Control and a `BRAIN_LOST` removal are no kill for growth.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Ice Folk                | An Egg cannot be Frozen (a Bolas or Frost Bolt on it is `TARGET_IMMUNE`; every other freeze source skips it) and is never shattered; it is an ordinary target of Ice Folk attacks (Defense 1, no retaliation), and a Sweep flank hit deals it 2. Dinosaurs are Frozen and shattered like any unit, the two-slot ones included (a Frozen T-Rex only by the hit that leaves it at 1 to 3 of its HP); a Brontosaurus (`JUGGERNAUT`) never. Growth from killing Ice Folk units is ordinary; its full heal takes a unit out of the Shatter window but does not thaw it. A Triceratops's Move ends on its first Snow tile, so its run-up inside Snow is at most the tiles up to that one; its Charge! ignores an Ice Folk defender's fortification, not its Snow cover, and a pushed unit stays Frozen (a Mountain-born one may be pushed onto a Mountain). A Raptor's Pounce needs its first tile off Snow (Fieldcraft waives deep snow); a Frozen Raptor cannot Pounce, and a Frozen T-Rex cannot attack. Acid ignores Snow cover; a Spitter's shot from distance 2 at an Ice Folk unit in its own Witch's Blizzard is halved. An Ankylosaurus takes 1 from a Sweep flank hit, Armoured applying before the Shatter test. Wallbreaker removes Walls levels, and the Ice Folk defender on that center still has no Snow cover. The Shaman's Tend Wounded thaws a Frozen unit; a Frozen Shaman can use neither War Drums nor Hatch. |
| Dwarves                 | Dinosaur-faction units and Eggs on the eight tiles around a surfacing Steam Mole take its eruption (2, 3 with Blasting Charges): an Ankylosaurus 1 (2), a 6-HP Egg is left at 4 (3), a 10-HP Egg with Nesting at 8 (7). A bomb hits any form: it destroys a 6-HP Egg (6 since `7r102`; 5 left it at 1) and takes 5 (Dive 6) from an Ankylosaurus. A destroyed Egg is the Mole's or the Gyrocopter's kill; a dinosaur grows from killing Dwarf units as from any kill. No Egg is laid, and no hatching, Push, Charge! push or follow, or Rampage ends, on a mound tile. The Triceratops's Charge! and Acid ignore Dig In with the rest of the fortification; Wallbreaker removes only the Walls levels, so Dig In stays. A two-slot dinosaur and an Egg are never knocked back by the Steam Cannon.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### 19.13 Commands, events, errors, and queries

- **Commands:** `LAY_EGG { kind, cityId, role, at }` (in
  `COMMAND_KIND_ORDER_V7` right after `TRAIN_NAVAL`) and
  `HATCH { kind, unitId, eggUnitId }` (right after `KABOOM`). `DISBAND`
  also accepts an own Egg. There is no `STAMPEDE` command: revision 20
  removed it, and a command object with that kind fails parsing like any
  unknown kind.
- **Events:** `EGG_LAID` and `EGG_HATCHED`
  (`{ playerId, unitId, role, at, cause: "TIME" | "SHAMAN", sourceUnitId }`)
  right after `NAVAL_UNIT_TRAINED`, and `UNIT_GREW` right after
  `UNIT_PROMOTED`, in `DOMAIN_EVENT_KIND_ORDER_V7`. `UNIT_DIED.cause` gains
  `CITY_CAPTURED`. There is no separate "Egg destroyed" event.
- **Combat preview** (`CombatPreviewV7`, so also `COMBAT_RESOLVED`):
  `runUp` (0–2, in `attack2`; at most 1 without Wallbreaker since `7r53`),
  `fortificationIgnored` (levels removed by
  Charge! or Wallbreaker), `acid`, `defenderArmoured`, and
  `attackerArmoured`; `push` and `advances` cover the Charge! Push and
  follow. Alpha needs no field (it is in `attack2`).
- **Errors:** `HATCH_NOT_LEGAL` (reasons `EMBARKED`, `NO_EGG`,
  `LAID_THIS_TURN`) and `UNIT_IS_EGG`; `LAY_EGG` reuses existing codes
  ([section 19.4](#194-laying-an-egg)).
- **Registration:** faction `DINOSAUR`, tree `DINOSAUR_BASELINE_V1`, display
  name "Dinosaur"; unlock kinds `NESTING { eggHp: 4, hatchTurns: 0, citySlots: 1 }`
  and `WALLBREAKER`; capabilities `eggHpBonus`, `eggHatchTurnReduction`,
  `nestingCityCapacityBonus`, and `ignoresCityWalls`; abilities `HATCH`,
  `ACID`, `ARMOURED`, `GROW`, and `LINEBREAKER`; faction rule
  `treasureUnitRole`; role mechanics `capacitySlots` (1 or 2), `hatchTurns`
  (null, or 1–4), `runUpBonus2` (0 or 2), `packHuntBonus2` (0, or 2 on
  the Caveman; `CAVEMAN_PACK_HUNT_BONUS2_V7`), and `armourReduction` (0 or
  1); the capability `runUpTiles` (`RUN_UP_BASE_TILES_V7` 1, or 2 with
  `WALLBREAKER`);
  constants `EGG_HP_V7` 6, `EGG_DEFENSE2_V7` 2, `GROWTH_KILLS_V7` `[1, 3]`,
  `GROWTH_HP_V7` 4, `ALPHA_ATTACK2_V7` 2, and `RUN_UP_MAXIMUM_TILES_V7` 2.
- **`queryPlayerCommandsV7`** offers, for a Dinosaur seat, one `LAY_EGG` per
  legal `(city, role, nest tile)` in city-ID, role, then `(y, x)` order;
  `HATCH` for every Shaman and adjacent own Egg not laid this turn;
  `DISBAND` for own Eggs with Administration; and the Triceratops's ordinary
  `ATTACK` before and after its Move. It never offers `TRAIN` of an egg-laid
  role (it does offer its `HIRE` on a Market with Commerce since `7r53`,
  [section 9.4](#94-market)), Field Defense, `PROMOTE` for a dinosaur, or any other command for an
  Egg. Every offered command is accepted.
- **`previewLayEggV7(view, cityId, role)`** returns null unless the city is
  the viewer's and the role is egg-laid in its registration; otherwise
  `{ cityId, role, cost, slots, usedSlots, capacity, hp, turnsToHatch, nestTiles, unavailableReason }`,
  with `nestTiles` in `(y, x)` order and `unavailableReason` null or the
  rejection that applies whatever the tile (`CITY_ACTION_SPENT`,
  `CITY_BESIEGED`, `CITY_REWARD_PENDING`, `TECH_REQUIRED`, `INVALID_TILE`
  when no nest tile is free, `CITY_CAPACITY_FULL`, `INSUFFICIENT_COINS`).
- **`previewHatchV7(view, unitId, eggUnitId)`** returns null unless that
  `HATCH` is offered, otherwise `{ unitId, eggUnitId, role, at, hp, turnsSaved }`.
- `queryCombatPreviewV7` and `estimateCombatV7` include Alpha, Acid,
  Armoured, Charge! (the run-up from the unit's current `movedPathLength`,
  or a planned Move's length for an estimate), and Wallbreaker, and accept
  an Egg as the target. `previewAttackExplosionsV7` and every other public
  simulation apply the follow after a Push and the full-heal growth.
  `queryThreatenedTilesV7` gives a hostile Triceratops its ordinary
  move-then-melee reach.
- **Public unit stats** carry, for every unit of a Dinosaur seat, the
  `dinosaur` block: `capacitySlots`, `growthStage` (0–2, or null for a role
  that does not grow), `killsToNextStage` (or null), `armourReduction`,
  `acid`, `runUpBonus`, `runUpMaximum` (the tiles that count for the
  unit's owner: 1, or 2 with Wallbreaker), and `egg` (null, or
  `{ turnsRemaining, hatchesAs }`). An Egg's stat rows are HP, Attack 0,
  Defense 1, Move 0, Range 0, and Sight 0. The Attack row lists the source
  `RUN_UP` while the Triceratops can still attack this turn, and `ALPHA`
  for an Alpha; the HP row lists `GROWTH`.
- `previewCityCapacityV7` reports used slots (the sum), capacity (with
  Nesting), and each producible role's slots; `previewDisbandV7` covers
  Eggs. `PublicPlayerV7` and the leaderboard carry `DINOSAUR` and
  `DINOSAUR_BASELINE_V1`; the leaderboard unit count includes Eggs.

### 19.14 Pack Hunt

The Dinosaur pass (`7r53`,
[its section 6.2](RULESET_7_TUNING_DINOSAUR.md#62-pack-hunt)). The
Caveman (role mechanic `packHuntBonus2` 2, the Dinosaur `FIGHTER` only;
0 for every other role of every faction) has **+1 Attack on an `ATTACK`
it makes** when at least one unit of its owner that is on the board in
land form and has `GROW` (a hatched Raptor, Spitter, Ankylosaurus,
Triceratops, T-Rex, or Brontosaurus, at any stage) stands at distance 1
from the **target** (`packHuntAttack2V7`), **or the target is hunted**
(the correction of `7r53`): a hatched dinosaur of the Caveman's owner
attacked it this turn and it survived.

- **Hunted.** After an accepted `ATTACK` by a land-form unit with `GROW`
  of the active seat, its target, when it is still on the board and not
  that seat's own, is added to `huntedThisTurn` (sorted unit IDs; state and
  view, the view's holding the visible ones). The list is emptied at that
  seat's End Turn and loses a unit that leaves the board. Only the active
  seat attacks, so the list is always the attacking Caveman's side's. A
  Spitter's shot from two tiles sets it up for a Caveman anywhere beside
  the target; a Caveman's, a Shaman's, or another faction's attack marks
  nothing, and a killed target is not listed. A state whose list names a
  unit not on the board, a unit of the active seat, or any unit in a match
  without a Dinosaur seat does not parse.

- A Caveman, a Shaman, an Egg, an embarked dinosaur, an allied player's
  dinosaur, and a dinosaur two tiles from the target give nothing. The
  dinosaur need not have attacked, and it may be the unit that just
  charged and followed.
- It applies to the Caveman's own attack only: never to its retaliation,
  never to another unit's attack, and not to a Caveman afloat.
- It adds to War Drums (Inspired) and to a promoted Caveman's numbers; it
  is part of `attack2` in the preview and in `COMBAT_RESOLVED`, and has no
  field of its own. The Caveman's unit card and the Help page state it,
  the attack preview shows the line "Pack Hunt +1"
  (`chargePreviewLinesV7`), and the Normal AI's projected damage counts it
  for a hostile Caveman when a visible dinosaur of its owner stands within
  three tiles of the target (`packHuntForPolicyV7`).
- Examples (full HP, Grass): a Caveman deals a Fighter 5 and takes 5; with
  Pack Hunt 8 and takes 4; it deals a Swordsman 4, with Pack Hunt 7;
  with War Drums too it kills a full-HP Fighter (12). A Spitter deals a
  Swordsman 4 from two tiles, and the Caveman on its far side then deals
  the Swordsman (11 of 15 HP) 8.

### 19.15 The Stegosaurus: the Thagomizer

`pulp-wars-poc-7r55` (`pulp_wars-w49.17`). The **Triceratops is the
Dinosaur heavy line unit** (role `SWORDSMAN`, tactical label `LINE`,
Metallurgy): every number and rule it had as the `CATAPULT` role is
unchanged (8 Coins, an Egg of two turns, two slots, 20 HP, Attack 3,
Defense 2, Move 2, Charge!; since `pulp_wars-ke95` it captures; War Drums still skip it and its
attacks still destroy Field Defense, with the reason `CATAPULT`). Where
sections 19.1 to 19.14 call the Triceratops the `CATAPULT` role or a
`SIEGE` unit, read the `SWORDSMAN` role.

The **Stegosaurus** is the siege unit it left (role `CATAPULT`, `SIEGE`;
Sawmilling, which a Dinosaur player sees as Timber): 7 Coins, an Egg that
hatches in two turns, one slot, 12 HP, Attack 2.5, Defense 1, Move 1, range
2 to 3 (never an adjacent target), no attack after moving, capture, no
advance after a kill. It is a dinosaur: Wild, it grows Big and Alpha with
kills ([section 19.8](#198-grow)), and with Wallbreaker it ignores City
Walls like every growing unit. War Drums skip it (a `SIEGE` label). Its
numbers are first guesses.

- **The Thagomizer** (`cracksArmour`). A unit that a Stegosaurus's attack
  hits and does not kill is **Cracked** until the end of the Stegosaurus's
  owner's turn: its Defense is 1 lower (`CRACKED_DEFENSE2_V7` 2
  half-points), never below 0.5 (`CRACKED_MINIMUM_DEFENSE2_V7`). The shot
  that cracks it meets the uncracked Defense. Cracked lowers the Defense
  the unit has against every later attack of that turn, at any distance,
  and the Defense its own strike back is computed from. It does not stack
  (a second shot refreshes nothing), an Egg and the Monster are never
  Cracked, and the list (`ninthUnit.crackedThisTurn`) is emptied at the
  owner's End Turn.
- Every attack of a Stegosaurus destroys a Field Defense on the target's
  tile, as every siege role's does
  ([section 12.3](#123-field-defense)).
- The combat preview says `crackApplied` when the attack would crack its
  target, and a Cracked unit's public stats list "Cracked: -1 Defense this
  turn" (modifier source `CRACKED`).

## 20. Martian faction rules

Humans are sustain, Undead are attrition, Goblins are a reckless horde,
Dinosaurs are few, big, and growing, and Martians are a **small high-tech
invasion force**: frail bodies behind energy Shields that recharge every
turn, heat rays that hit hard and then run hot, machines that walk or fly
over any terrain, troops beamed down from Saucers, and enslaved locals to
hold the front line. They are weak when rushed and focus-fired, and weak in a
sustained brawl. Every rule in this section applies only to units of a
`MARTIAN` seat, except where a rule names its target (Mind Control, the
Tractor Beam, and Pierce act on other players' units); in a match without
one the lists `shields`, `cooling`, `mindControlled`, and `mindControlCooldowns` are
empty, no `BEAM_DOWN`, `MIND_CONTROL`, or `TRACTOR_BEAM` is offered or
accepted, every role has movement mode `GROUND`, and every combat preview
has `rayPower: "NONE"`, `coolingApplied: false`, and both Shield damages 0.
Each rule resolves through the unit's kind's registration (`FACTION_RULES_V7`,
`MARTIAN_ROLE_RULES_V7`, `MARTIAN_ROLE_MECHANICS_V7`) and the helpers of
`src/engine/v7/martian.ts`. Human, Undead, Goblin, Dinosaur, Ice Folk,
Dwarf, and Candy units keep every ability against Martians, with the Shield rules of
[section 20.2](#202-shields) applied to the damage they deal (Frozen is not damage and ignores Shields,
[section 21.14](#2114-interactions-with-other-rules); a Shield absorbs an
eruption and a bomb first,
[section 22.13](#2213-interactions-with-other-rules)).
Specification, per-unit battle analysis, decisions, and the tuning record:
the [Martian overlay](RULESET_7_MARTIANS.md) and the
[Martian balance report](../validation/RULESET_7_MARTIAN_BALANCE.md) (the
`7r25` coarse pass on Dry Land).

### 20.1 Roles, machines, and labels

| Mechanical role | Martian unit     | Kind                       |
| --------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------- |
| `FIGHTER`       | Grunt            | foot                       |
| `RAIDER`        | Saucer           | machine, flyer             |
| `MARKSMAN`      | Ray Gunner       | foot, ray unit             |
| `GUARD`         | Shield Projector | foot                       |
| `CAPTAIN`       | Brain            | foot                       |
| `CATAPULT`      | Tripod           | machine, walker, ray       |
| `KNIGHT`        | Mothership       | machine, flyer             |
| `SWORDSMAN`     | Shock Trooper    | foot; Shock Field (`7r55`) |
| `JUGGERNAUT`    | Colossus         | machine, walker, ray       |

- **Shielded units** are the Martian land roles in every form and, since
  the Hover Fleet (`7r95`), the three Martian ships (Skimmer 2, Hover
  Cruiser 3, Bathysphere 2; a trained ship starts full). A mind-controlled
  unit of another kind has none (its kind's Shield maximum is 0).
- **Machines** have the movement mode `STRIDE` (walkers: Tripod, Colossus)
  or `FLY` (flyers: Saucer, Mothership); every other role of every faction
  is `GROUND`. The public abilities `STRIDE` and `FLY` mirror it. Machines
  never get cover or fortification, need no Engineering for a Mountain, and
  cross water without a Port
  ([section 20.6](#206-movement-stride-flying-and-crossing-water)). **Foot
  units** move like any land unit.
- **Labels:** Rally is **Psychic Command** (the Brain) and the Raider Charge
  is **Strafe** (the Saucer); the commands, flags, and events are the shared
  ones (`RALLY`, `inspired`, `UNITS_RALLIED`; `chargeApplied`). The Tripod
  keeps the `SIEGE` and the Brain the `SUPPORT` label, so neither is ever
  Inspired; the Grunt, Saucer, Ray Gunner, Shield Projector,
  Mothership, and Colossus are Psychic Command targets, and so is a
  mind-controlled unit of another kind by its own role (never `SUPPORT` or
  `SIEGE`).
- **Psychic Command every second turn** (the Martian pass's correction,
  `7r52`; role mechanic `rallyCools`, the Martian `CAPTAIN` only). An
  accepted `RALLY` by a Brain adds `{ unitId, firedThisTurn: true }` to
  `GameStateV7.cooling` ([section 20.4](#204-heat-rays-and-cooling); the
  Cooling step turns it into a Cooling entry at the owner's End Turn and
  removes it at the next), and a Cooling Brain's `RALLY` is not offered
  and is rejected with `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`. So a Brain commands in one
  turn of two. Its Move, its attack, and Mind Control are not affected,
  and a Human Captain (also a controlled one) rallies every turn. State
  parsing accepts a `cooling` entry for a unit whose role has `HEAT_RAY`
  or `rallyCools` under its kind.
- **No Field Defense, no healer:** no Martian unit builds Field Defense, and
  the Brain has no Tend Wounded, so a Martian seat cures neither Plague nor
  Bitten. City Walls are unchanged: a Martian city may choose the Walls
  reward, and Walls fortify a Martian foot unit on its own center.
- **Treasure unit:** a Saucer (`treasureUnitRole` `RAIDER`). **Starting
  unit:** one Grunt. **Militia:** one Grunt. **Level-5+ reward:** a Colossus.
  Every new Martian unit (starting, trained, reward, treasure, Showcase)
  starts at its Shield maximum; no unit is ever created mind-controlled.

### 20.2 Shields

- **Maximum** (role mechanic `shield`): Grunt, Saucer, Ray Gunner, Brain,
  and Tripod 2; Shield Projector and Colossus 3; Mothership 4. It is 0 for
  the boats and for every role of every other faction (read by kind, so
  also for a mind-controlled unit of another faction). No Shield in the game exceeds 4 (`SHIELD_CAP_V7`), so
  a hit of 5 always costs HP.
- **State.** `GameStateV7.shields: { unitId, shield }[]`, sorted by unit ID,
  has one entry for each unit on the board whose current Shield is at least
  1; a unit without an entry has Shield 0. State parsing rejects an entry
  without a unit on the board, a duplicate or unsorted entry, a `shield`
  that is not an integer from 1 to `max(maximum, FORCE_FIELD_SHIELD_V7)`,
  and an entry for a unit whose Shield maximum is 0 (so any entry in a match
  without a Martian seat, and any entry for a boat or a unit of another
  kind).
  `PlayerViewV7.shields` lists the visible units' entries: a visible unit's
  Shield and Shield maximum are public, like its HP.
- **Recharge** at its owner's Start Turn, after the reset, the city actions,
  and the Mind Control cooldown step and **before Plague**
  ([section 3](#3-players-turns-and-victory)): every shielded unit of that
  player on the board, land or embarked, has its Shield **set** to its
  maximum, or to `max(maximum, 4)` when the Force Field covers it
  ([section 20.3](#203-force-field-and-force-fields)). One
  `SHIELDS_RECHARGED { playerId, results: [{ unitId, shield }] }` lists the
  units whose Shield changed, in unit-ID order (none when nothing changed).
  The recharge is not healing: HP is untouched. A Shield recharges at no
  other time, except at End Turn with Force Fields.
- **Damage.** Every instance of damage to a unit is taken from its Shield
  first: `shieldDamage = min(shield, damage)` and
  `hpDamage = min(hp, damage − shieldDamage)`; the unit dies when its HP
  reaches 0. This applies to an attack's hit, the retaliation a unit takes
  as attacker, a splash or Pierce hit, a Wail hit, and a Kaboom or
  death-blast hit; Armoured (no Martian unit has it) applies before the
  Shield. **Plague damage bypasses the Shield.** The damage formula is
  unchanged: both forces use HP and maximum HP, a full Shield raises
  neither, and a hit is capped at Shield plus HP.
- **Derived effects use HP damage:** Lifesteal heals a Vampire by the HP
  damage it dealt; a Zombie bites only a unit that lost HP to its hit; a
  Lich plagues the primary and splash targets that lost HP (a hit a Shield
  absorbed completely plagues nobody, while an unshielded target of a hit of
  0 is still plagued, as before); Infect needs a kill. **Collateral damage
  uses the whole hit:** splash and Pierce are computed from
  `shieldDamage + hpDamage` on the primary target, then each victim's own
  Shield absorbs its share. Plague spread is not damage and ignores Shields.
  Kill credit, growth, Plunder, Graves, and death blasts follow deaths as
  usual.
- **Not damage, so never absorbed:** Push, the Charge! push and follow,
  Knockback, the Tractor Beam, Mind Control, Frozen (every freeze source), Field Defense destruction, and removals. A Shield absorbs a
  Sweep flank hit, a Dwarf eruption, and a Dwarf bomb like any damage, and
  Shatter reads the HP left after the Shield.
  Recovery, Windmill healing, Tend Wounded, Troll regeneration, Promotion,
  and growth change HP only.

Examples (engine formula, full HP, open Grass):

| Hit                                             | Hit | Shield absorbs | HP lost | Note                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --: | -------------: | ------: | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Fighter attacks a Grunt (8 HP, Shield 2)        |   5 |              2 |       3 | the Fighter takes 3 back                           |
| A second Fighter attacks the same Grunt         |   5 |              0 |       5 | the Grunt is dead (two Fighter hits kill it)       |
| Guard attacks a Grunt                           |   3 |              2 |       1 |                                                    |
| Banshee Wail on a Grunt                         |   2 |              2 |       0 | the Wail strips every Shield in its radius         |
| Goblin Kaboom (6) on a Grunt                    |   6 |              2 |       4 | a second blast of 4 or more kills (`w49.35`)       |
| Zombie attacks a Grunt                          |   5 |              2 |       3 | HP was lost, so the Grunt is Bitten                |
| Zombie attacks a Grunt in a Force Field         |   5 |              4 |       1 | still Bitten                                       |
| Fighter attacks a Mothership (20 HP, Shield 4)  |   4 |              4 |       0 | Defense 3 since `7r108` (hit 5, HP 1 at Defense 2) |
| Grunt attacks a Fighter; the Fighter retaliates |   5 |              2 |       3 | the Grunt meets the enemy turn with Shield 0       |
| Vampire at 4 of 10 HP attacks a Grunt           |   6 |              2 |       4 | the Vampire heals 4 (to 8), not 6                  |
| Lich attacks a Grunt next to another Grunt      |   9 |              2 |       7 | splash 5 on the neighbour: Shield 2, HP 3, Plague  |

### 20.3 Force Field and Force Fields

- **Force Field** (the Shield Projector's `FORCE_FIELD`). Since the
  Martian pass (`7r52`) it **needs Force Fields**: a player without the
  technology (capability `projectsForceField`, read from the unit's
  owner's technologies) has no covered unit, and its Projectors' public
  stats carry no `forceField` flag. With it, a shielded unit is
  **covered** when, at the moment of a recharge, one of its owner's Shield
  Projectors in land form, other than itself, stands on one of the eight
  tiles around it. A covered unit recharges to `max(maximum, 4)`
  (`FORCE_FIELD_SHIELD_V7`): the Grunt, Saucer, Ray Gunner, Brain, and Tripod
  to 4 instead of 2, the Shield Projector and Colossus to 4 instead of 3,
  and the Mothership to its own 4. It is not cumulative (two Projectors still
  give 4) and is read at the recharge only: a unit that walks away keeps the
  Shield it has until its next recharge, a unit that walks next to a
  Projector gains nothing until then, and killing the Projector removes
  nothing already granted. The covered unit's form does not matter (an
  embarked unit next to a Projector on the shore is covered); the Projector
  must be in land form; a Martian ship beside it is covered too (`7r95`).
  Boats of other factions and units of another kind (Shield maximum 0)
  gain nothing.
- **The field holds** (the Martian pass's correction, `7r52`;
  `forceFieldHoldsV7`). A unit at full HP whose current Shield is
  `FORCE_FIELD_SHIELD_V7` and above its own Shield maximum (so raised by
  a field and not yet hit since its recharge) is **not killed by one
  attack**: the primary hit of an `ATTACK` on it is capped so that it is
  left at 1 HP (`absorbHitV7` with `holds`; the Shield absorbs first as
  always, so the hit takes the 4 and all but 1 HP). The preview and
  `COMBAT_RESOLVED` carry the capped `damageToDefender` and
  `defenderDies: false`, so there is no advance and no Overrun from it;
  `defenderArmoured` is false for a held hit. The hit spends the Shield,
  so the field holds once and again after the next recharge; no state
  records it. Not held: a wounded unit; a unit whose Shield is below 4; a
  Mothership (its 4 is its own maximum); the retaliation an attacker
  takes; splash, Pierce, a blast, a Dwarf bomb, a Wail, and the ice crush
  (none is the primary hit of an attack); and an Ice Folk Shatter, which
  reads the HP the held hit leaves. A bite, a Plague, Frozen, and a Push are not damage and are as before.
- **Shield Canopy** (the Mothership redesign, `pulp_wars-ewpj`, `7r108`;
  role mechanic `shieldCanopy`, the Martian `KNIGHT` only; ability
  `SHIELD_CANOPY`). A shielded unit beside an own land-form Mothership
  (`isUnderShieldCanopyV7`; not the Mothership itself) is covered at a
  recharge exactly as by a Force Field (`max(maximum, 4)`), **with no
  technology**, and the field holds for it. Without Force Fields the End
  Turn recharge still runs for the units under a Canopy (only for them;
  every other unit keeps its Shield until the Start Turn), so the army
  gathered around a Mothership meets the enemy turn at Shield 4. A
  Mothership's own Shield is its maximum, 4, so it gains nothing and is
  no field. The public `martian` stats carry `shieldCanopy`, and a
  selected Mothership shows the ring like a Projector's.
- **Force Fields** (the Martian `FORTIFICATION`, Industry tier 2, requires
  Drill, ordinary tier-2 cost; capabilities `projectsForceField` and
  `shieldsRechargeAtEndTurn`). While
  its owner has it, its Projectors project the Force Field above, and the
  recharge also runs at that owner's End Turn, after
  idle recovery, the expiry of Inspired and Overrun, and the Cooling step,
  and before the income preview, with the Force Field test made on the
  positions at that moment, emitting `SHIELDS_RECHARGED` like the Start Turn
  step. So Shield spent on retaliation during the owner's own attacks is back
  before the enemy moves, and a unit that ends its turn next to a Projector
  is covered during the enemy turn.

### 20.4 Heat rays and Cooling

Every `ATTACK` made by a land-form unit with `HEAT_RAY` (Ray Gunner, Tripod,
Colossus), at range 1 or 2, is a ray. It fires at **full power** when the
unit has not moved this turn (`activation.moved` false, an interrupted Move
counting as moved) and is not Cooling; otherwise at **half power**:

```text
ray attack2 = full power: role attack2
              half power: floor(role attack2 / 2)
attack      = ray Attack + 1 (Psychic Command)
```

| Unit       | Full Attack (`attack2`) | Half Attack (`attack2`) |
| ---------- | ----------------------: | ----------------------: |
| Ray Gunner |                   3 (6) |                 1.5 (3) |
| Tripod     |                   4 (8) |                   2 (4) |
| Colossus   |                   4 (8) |                   2 (4) |

- The halving applies to the role's base Attack only; Psychic Command's +1
  comes after it. Everything else is the ordinary attack: range,
  visibility, the damage formula, retaliation from a defender that reaches
  the shooter, the advance of a Ray Gunner or Colossus after an adjacent
  kill, and Push for the Colossus at range 1.
- A ray unit's **retaliation** is not a ray: it depends on Defense, is never
  halved, and never causes Cooling.
- **Heat Sinks** (the Martian `FIELDCRAFT`, `7r52`; unlock `HEAT_SINKS`,
  capability `heatSinks`, role mechanic `heatSink` on the Martian
  `MARKSMAN` only; `rayOverheatsV7`). A Ray Gunner whose owner has it
  **does not overheat**: its full-power ray adds no Cooling entry, so it
  fires at full power every turn it has not moved. A ray after a Move is
  still at half power, an entry it already has runs out as usual, and a
  Tripod and a Colossus overheat with or without the technology.
- **Cooling.** A full-power ray (one that the attacker survives) leaves the
  unit Cooling until the end of its owner's next turn (except under Heat
  Sinks); a half-power ray changes nothing. So a ray unit that stands still fires full, half, full,
  half, and on its Cooling turn it loses nothing by moving.
  `GameStateV7.cooling: { unitId, firedThisTurn }[]` (sorted by unit ID): a
  full-power ray adds `{ unitId, firedThisTurn: true }`; a unit **is
  Cooling** exactly while its entry has `firedThisTurn` false. The **Cooling
  step** at the owner's End Turn removes every entry of that player's units
  with `firedThisTurn` false, then sets `firedThisTurn: false` on the
  others. Cooling changes nothing but the ray's power (not Defense, the
  Shield, Move, retaliation, or another ability), persists through embarking
  and landing, and ends when its entry is removed or the unit leaves the
  board. State parsing rejects an entry without a unit on the board whose
  role has `HEAT_RAY` under its owner's registration, a duplicate or unsorted
  entry, a non-boolean flag, and `firedThisTurn: true` for a unit of a
  player other than the active one. `PlayerViewV7.cooling` lists the visible
  units' entries: Cooling is public.
- The combat preview and `COMBAT_RESOLVED` carry `rayPower` (`"FULL"`,
  `"HALF"`, or `"NONE"`; `attack2` includes the halving) and
  `coolingApplied` (true only for a full-power ray of a unit that
  overheats). An estimate for an attack after a planned Move uses half
  power.

Worked examples (engine formula, full HP, open Grass, range 2; the damage
to the target, before the cap at its HP):

| Target (HP, Defense)                       | Ray Gunner full / half | Tripod or Colossus full / half | Marksman | Catapult |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------: | -----------------------------: | -------: | -------: |
| Fighter (12, 2)                            |                  8 / 3 |                         12 / 5 |        5 |       10 |
| Guard (17, 3)                              |                  7 / 2 |                         10 / 4 |        4 |        8 |
| Guard on Field Defense                     |                  6 / 2 |                          9 / 3 |        3 |        7 |
| Guard on a Walled center                   |                  5 / 2 |                          8 / 3 |        3 |        6 |
| Raider or Marksman (12, 1), Knight (10, 1) |                 10 / 4 |                         14 / 6 |        6 |       12 |
| Zombie (18, 2)                             |                  8 / 3 |                         12 / 5 |        5 |       10 |
| Fighter, with Psychic Command              |                 12 / 6 |             — (never Inspired) |        — |        — |

Two turns of a shooter that stands still, against fresh targets: Ray Gunner
8 + 3 = 11 on Fighters (Marksman 5 + 5 = 10); Tripod 12 + 5 = 17 (Catapult
10 + 10 = 20).

### 20.5 Pierce and the Disintegrator

- **Pierce** (the Tripod's `PIERCE`, on every `ATTACK` it makes in land form,
  at full and half power). When the primary target stands in one of the
  eight directions from the Tripod (the offset's `|dx|` and `|dy|` are each 0
  or equal to the distance, at distance 1 or 2; the Tripod fires at distance
  2 only since `pulp_wars-b5f.2`), the unit on the tile
  directly behind it (the target's tile plus one step in that direction) is
  also hit for `max(1, ceil(whole hit on the primary target / 2))`, where the
  whole hit is the Shield plus HP damage the target took (so it is capped at
  the target's Shield plus HP). A target at a knight's-move offset has no
  tile behind it. Pierce hits **any** unit on that tile, own, allied, or
  hostile, hidden or visible, of any form, Eggs included, under the splash
  rules with target mode `ALL`: no retaliation, no modifiers, Armoured and
  the victim's Shield apply, the death cause is `SPLASH`, hostile kills count
  for the Tripod, own or allied kills do not, and the Pierce entry is listed
  in the preview's `splash`. Pierce destroys no Field Defense on the pierced
  tile (the Tripod destroys it on the target tile as a `CATAPULT`-role
  attacker). Examples: a full-power ray on a Fighter (a whole hit of 12, a
  kill) pierces the Marksman behind it for 6; at half power 5 and 3; a
  full-power ray on a Guard 10 and 5.
- **Disintegrator** (the Martian `EXPLOSIVES`, Industry tier 3, requires
  Fortification, ordinary tier-3 cost; capability `raysIgnoreFortification`).
  It keeps Blast Mountain and Breach and adds:
  when a ray (full or half power) is fired by a unit whose owner has it, the
  defender's fortification level is 0 for the damage
  it takes (the Charge! convention; the retaliation never uses
  fortification, [section 13.2](#132-damage)); cover stays,
  and Walls and Field Defense are not destroyed by this rule. The preview
  reports `fortificationLevel: 0` and the removed levels in
  `fortificationIgnored`. Example: a Ray Gunner's full ray on a Guard on a
  Walled center with Field Defense deals 7 instead of 5; a Tripod's 10
  instead of 7.

### 20.6 Movement: Stride, Flying, and crossing water

A **walker** (Tripod, Colossus) in land form:

- enters a Mountain without Engineering, in every rule that asks whether a
  unit may stand on a tile (`canEnterTerrainV7`: `MOVE`, `DISEMBARK`, the
  advance, Push and Tractor Beam destinations, Beam Down, treasure-unit
  placement, reward displacement, and their public twins);
- is never stopped by terrain (`terrainStopsMoveV7`): entering a Forest or a
  Mountain does not end its Move, while an unexplored cell and hostile ZOC
  still do;
- never gets cover or fortification (cover 1 on every terrain, fortification
  level 0 on every tile, Walls and Field Defense included);
- may cross Shallow Water inside a Move and end a Move on it (self-launch,
  below);
- exerts and suffers ZOC, uses Roads, passes only its owner's units, and is
  blocked by other units like any land unit.

A **flyer** (Saucer, Mothership, and the Dwarf Gyrocopter, which has the
same `FLY` movement mode,
[section 22.5](#225-gyrocopters-and-the-bombing-run)) in land form has every
walker rule, and:

- **passes over any unit:** a step onto a tile that holds a unit of any
  owner is entered as if it were empty, at any point of the path except the
  last; a flyer never ends a Move on an occupied tile, and no other player's
  unit passes it;
- **ignores hostile ZOC** (entering it never ends its Move) and **exerts no
  ZOC**;
- may cross Shallow Water, and Deep Water with Navigation, inside a Move;
- **may end a Move, or land from the water, on any settlement center**,
  like any land unit (`pulp_wars-ke95`, user direction 2026-10-09: any unit
  can capture). On a hostile center it besieges the city and blocks its
  capture; on a neutral village or a hostile center it becomes
  capture-eligible at its owner's next Start Turn and may then `CAPTURE`
  ([section 4.7](#47-siege-and-capture)). On its owner's own center it
  blocks training like any unit. (From the Martian revision until
  `pulp_wars-ke95` a flyer could stand only on its owner's own centers: a
  `MOVE` or `DISEMBARK` onto another center was rejected with reason
  `SETTLEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, and it never besieged or captured.);
- **never advances** after a kill (`advancesAfterKill` false) and cannot
  Pillage;
- never destroys Field Defense by entering a tile (it is not on the
  ground); it still destroys it by attack under the ordinary reasons.

What stays ordinary for a flyer: a Move still ends on entering an
unexplored cell and reveals sight from every tile entered, water included;
it occupies its tile; anyone in range attacks it, and it retaliates at range
1; it can be pushed and pulled; it takes a treasure chest by ending a Move
on it; it recovers, is healed, plagued, bitten, and infected, and leaves a
Grave like any land unit. A unit is hidden only on an unexplored tile, so a
flyer meets a hidden unit only on the last tile of its Move, which is then
interrupted as usual.

**Crossing water.** Machines need no Port.

- **Inside a Move,** a flyer may step onto Shallow Water, and onto Deep Water
  if its owner has Navigation; a walker onto Shallow Water only
  (`canCrossWaterV7`). A water step costs what a land step costs, and the
  step that leaves a water tile costs a full point. The unit keeps its land
  form while the Move is validated; only the tile where the Move ends
  matters.
- **Self-launch.** A machine whose Move ends on a water tile, by choice or
  because the Move was stopped or interrupted there, **embarks** there with
  the ordinary result of embarking: form `EMBARKED`, the exhausted
  activation, and `UNIT_EMBARKED`. The tile needs no Port, and the owner
  needs no Shorecraft.
- **Afloat,** a machine is an ordinary embarked unit: Move 2, Defense 1,
  Sight 1, no Attack, no retaliation, no ZOC, no ability, Deep Water with
  Navigation (walkers too), and landing with `DISEMBARK` on an adjacent land
  cell it can enter (a Mountain included, under its movement mode), which
  ends its activation. It keeps its Shield and its Cooling entry, and on a
  hostile dock it blockades. It is drawn as the machine itself over the
  water, never as a boat.
- **Foot units** embark at an own active, empty Port or Shipyard with
  Shorecraft, exactly like Human land units.

**Rifts** (`pulp_wars-9s0.5`): a flyer may enter, cross, and end a Move on
a Rift, and land on it or be pushed, pulled, or placed there; a walker or
foot unit never; a flyer on a Rift is a Mind Control target like any unit
(since `7r99`; it was immune), a flyer
killed there does not rise, and Beam Down never targets a Rift
([Rift overlay](RULESET_7_RIFT.md), implementing
[Martian overlay section 7.4](RULESET_7_MARTIANS.md#74-rift)).

**Overstride** (`pulp_wars-w49.30`,
[section 11.1](#111-the-giants-signatures)): the Colossus has Move 2 and
its `MOVE` passes like a flyer's: through tiles holding units or Eggs of
any owner (never ending on one), ignoring hostile zones of control; an
unexplored tile still ends it, and Mountains, Forests, and Shallow Water
are as for any walker. Each hostile land-form unit or Egg that does not fly
on a tile it passed takes 3 fixed damage once, in path order, after the
Move's events (`UNITS_TRAMPLED`; cause `TRAMPLE`); a passed tile's chest,
curiosity, Crumbs, and Field Defense are untouched. The Colossus lost Push;
its heat ray after an Overstride is at half power.

### 20.7 Beam Down

`BEAM_DOWN { kind, unitId, passengerUnitId, to }` is a primary action of a
**carrier**, a role with `BEAM_DOWN`: the Saucer (the Mothership too
until `7r108`; its carrier action is now Mass Beam Down,
[section 20.7.1](#2071-mass-beam-down)). It
moves one own unit, from a city or from up to two tiles away, to a tile next
to the carrier, and the unit can still attack. It is not an Attack, costs no
Coins, needs no technology beyond the carrier, and spends no city action.
The balance round (`pulp_wars-1wy.3`, `7r37`,
[balance design section 5.1](RULESET_7_BALANCE_MARTIAN_ICE.md#51-m1-beam-down-freed))
freed it: before it only an unmoved Saucer could beam, only from a city,
and the passenger arrived exhausted. Legality is checked in this order, the
first failure being the (atomic) rejection:

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Rejection                                        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | the ordinary unit errors                         |
| 2   | Its role has `BEAM_DOWN`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                     |
| 3   | It has not used a primary action and has not landed this turn. It may have moved; a Frozen carrier may not ([section 21.3](#213-what-a-frozen-unit-cannot-do)).                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                             |
| 4   | It is in land form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `BEAM_DOWN_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`     |
| 5   | (removed in `7r37`: the carrier may have moved; the reason `MOVED` is retired)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | —                                                |
| 6   | `passengerUnitId` is another own unit on the board in land form, whose role uses one slot and whose movement mode is not `FLY`, that has not been beamed this turn, and that **either** stands on or next to the center of a city the actor owns **or** stands within Chebyshev 2 of the carrier (`BEAM_DOWN_PICKUP_RANGE_V7`). A controlled unit or a Tripod qualifies. | `BEAM_DOWN_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NO_PASSENGER" }` |
| 7   | `to` is one of the eight tiles around the carrier, land the passenger can enter (a Mountain needs Engineering unless it strides; never a Rift), with no unit, no mound, and no treasure chest, not a settlement site, and not in territory allied to the actor.                                                                                                          | `INVALID_TILE { action: "BEAM_DOWN" }`           |

Rows 3, 6, and 7 are each one predicate that the reducer and the public
command query share (`beamDownCarrierReadyV7`, `beamDownPassengerLegalV7`,
`beamDownDestinationLegalV7` in `src/engine/v7/martian.ts`), so every
offered `BEAM_DOWN` is accepted and every rejected one is not offered.

- **Result.** The passenger stands on `to` and **counts as having moved
  this turn**, exactly as after an ordinary Move: its activation gets
  `moved` and `handled`, `movedPathLength` is unchanged (a Beam Down is
  never a Charge! run-up), and every other activation flag is kept;
  `captureEligible` becomes false. So a passenger that has not yet acted
  may still use any primary action a unit may use after moving: a Grunt
  shoots at full Attack, a ray unit fires at **half power**
  ([section 20.4](#204-heat-rays-and-cooling)), a Brain may use Mind Control
  or Psychic Command, and a Shield Projector cannot attack (it never
  attacks after moving). It cannot Move again (a pending Escape of a
  controlled unit is spent), Recover, or Capture this turn. A passenger
  that had already acted is only relocated. It keeps its HP, Shield, kills,
  home city, Cooling, and statuses (it may be plagued or bitten). Field
  Defense on `to` is destroyed when the tile's territory belongs to a
  player hostile to the actor (reason `OCCUPATION`). The passenger reveals
  its sight; the carrier has used its primary action and is handled.
- **Once per turn per passenger.** The passenger's ID joins
  `GameStateV7.beamedThisTurn` (sorted unit IDs of the active seat's turn,
  emptied at its End Turn), and a listed unit is not a passenger again
  until its owner's next turn: no chain teleport. The list is public on a
  visible unit (`PlayerViewV7.beamedThisTurn`). State parsing rejects an
  entry that is not a unit on the board owned by the active player, an
  unsorted or duplicate entry, and any entry in a match without a `MARTIAN`
  seat; an entry whose unit left the board or changed owner in the same
  turn (a controlled unit released when its Brain is lost) is dropped.
- **Pick-up and extraction.** A unit that has fired may be picked up by a
  carrier within two tiles and set down on the far side of it, up to three
  tiles from where it fired: the faction's hit-and-run is done by its
  flyers, one carrier action per unit.
- **Events:** `UNIT_BEAMED { playerId, unitId, passengerUnitId, from, to }`,
  `FIELD_DEFENSE_DESTROYED`, `TILES_REVEALED`, then the economy, reward, and
  achievement tail.
- Beam Down is not a Move: no path, ZOC, terrain stop, Road, treasure, or
  embarking. Every tile around a carrier is explored by its owner, so the
  command is exact.

### 20.7.1 Mass Beam Down

The Mothership redesign (`pulp_wars-ewpj`, `7r108`; the user, 2026-10-24:
"like idk - beaming down enemy units into the middle of your army. or mass
beam down of your units. or very strong defence"). The Mothership is slow
(Move 2) and tough, and it **projects the army**:
`MASS_BEAM_DOWN { kind, unitId, passengerUnitIds, to }` is its primary
action (role ability `MASS_BEAM_DOWN`; the Mothership has no single
`BEAM_DOWN` since `7r108`, the Saucer's carrier action). It costs no Coins
and spends no city action. `passengerUnitIds` lists 1 to
`MASS_BEAM_DOWN_CAPACITY_V7` (3) unit IDs in strictly ascending order
without the actor (command parsing rejects any other list). Legality, in
this order (all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Rejection                                             |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | the ordinary unit errors                              |
| 2   | Its role has `MASS_BEAM_DOWN`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                          |
| 3   | The Beam Down carrier rule (`beamDownCarrierReadyV7`): no primary action used and not landed this turn; it may have moved (and used its free Heavy Tractor Beam); a Frozen Mothership may not.                                                      | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                                  |
| 4   | It is in land form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `MASS_BEAM_DOWN_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`     |
| 5   | Every passenger passes the Beam Down passenger rule without the city clause (`massBeamDownPassengerLegalV7`): another own living land-form one-slot unit that does not fly, not beamed this turn, within Chebyshev `BEAM_DOWN_PICKUP_RANGE_V7` (2). | `MASS_BEAM_DOWN_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NO_PASSENGER" }` |
| 6   | `to` is on the board and explored by the actor (every unit on an explored tile is visible, so the command is exact).                                                                                                                                | `INVALID_TILE { action: "MASS_BEAM_DOWN" }`           |
| 7   | `to` is within Chebyshev `MASS_BEAM_DOWN_RANGE_V7` (3) of the Mothership (0 included).                                                                                                                                                              | `MASS_BEAM_DOWN_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OUT_OF_RANGE" }` |
| 8   | Every passenger finds a landing tile (below).                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `MASS_BEAM_DOWN_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NO_ROOM" }`      |

- **Placement** (`massBeamDownPlacementsV7`, deterministic). The landing
  tiles are `to` itself, then the eight tiles around it in (y, x) order
  (`massBeamDownLandingTilesV7`). In unit-ID order each passenger takes
  the first one that passes the Beam Down tile rule of
  [section 20.7](#207-beam-down) row 7 without the carrier adjacency
  (`beamDownLandingLegalV7`: explored land the passenger can enter, never a
  Rift, no unit, mound, or chest, not a settlement site, not in territory
  allied to the actor) and that no earlier passenger took. So a target
  that holds an enemy unit, or a city center, sets the strike force down
  around it. Tiles are read before the command: a passenger's own tile is
  not freed for another.
- **Result.** Each passenger stands on its tile with the Beam Down
  passenger result: it **counts as having moved** (`beamedActivationV7`),
  so one that has not acted may still attack (a ray at half power; a
  Shield Projector not at all), but not Move; `captureEligible` false; its
  ID joins `beamedThisTurn`, once a turn. Field Defense on a landing tile
  in hostile territory is destroyed (`OCCUPATION`). The Mothership stays
  where it is, has used its primary action, and is handled (its free Heavy
  Tractor Beam is still its own). Each passenger reveals its sight.
- **Events:** one `UNIT_BEAMED { playerId, unitId, passengerUnitId, from,
to }` per passenger in unit-ID order (`unitId` is the Mothership), then
  `FIELD_DEFENSE_DESTROYED`, one `TILES_REVEALED`, and the tail. The
  board plays the Beam Down column of light for each passenger.
- **What is offered.** The public query offers one `MASS_BEAM_DOWN` per
  explored tile in reach, in (y, x) order, with the passengers
  `massBeamDownOfferedPassengersV7` picks: the legal passengers that have
  not used a primary action (a fresh strike force), nearest the
  Mothership first and then by unit ID, each one that can still be placed
  with those already chosen, up to three. A tile with none is not
  offered. The reducer accepts any legal set (a unit that has acted may be
  carried, and is only relocated); every offered command is accepted.
  `previewMassBeamDownV7(view, command)` gives the placements and the
  Field Defense the landing destroys, exactly.
- **Board.** Its button arms the aiming: every offered tile is a Place
  target, the pick-up range is tinted, and each unit that would go wears
  "Beam". Choosing a tile previews it ("Beam 3 units" on the tile,
  "Beaming" on the passengers, and on each landing tile, in the Tractor
  Beam's magenta, the name of the unit that lands there); choosing it again,
  or the panel's "Beam down", beams. Back clears the choice. The log line
  names every passenger of one beam ("Your Mothership beamed down a Grunt,
  a Grunt, and a Ray Gunner").
- **Normal AI** (`massBeamDownScoreV7`): per passenger, its best shot on
  arrival (as a Beam Down's: 2 a point of the hit, the target's value on a
  kill, 6 more from two tiles; a passenger that can already shoot where
  it stands counts only a kill), 6 for landing next to a hostile city
  center (16 when the center is empty), and 4 a step toward the wave
  target, less twice its visible danger there and its retained value when
  it would die there without a kill. 1180 with a kill, 906 with a shot,
  865 (the delivery tier) otherwise; nothing without a purpose.
- **Limiters** (`pulp_wars-ewpj`): once a turn per Mothership (a primary
  action) and per passenger (`beamedThisTurn`), passengers only from
  within two tiles (no city pick-up, so the army must gather under the
  slow Mothership), landings never in own territory, and a beamed unit
  cannot Move. No cooldown or extra technology: the Mothership is a
  Chivalry unit already.

### 20.8 Mind Control

`MIND_CONTROL { kind, unitId, targetUnitId }` is a primary action of the
Brain: **any enemy unit beside it** changes sides and **stays what it is**
(`pulp_wars-b5f.3`, `7r33`; the
[Mind Control overlay](RULESET_7_MIND_CONTROL.md) retired the Thrall;
bolder abilities, `pulp_wars-w49.42`, `7r99`, removed the HP limit and
every immunity but an Egg, a neutral unit, and an already controlled unit,
made the reach 1, and raised the limit to three). It is not an Attack and
costs no Coins. Legality, in this order (all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Rejection                                              |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board and is not itself mind-controlled.                                                                                                                                                                                       | the ordinary unit errors; `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }` |
| 2   | Its role has `MIND_CONTROL`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                           |
| 3   | It has not used a primary action and has not landed this turn (it may have moved).                                                                                                                                                                                     | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                                   |
| 4   | It is in land form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`        |
| 5   | It has no entry in `mindControlCooldowns`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "COOLDOWN" }`        |
| 6   | It controls fewer than `MIND_CONTROL_LIMIT_V7` (3; 1 before `7r99`) units.                                                                                                                                                                                             | `MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "CONTROL_LIMIT" }`   |
| 7   | `targetUnitId` is a unit on the board that the actor can see.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `TARGET_NOT_FOUND`                                     |
| 8   | It is hostile to the actor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `TARGET_ALLIED`                                        |
| 9   | It is not an Egg, not a neutral unit, and not already mind-controlled (by any Brain); its tile is known. Any role, size, and form else: a giant, a two-slot unit, a construct, a daemon, a ship or sea beast, an embarked unit, a unit on a settlement site or a Rift. | `MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "TARGET_IMMUNE" }`   |
| 10  | It is on one of the eight tiles around the Brain (Chebyshev distance 1, `MIND_CONTROL_RANGE_V7`; 2 before `7r99`).                                                                                                                                                     | `MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OUT_OF_RANGE" }`    |
| 11  | It is not afloat (`EMBARKED` or `NAVAL`) on Deep Water unless the actor has Navigation (no seat owns a unit afloat there without it).                                                                                                                                  | `MIND_CONTROL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "DEEP_WATER" }`      |

Row 1's own failure (a controlled Brain, possible only in a state with two
Martian seats, which setup's one faction per seat forbids) is
`UNIT_ROLE_INVALID`: a controlled unit's role rule drops `MIND_CONTROL`
([section 20.9](#209-mind-controlled-units)), so such a Brain is never
offered it. Rows 9 to 11 are one shared test (`mindControlTargetBlockV7`)
for the reducer and the public query. Before `7r99` row 9 also refused a
unit not in land form, a `JUGGERNAUT`-role, two-slot, or construct unit,
and one on a settlement site or a Rift, and rows 11 and 12 refused a unit
above 6 HP or unwounded (`TARGET_HEALTHY`, retired).

- **Result.** In one step: the entry
  `{ unitId: target, brainUnitId, originalOwnerId: target's owner }` is
  added to `mindControlled`; the target's `ownerId` becomes the actor, its
  `homeCityId` null (its old city's slot frees at once), `captureEligible`
  false, and it gets the exhausted activation. It keeps everything else: ID,
  role, kind, HP, maximum HP, kills, `veteran`, form, tile, and every status
  entry (Plague, Bitten, Frozen, Shield, Cooling, the Dwarf lists, a
  cooldown). Nothing that depends on it ends: a Lich's Plagues and a
  Witch's Blizzard stay, now on the controller's side. If the target is a
  Brain, its own controlled units are released (section 20.9). Since
  `7r99`: a daemon's strands end (its owner changed: `prunedChannelV7`);
  an Abomination that holds a victim spits it out on the first free land
  tile around it in `(y, x)` order (not a Rift, no unit, Egg, mound, or
  chest; `mindControlSpitTileV7`), in land form, exhausted, not
  capture-eligible, with `SWALLOWED_UNIT_RELEASED`, or, with no such tile,
  it is digested (`UNIT_DIED` cause `DIGESTED`, no credit): a controlled
  Abomination has no Swallow. The Brain has
  used its primary action, is handled, and gets the cooldown entry
  `{ unitId, turnsRemaining: 2 }` (`MIND_CONTROL_COOLDOWN_TURNS_V7`). The
  unit reveals its sight for the actor; then the tail and the naval
  blockade and sea-network events. There is no `UNIT_DIED`, Grave, rising,
  death blast, kill credit, growth, or Plunder.
- **Cooldown.** `GameStateV7.mindControlCooldowns: { unitId, turnsRemaining }[]`
  (sorted by unit ID, 0 to 2): at the Brain's owner's Start Turn, before the
  Shield recharge, each of that player's entries at 0 is removed and every
  other loses 1. So a Brain that used Mind Control on turn `N` cannot on
  `N + 1` and `N + 2` and can again on `N + 3`; the cooldown starts at the
  Mind Control, not at a loss. The cooldown is public on a
  visible Brain (`PlayerViewV7.mindControlCooldowns`). State parsing rejects
  an entry without a unit on the board that has `MIND_CONTROL`, a duplicate
  or unsorted entry, and a value outside 0 to 2.
- **Events:** `UNIT_MIND_CONTROLLED { playerId, unitId, targetUnitId, targetOwnerId, targetRole, at, hp }`
  (the unit keeps its ID: `targetUnitId` is the controlled unit); for a
  Brain target, the release events of section 20.9; `TILES_REVEALED`; the
  tail; the naval blockade and sea-network events.
- Only visible units are targets and no tile changes, so the preview equals
  the result. A plagued or bitten Brain may use Mind Control.

### 20.9 Mind-controlled units

A **mind-controlled** unit is a unit with an entry in
`GameStateV7.mindControlled: { unitId, brainUnitId, originalOwnerId }[]`
(sorted by unit ID; empty in a match without a Martian seat; up to three
entries per Brain since `7r99`). Its owner is
its **controller**; its **kind** is its original owner's faction
(`unitFactionV7`). It resolves label, art, cost, stats, maximum HP,
abilities, role mechanics, and its faction's body rules through its kind,
and every unit-level technology through `unitCapabilitiesV7` (the
controller's research read through the kind's tree; the technology graph
and IDs are the same in every tree). So a controlled Knight is a Knight, a
controlled Goblin can Kaboom, and a Martian without Raiding commands a Wolf
Rider with no Charge. Three rulings decide the rest:

1. **Body rules follow the kind:** everything the unit is and does by itself
   (stats, attacks and their modifiers, movement modes, statuses it causes,
   blasts, healing restrictions such as Restless or Deep Winter recovery).
2. **Seat rules follow the controller:** Coins, cities, capacity,
   territory (Snow from territory too), research, achievements, Plunder,
   hostility, and "own".
3. **No spawning under control:** a controlled unit's role rule drops
   `RAISE_DEAD`, `INFECT`, `BITE`, `HATCH`, `ASSEMBLE`, `MIND_CONTROL`, and
   `RIDES_TUNNEL`, the Favour and Cult-seat abilities, and since `7r99`
   `SWALLOW`, `BREAK_OFF`, `DROWNED_CREW`, and `DEEP_OFFERING`
   (`MIND_CONTROLLED_LOST_ABILITIES_V7`): the commands are
   never offered and are rejected with `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`, and the
   passive rules do not trigger (a controlled Zombie's kill is an ordinary
   death, with a Grave where the Grave rules allow).

| Rule                              | Controlled unit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Turn and commands                 | its controller's; its activation resets at the controller's Start Turn                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Home and capacity                 | `homeCityId` null: no slot anywhere, never re-homed (not even by a capture it makes), an orphan; its public `capacitySlots` is 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Healing                           | ordinary, under the controller ("own territory" is the controller's), with its kind's body rules (Restless for an Undead kind, Deep Winter recovery for Ice Folk)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Promotion, growth                 | by its kind's rules (`PROMOTE` offered to the controller; a dinosaur grows)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Disband                           | `DISBAND` is **Release** (the Martian pass's correction, below); it never pays Coins                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Capture, siege, Pillage, treasure | if its kind can, for the controller                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Psychic Command, Beam Down        | a target and a passenger like an own unit of its role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Kill credit, Slayer, Muster       | its kills keep counting and are its controller's; Muster counts its role for the controller                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Sight and fog                     | reveals for the controller; the original owner sees it as a hostile unit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Per faction                       | Human: all (Field Defense, Rally, Tend Wounded on the controller's units, Charge, Escape, Overrun). Undead: all but Raise Dead, Infect, Bite. Goblin: all (Kaboom, blasts, Ram, Berserk, Gang Up with the controller's helpers). Dinosaur: all but Hatch. Martian: all but Mind Control. Ice Folk: all (her Blizzard halves ranged hits only for Ice Folk units of her controller and stops the controller's ground units). Dwarf: all but Assemble and tunnel riding (a controlled Mole tunnels alone; a controlled Engineer repairs) |

- **Limit.** A Brain controls at most `MIND_CONTROL_LIMIT_V7` (3) units
  (1 before `7r99`). At the limit it is offered no Mind Control
  (`CONTROL_LIMIT`); it never lets the oldest go to take another. A
  release by its controller (below) or a controlled unit's death frees a
  place.
- **Daemons** (since `7r99`). A bound daemon a Brain holds is held by the
  Brain, not by strands: the channel check of its controller's Start Turn
  passes it by (it is never Unbound by the check and owes no Herald
  Hunger), its kills feed no Favour (`daemonKillFavourV7` needs a seat with
  Favour), and it keeps its summoned rules (Boo!, Ravage, Proclaim). When
  it is released it is its Cult seat's bound daemon again, with no strand,
  checked at that seat's next Start Turn.
- **Ships** (since `7r99`). A ship or an embarked unit a Brain holds sails
  for its controller by its kind's rules. A ship a Brain holds that another
  seat boards becomes the boarder's prize of the boarder's kind, and no
  Brain holds it any more.
- **Release by the controller** (the Martian pass's correction, `7r52`).
  `DISBAND { unitId }` on an own mind-controlled land-form unit is offered
  on every turn of its controller, whatever the unit has done and
  whatever the controller has researched, and releases it exactly as the
  loss of its Brain would (`releaseControlledV7`): to its original owner
  where it stands, with `homeCityId` null, `captureEligible` false, and
  the exhausted activation, keeping HP, kills, and statuses; or removed
  with `UNIT_DIED { cause: "BRAIN_LOST" }` if that owner is out of the
  game. Events: `UNIT_RELEASED` and the released unit's `TILES_REVEALED`;
  no `UNIT_DISBANDED` and no Coins. The Brain keeps its Mind Control
  cooldown and may take another unit when it is over.
- **Release.** A controlled unit is released when its Brain leaves the
  board (killed, infected, shattered, disbanded, removed by displacement or
  elimination) or changes owner (mind-controlled itself); a Brain that
  embarks keeps the link. For each of the Brain's entries, in unit-ID
  order (`releaseControlledV7`): if the original owner is not eliminated,
  the entry is removed and the unit returns to it (`ownerId` becomes
  `originalOwnerId`, `homeCityId` stays null, `captureEligible` false, the
  exhausted activation; it keeps HP, kills, statuses, form, and tile,
  standing where it is whatever the movement-entry rules), with
  `UNIT_RELEASED { unitId, brainUnitId, fromPlayerId, toPlayerId, at }`, and
  after the command it reveals its sight for its owner at its final tile; a
  burrowed unit is released in `burrowed` and surfaces at its owner's next
  Start Turn. If the original owner is eliminated, or (since `7r99`) the
  unit is afloat (embarked or naval) on Deep Water and its original owner
  has no Navigation (no seat holds a unit afloat there without it), the
  unit is removed with
  `UNIT_DIED { cause: "BRAIN_LOST" }`: a removal, with no kill credit,
  Plunder, Grave, rising (even if Bitten), or growth. Releases happen right
  after the Brain's own death events (its `UNIT_DIED`, Grave, or rising)
  and before the advance, Push, and any chain of the same command.
- **Seats leaving.** When the controller is eliminated, each unit it
  controls is released first, then its own units are removed (cause
  `ELIMINATION`). When the original owner is eliminated, its controlled
  units stay controlled (the entry keeps `originalOwnerId`, so the kind
  still resolves) and a later release removes them (`BRAIN_LOST`).
- **Death.** A controlled unit's death is an ordinary death of a unit of
  its kind (Graves, Infect and Bitten risings, death blasts, Plunder for the
  killer's seat, kill credit); its entry ends and the Brain's limit frees.
  Bitten and Frozen persist through control and release.
- **Presentation** (`pulp_wars-b5f.3` UI step; details in
  [the Martian overlay of SCREEN_FLOW](../ui/SCREEN_FLOW.md#current-ruleset-7-martian-overlay)).
  A controlled unit is drawn with its kind's sprite and portrait under a
  code-drawn **control halo** (a ring over the head with two tendrils
  down to it, pulsing, static for reduced motion, white in high contrast)
  and a **brain chip**, both in the Martian faction colour; selecting it or
  its Brain draws the dashed control link. Its dock shows a brain badge
  "Controlled" with the controller's and the original owner's names, the
  Brain's "Controls 1 / 3" chip shows its portraits ("Controls three units
  already" at the limit), and a release shatters the halo. Tooltip (since
  `7r99`): "Take any enemy unit next to this Brain, up to three at a time.
  It fights for you as itself until this Brain is lost." The board marks
  every enemy beside the Brain as a target; one it may also hit opens the
  tile's chooser (Attack, Mind Control). Log:
  "{owner} Brain took control of {original owner}'s {unit}", "{unit}
  returned to {owner}", "{unit} was lost with its Brain". The Thrall art
  subjects are retired.
- **State parsing** rejects a duplicate or unsorted entry; a `unitId` that
  is not a unit on the board or burrowed, or whose form is not `LAND` or
  `EMBARKED`, or whose `homeCityId` is not null; an `originalOwnerId` equal
  to the unit's owner or not a player of the match (an eliminated player is
  allowed); a `brainUnitId` that is not a unit on the board of the same
  owner whose role, under its kind, has `MIND_CONTROL`, or that is itself
  controlled; more than `MIND_CONTROL_LIMIT_V7` entries for one Brain; an
  Egg (since `7r99` any other form, role, and size is legal: before, a
  `JUGGERNAUT`-role, two-slot, or construct unit and any form but `LAND`
  or `EMBARKED` were rejected, and a summoned unit could not be
  controlled); an owner that is not a `MARTIAN` seat; and any entry in a
  match without a `MARTIAN` seat.
- **View.** `PlayerViewV7.mindControlled` lists
  `{ unitId, brainUnitId, originalOwnerId }` for every visible controlled
  unit (and visible mound), with `brainUnitId` null when the viewer cannot
  see the Brain; `originalOwnerId` is public.

### 20.10 Tractor Beam

`TRACTOR_BEAM { kind, unitId, targetUnitId }` pulls a unit **toward the
puller**, the mirror of Push. It deals no damage, is not an Attack, and
costs no Coins. Two roles have it since the balance round
(`pulp_wars-1wy.3`, `7r37`,
[balance design sections 5.2 and 5.3](RULESET_7_BALANCE_MARTIAN_ICE.md#52-m2-the-tractor-beam-on-the-saucer);
before it only the Mothership, as a primary action at exactly two tiles):

| Puller         | Reach (Chebyshev)                         | Pull                                                         | Action cost                                                                              |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Saucer**     | exactly 2 (`TRACTOR_BEAM_RANGE_V7`)       | 1 tile (`TRACTOR_BEAM_PULL_V7`)                              | its primary action (one of Attack, Beam Down, Tractor Beam per turn)                     |
| **Mothership** | 2 or 3 (up to `HEAVY_TRACTOR_RANGE_V7` 3) | up to 2 tiles (`HEAVY_TRACTOR_PULL_V7`), stopping next to it | the **Heavy Tractor Beam**: free, once a turn; it may still Move (if it has not) and act |

The Heavy Tractor Beam is the role mechanic `heavyTractorBeam` (the Martian
`KNIGHT` only); `tractorBeamRuleV7` returns a puller's reach, pull, and
cost.

- **Actor.** The actor's own puller (`TRACTOR_BEAM`) in land form. A
  **Saucer** has not used a primary action and has not landed this turn
  (it may have moved). A **Mothership** has not landed this turn (more
  exactly: its activation is not the exhausted one of a unit that landed,
  embarked, or was trained this turn) and has not used its Tractor Beam
  this turn; it may have moved and may have used its primary action. A Frozen puller cannot use it
  ([section 21.3](#213-what-a-frozen-unit-cannot-do)).
- **Target.** A unit on the board the actor can see, **own or hostile**
  (never allied), within the puller's reach, in any form, that is not an
  Egg, whose role is not `JUGGERNAUT`, that is not the Giant Spider, and
  that uses one slot. A construct is a legal target.
- **City Walls hold** (step two of the Martian pass, `7r58`;
