| Lifesteal, Unanswered   | A Vampire is a melee attacker, never halved; an Ice Folk unit never retaliates against it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Undead actions          | A Frozen Necromancer, Ghoul, or Banshee can use neither Frenzy, Raise Dead, Devour, nor Wail. Undead units are Frozen like anyone. Restless is not an Ice Folk rule.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Goblin rules            | [Section 18.11](#1811-interactions-with-other-rules): blasts ignore Snow cover and the Blizzard, a shattered exploding unit does not explode, a Frozen goblin-crewed unit cannot Kaboom, and Gang Up beats cover (a Goblin with two helpers deals a Yeti 11 in the open and 10 on Snow, either way more than its 9 HP).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Dinosaur rules          | [Section 19.12](#1912-interactions-with-other-rules): Eggs are never Frozen or shattered; deep snow cuts a run-up and a Pounce short; Charge! and Wallbreaker ignore fortification but not Snow cover, which is read from the defender's own fortification.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Martian rules           | [Section 20.11](#2011-interactions-with-other-rules): Frozen ignores Shields; Shatter reads the HP after the Shield; walkers and flyers ignore deep snow; the Frost Giant is immune to the Tractor Beam (a Brain takes it since `7r99`); a mind-controlled Ice Folk unit keeps its Ice Folk rules (a controlled Witch's Blizzard serves her controller).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Human abilities         | Field Defense and Walls give a defender their bonus against every Ice Folk attack except a Boulder Yeti's; a Mammoth's attack tramples the Field Defense on the target tile after the exchange; with Brittle, Ice Folk melee attackers demolish Field Defense like any owner of Explosives. A Frozen Captain cannot Rally and a Frozen Knight cannot attack. A Catapult always shoots from distance 2 or 3 and a Marksman from 2 is halved against a protected unit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Cities, siege, capacity | An Ice Folk unit on a hostile center besieges it (never a Sabretooth). A Frozen unit on a center still besieges it but cannot capture it until it thaws. Every Ice Folk role uses one slot; a reward Frost Giant may exceed capacity. Land Grant, Spoils, rewards, and the city action are unchanged; Bolas and Cold Snap spend no city action.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Boats, water            | The Ice Folk have no boats and never embark; they freeze the sea ([section 21.16](#2116-the-frozen-sea)). No embarked or naval unit of any faction is Frozen or shattered, so an icebound ship is crushed, not shattered; an attack from the shore on an embarked unit never shatters it, and a naval attack from distance 2 or more on a protected unit is halved (a Battleship's splash from the halved hit). The `blizzard` flag covers water tiles for drawing only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Rift                    | A Rift is never Snow and Mountain-born does not cover it, so no Ice Folk unit enters one. A flyer on a Rift is in land form: it can be Frozen, attacked from an adjacent tile, and shattered; the attacker does not advance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Achievements, Promotion | Promotion is the ordinary rule for every Ice Folk unit (3 kills, +5 maximum HP, a full heal that takes a unit out of the Shatter window but does not thaw it). Shatter, hostile Sweep, Rockfall, Boulder, and retaliation kills are credited; a Bolas and a Cold Snap are not kills. Muster counts the Ice Folk trainable roles and excludes the Frost Giant; Slayer counts Shatter and Sweep kills.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Dwarf rules             | [Section 22.13](#2213-interactions-with-other-rules): tunnels ignore Snow, and a surfaced unit stands on Snow like any ground unit; deep snow ends a Dwarf ground unit's Move (only the Move-2 Steam Tank notices), and the Gyrocopter flies over it. Every Dwarf land unit can be Frozen, constructs and the Brass Titan included, and shattered, except the Brass Titan (`JUGGERNAUT`); a mound is neither; a burrowed unit's Frozen entry keeps counting down at its owner's End Turn, and the Engineer's Repair thaws it. A Frozen Gyrocopter cannot bomb, a Frozen Mole cannot tunnel, a Frozen Hammerer cannot ride, a Frozen Gunner cannot fire, and a Frozen Engineer can neither Repair nor Assemble. The Shatter test reads a Steam Tank's HP after the Plated cap. The Blizzard halves a Gunner's or a Steam Cannon's shot from distance 2 or more, never a bomb or an eruption (not attacks); bombs and eruptions also ignore Snow cover. |

### 21.15 Commands, events, errors, and queries

- **Commands:** `THROW_BOLAS { kind, unitId, targetUnitId }` and
  `COLD_SNAP { kind, unitId }`, in that order right after `TRACTOR_BEAM` in
  `COMMAND_KIND_ORDER_V7`; `FROST_BOLT { kind, unitId, targetUnitId }` and
  `STAMPEDE { kind, unitId, at }` (`pulp_wars-w49.37`), in that order right
  after `BREAK_OFF`. `MOVE` accepts the Glide costs, the Mountain-born
  paths, and the Sabretooth's paths through ZOC, and applies deep snow;
  `ATTACK` accepts a Yeti's distance-2 target from a Mountain. A pending city reward blocks these commands like every command.
- **Events** (`DOMAIN_EVENT_KIND_ORDER_V7`): `UNITS_FROZEN` (named
  `UNITS_CHILLED` before `pulp_wars-w49.37`, in the same place) right after
  `UNITS_RALLIED`, with `results: [{ unitId, turnsLeft }]`;
  `MAMMOTH_STAMPEDED` right after `GIANT_BROKE_OFF`
  ([section 21.18](#2118-the-mammoths-stampede)).
  `UNIT_DIED.cause` gains `SHATTER` and `STAMPEDE` (never followed by `GRAVE_CREATED`; it
  may be followed by `BITTEN_UNIT_RISEN`); `FIELD_DEFENSE_DESTROYED.reason`
  gains `TRAMPLE`; `UNIT_MOVE_INTERRUPTED.reason` gains `SNOW`;
  `WOUNDED_TENDED` results gain `curedFrozen`; `noRetaliationReason` gains
  `FROZEN`. There is no event for the countdown or the thaw, or for Snow
  appearing or disappearing.
- **Combat preview** (`CombatPreviewV7`, so also `COMBAT_RESOLVED`), eight
  fields, all false for an attack that involves no Ice Folk unit:
  `shatters`, `coldBloodApplied`, `rockfallApplied`, `plantedApplied`,
  `blizzardHalved` (`damageToDefender` is the halved value), `snowCover`
  (the defender's × 1.25 comes from Snow), `sweep` (the flank victims are the
  `splash` entries), and `hiddenBlizzardPossible` (public previews only).
  Boulders report `fortificationLevel: 0` and `fortificationIgnored`; a
  Trample is read from `sweep` and the target tile's Field Defense.
- **Errors:** `UNIT_FROZEN { unitId }`; `BOLAS_NOT_LEGAL` and
  `FROST_BOLT_NOT_LEGAL` (reasons `EMBARKED`, `TARGET_IMMUNE`,
  `OUT_OF_RANGE`), `COLD_SNAP_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `NO_TARGET`), and
  `STAMPEDE_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `MOVED`, `DIRECTION`, `BLOCKED`); the
  movement failure reasons gain `SNOW_STOPS_MOVE` (`SETTLEMENT_FORBIDDEN`
  covered the Sabretooth until `pulp_wars-ke95`). A Frozen unit's refused
  command is `UNIT_FROZEN`.
- **Registration:** faction `ICE_FOLK`, tree `ICE_FOLK_BASELINE_V1`,
  display name "Ice Folk"; unlock kinds `WITCH_SUPPORT`, `DEEP_WINTER`, and
  `BRITTLE`; capabilities `deepWinter` and `shatterThreshold`; abilities
  `MOUNTAIN_BORN`, `ROCKFALL`, `BOLAS`, `COLD_BLOOD`, `SWEEP`, `TRAMPLE`,
  `BLIZZARD`, `COLD_SNAP`, `FROST_BOLT`, `BOULDERS`, `PROWL`, `COLD_AURA`,
  and `STAMPEDE`; role
  mechanics `mountainBorn`, `glides`, `ignoresZocStops`, `sweepDamage`,
  `tramplesFieldDefense`, `ignoresFortification`, `plantedBonus2`,
  `rockfallAttack2`, and `coldBloodBonus2`, with `buildsFieldDefense` false
  for the Yeti and the Mammoth and `advancesAfterKill` false for the Boulder
  Yeti; faction rules `snow` true and `treasureUnitRole` `RAIDER`; constants
  `SHATTER_HP_V7` 3, `BRITTLE_SHATTER_HP_V7` 4, `BOLAS_RANGE_V7` 2,
  `COLD_SNAP_RANGE_V7` 1, `FROST_BOLT_RANGE_V7` 2, `STAMPEDE_RANGE_V7` 3,
  `STAMPEDE_DAMAGE_V7` 3, `GLACIER_ICE_MOVE_BONUS_V7` 1,
  `BLIZZARD_RADIUS_V7` 1,
  `DEEP_WINTER_RADIUS_V7` 2, `DEEP_WINTER_RECOVER_V7` 6, `SWEEP_DAMAGE_V7`
  2, `ROCKFALL_ATTACK2_V7` 3, `PLANTED_BONUS2_V7` 2, and
  `COLD_BLOOD_BONUS2_V7` 1.
- **Derived queries** for a state and a view: `isSnowV7` and `isBlizzardV7`
  (on a view, the public `snow` and `blizzard` tile flags, which the UI
  draws from and never recomputes), `unitIsFrozenV7`,
  `unitMayActAfterMoveV7`, and `unitMayEnterMountainV7`.
- **`queryPlayerCommandsV7`** offers, for an Ice Folk seat, `MOVE` commands
  that follow Glide, Mountain-born, and Prowl; `ATTACK` at distance 2 for a
  Yeti on a Mountain; `THROW_BOLAS` for every legal `(Sled, target)` and
  `FROST_BOLT` for every legal `(Witch, target)` in unit-ID then target-ID
  order; `COLD_SNAP` for every Witch with a target; and `STAMPEDE` for
  every open end of every line of an unmoved Mammoth. For every seat it
  withholds every command naming a Frozen unit (but Promote, Disband, and
  Wait) and offers no `MOVE` through a known Snow stop. It never offers an
  Ice Folk seat Field Defense, Rally, or Tend Wounded. Every offered
  command is accepted.
- **`previewBolasV7(view, unitId, targetUnitId)`** returns null unless that
  command is offered, otherwise
  `{ unitId, targetUnitId, alreadyFrozen, turnsLeft, shatterSetups }`,
  where `shatterSetups` lists the viewer's own units whose offered attack on
  the target would shatter it once it is Frozen;
  **`previewFrostBoltV7`** returns the same for an offered Frost Bolt.
  **`previewColdSnapV7(view, unitId)`** returns null unless the command is
  offered, otherwise `{ unitId, targets: [{ unitId, alreadyFrozen }] }` in unit-ID
  order. **`previewStampedeV7(view, unitId, at)`**: see
  [section 21.18](#2118-the-mammoths-stampede).
- `queryCombatPreviewV7` and `estimateCombatV7` include Snow cover, the
  Blizzard of visible Witches, Rockfall, Planted (from the unit's `moved`
  flag; Attack 2 for an attack after a planned Move), Cold Blood, Sweep, and
  Shatter, no retaliation from a Frozen defender, and accept the option
  `assumeTargetFrozen`. Every preview
  equals the resolution, except one flagged `hiddenBlizzardPossible` or
  `touchesUnexplored` (a Wail preview flags it per target).
  `queryThreatenedTilesV7` gives a visible Ice Folk
  unit its Glide reach on known Snow, a Mountain-born unit its Mountain
  paths, a Sabretooth its reach through ZOC, a Yeti the distance-2 tiles
  from every Mountain origin, and a Boulder Yeti range 2 from every tile it
  can reach; it adds nothing for a Bolas, a Frost Bolt, a Cold Snap, or a Stampede, and
  a Frozen unit of any seat threatens nothing.
- **Public unit stats** carry, for every unit, `frozen` (null, or `{ turnsLeft }`), and for units of an Ice Folk seat the
  `iceFolk` block: `onSnow`, `inBlizzard`, `snowCover`, `glides`,
  `mountainBorn`, `shatterThreshold`, `rockfall` (true while it stands on a
  Mountain), `planted` (what an attack made now would be, or null),
  `sweepDamage`, and `blizzard` (true for a land-form Witch). The position
  facts are the Snow and Blizzard the reader knows of. The Attack row lists
  the source `PLANTED`; a snowy cover row reads `SNOW`.
- `PublicPlayerV7` and the leaderboard carry `ICE_FOLK` and
  `ICE_FOLK_BASELINE_V1`.
- The commands, events, errors, and queries of the frozen sea (`FREEZE`,
  the `ice` list, `WATER_FROZEN`, `ICE_MELTED`, `UNITS_CRUSHED`,
  `previewFreezeV7`) are in [section 21.16](#2116-the-frozen-sea).

### 21.16 The frozen sea

The Ice Folk Naval branch (`pulp_wars-5ti.3`, `pulp-wars-poc-7r44`; the
[naval branch overlay](RULESET_7_NAVAL_BRANCH.md), section 8), as
**redesigned** by `pulp_wars-5ti.25` at `pulp-wars-poc-7r100`
([RULESET_7_ICE_REDESIGN.md](RULESET_7_ICE_REDESIGN.md); the user,
2026-10-18: "ice should stay by default. other factions should have the
option to crack ice around them"). An Ice Folk seat never builds a ship.
With **Rime** its units freeze the water next to them, two tiles out in a
line (the Ice Witch: every tile around her), and **the ice stays**. Their
units **slide** across it; their cities **build on it** (the Ice Harbour,
Fishing Holes, and their mills and markets), so frozen home water is new
land, not lost water. Everyone else may walk on it slowly (a Move ends on
entering it), and every unit and ship of the other eight factions may
**Crack** the ice next to it back into open water. **Pack Ice** freezes
the deep sea, **Black Ice** freezes an enemy that steps onto the ice,
**Icebound** locks ships in to be crushed, and **Glacier** makes the ice
thick enough to take two Cracks. In a match without an Ice Folk seat
nothing here happens: the `ice` list is always empty.

| Rule       | One sentence                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Freeze     | A unit turns the water next to it to ice, two tiles out in a line; the Witch freezes every tile around her.                       |
| Ice stays  | Ice never melts; it is gone only when someone cracks it.                                                                          |
| Border ice | With Rime, the water inside your borders turns to ice, and again whenever a city's borders grow.                                  |
| Slide      | An Ice Folk unit that steps onto ice slides straight on until the ice ends, a unit blocks it, or an enemy's zone of control.      |
| Runners    | A Sled's slide is not stopped by zones of control.                                                                                |
| Slip       | Any other unit may walk onto ice, but its Move ends there.                                                                        |
| Crack Ice  | Any other unit or ship next to ice may break one tile of it back into water, unless a unit stands on it or it is built on.        |
| Build      | The Ice Folk build their Ice Harbour, Fishing Holes, mills, Workshop, Market and Monument on their own ice.                       |
| No ships   | Ships cannot enter ice; the Ice Folk have no ships at all.                                                                        |
| Black Ice  | An enemy that steps onto your ice is Frozen.                                                                                      |
| Icebound   | Freeze a ship in place: it cannot sail, shoot, or strike back, and the ice crushes it for 3 each turn until it sinks or is freed. |
| Glacier    | Your ice is thick: others must Crack Ice twice to break it, and your Freeze mends a crack; Snow cover and +1 Move across it.      |

**Ice tiles.**

- **State.** `GameStateV7.ice: { at, ownerId, cracked }[]`, sorted by
  `(y, x)`, hashed, saved, and replayed (`turnsLeft` is gone with `7r100`).
  An **ice tile** is a water tile (Shallow or Deep) with an entry. Its
  terrain does not change: ice is a layer, so no command turns water into
  land and map generation is untouched. `cracked` is true only on thick
  ice that has taken one Crack. State parsing rejects an entry off the
  board or on a land tile, a duplicate or unsorted entry, a `turnsLeft`
  key, an `ownerId` that is not a player of the match, `cracked` true on
  ice whose owner has no thick ice (no Glacier, or eliminated), and any
  entry in a match without an Ice Folk seat. It also rejects a building on
  water that is not on ice (except a Port or Shipyard on open Shallow
  Water), a unit of the Ice Folk kind in `NAVAL` or `EMBARKED` form, and
  an Ice Folk seat that owns a unit in `NAVAL` form, and it admits a
  land-form unit on a water tile only where that tile is ice. Ice may lie
  on a dock (an Ice Harbour) and under any Ice Folk building.
- **View.** `PlayerViewV7.ice` lists the entries on tiles the viewer has
  explored as `{ at, ownerId, cracked, thick }` (`permanent` and
  `turnsLeft` are gone). `thick` is the owner's Glacier (`thickIce`,
  through `technologyCapabilitiesV7`; an eliminated owner has none):
  publishing it reveals the owner's Glacier, which the public `iceCover`
  unit stat already does, so every Crack preview is exact.
- **Permanence.** Ice has no countdown and there is no thaw step: an entry
  leaves the list only by a Crack or by the elimination release below (a
  Redevelop or a Pillage removes the building and leaves the ice).
  Nothing anyone does keeps ice alive, so nothing has to be done.
- **Ownership.** A Freeze makes or takes the tile for the actor's owner.
  **Capture:** when a city changes owner, every ice entry of the former
  owner on that city's territory passes to the captor, with `cracked`
  false; ice elsewhere keeps its owner. **Elimination:** an eliminated
  seat's ice stays; every icebound unit on it floats free at once (its
  tile's entry goes: `ICE_MELTED { tiles, freed }`, kept for this one
  use), its cracks are gone (an eliminated owner has no thick ice), and
  the rest breaks with one Crack.
- **The border freeze** (`pulp_wars-5ti.31`, `7r109`; the user,
  2026-10-24: "when doing land grant and city boundaries expand any water
  within city boundaries (including water within the original boundaries)
  should get covered with ice IF you have the relevant technology"). When
  an Ice Folk city's borders grow, every tile of **that city's whole
  territory** goes through the Freeze table below on its own, with the
  seat's own `freezeWater` and `icebound` (`territoryFreezeV7`): open
  water with no unit (an own dock too, which becomes an Ice Harbour) is
  made ice; with Icebound a hostile ship on it is locked in; another
  player's ice is taken; own cracked ice is mended; own sound ice, an
  unexplored tile, Deep Water without Pack Ice, the Sea Serpent's tile,
  and a tile holding any other afloat unit are left. There is no line, no
  ring, and no stop. The triggers: a **Land Grant** of the city, a
  **capture** (a village captured into a city, or a city taken; after the
  former owner's ice there passed), and a **research** that changes the
  seat's `freezeWater` or `icebound` (Rime, Pack Ice, Icebound), which
  freezes the territory of every own city. City levels never grow borders
  in this ruleset. A seat without Rime, and every seat of another
  faction, freezes nothing. The result is one `WATER_FROZEN` with
  `unitId` null (no unit froze; projected like any `WATER_FROZEN`), right
  after `LAND_GRANTED` and its `TILES_REVEALED`, after the capture's
  `TILES_REVEALED`, or after `TECH_RESEARCHED`, and the live economy is
  recomputed as the command does anyway. No unit acts, nothing is
  charged, and Black Ice is not triggered (no unit stepped on). Tiles in
  other seats' borders are never touched. The Normal AI values an Ice
  Folk Land Grant two more for each water tile it would freeze
  (`landGrantIceTilesV7`).
- **Ground for land-form units.** For a land-form unit of every faction and
  movement mode an ice tile is ground (`canEnterTerrainV7`), whatever the
  depth and without Navigation or Engineering: it may be the end of a
  `MOVE`, a `DISEMBARK` target, the destination of a Push, a Charge! push
  or follow, a Knockback, a Tractor Beam pull, an advance, a Beam Down,
  and a bombing-run landing (a Gyrocopter stands on it and does not
  self-launch, and neither does a Martian machine that ends a Move there).
  A land unit projects ZOC onto adjacent ice as onto land.
- **Water for everything else.** No terrain cover (Glacier gives Ice Folk
  units the Snow cover there), no Walls or Field Defense, never Snow, and
  no Road, Grave, Egg, mound, Crumbs, chest, reward or treasure unit,
  rising, Re-bake, Assemble, or tunnel end on it; buildings only those of
  an Ice Folk seat ([section 8.1](#81-common-placement-gates)). **A unit
  on ice has no fortification of any kind** (since `7r45`, a Dwarf is
  never dug in on ice; [section 22.7](#227-dig-in)); Glacier's cover is the
  only shelter on ice. A unit standing on ice acts on the land beside it
  as usual. **A death on ice is a water death:** no Grave, no Infect or
  Bitten rising, no Crumbs. The tile's Fish or Pearls stay and may be
  harvested under the ordinary gates. A sea link counts an ice tile as
  water. A tunnel never passes under it, and an eruption hits a land-form
  unit standing on it. Ice is not land for Roads (the slide is the Ice
  Folk road) nor for the Port's shore rule.
- **Ships cannot enter ice.** A unit afloat (`NAVAL` or `EMBARKED`) never
  enters, passes, or is pushed, shoved, or pulled onto an ice tile, and a
  naval unit projects no ZOC onto ice. The only afloat unit ever on ice is
  one frozen in (Icebound, below).

**Freeze.** `FREEZE { kind, unitId, at }` is a primary action of every Ice
Folk land role (ability `FREEZE`). It is not an Attack and costs no Coins.
Legality, in this order (all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                     | Rejection                                     |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                                  | the ordinary unit errors                      |
| 2   | Its role, under its kind, has `FREEZE` (a land role of the Ice Folk), and it is in land form.                   | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                  |
| 3   | Its kind's capabilities under its owner have `freezeWater` `SHALLOW` or `DEEP` (Rime).                          | `TECH_REQUIRED { tech: "SHORECRAFT" }`        |
| 4   | It is not Frozen, and it has not used a primary action.                                                         | `UNIT_FROZEN`; `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`           |
| 5   | For the Ice Witch, `at` is her own tile; for every other role, `at` is one of the eight tiles next to the unit. | `FREEZE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OUT_OF_RANGE" }` |
| 6   | The freeze set (below) is not empty: **a Freeze that changes nothing is neither offered nor accepted**.         | `FREEZE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NO_TARGET" }`    |

A tile is **freezable** when it is on the board, explored by the actor, and
water (Shallow, or Deep with `freezeWater` `DEEP`, Pack Ice); a dock that
is not the actor's own never freezes (so no Port of another player is ever
frozen shut). Then:

| Tile                                               | Freeze does                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| open water with no unit (the actor's own dock too) | makes ice (a frozen dock is an Ice Harbour)       |
| open water holding a hostile ship, with Icebound   | makes ice and locks the ship in (icebound)        |
| ice of another player (any occupant)               | takes it for the actor (`cracked` false)          |
| the actor's own **cracked** ice (any occupant)     | mends the crack                                   |
| the actor's own sound ice                          | **nothing: passed over** (not taken, not offered) |

- **A line, for every role but the Witch** (`FREEZE_LINE_V7` 2): the tile
  `at` and the one beyond it, outward from the unit. Each is taken if
  freezable; the actor's own sound ice is passed over and the line goes
  on; any other tile ends the line, and so does a tile that holds a unit
  afloat. So a Yeti on a shore with one tile of its ice in front freezes
  the second tile, and a unit at the tip of a bridge freezes the next two.
- **A ring, for the Ice Witch** (`WITCH_FREEZE_RADIUS_V7` 1; the role with
  the Blizzard): every freezable tile within Chebyshev 1 of her, her own
  tile included when she stands on cracked or foreign ice.
- **Result.** Every tile of the set gets `{ at, ownerId: the actor,
cracked: false }`, replacing any earlier entry. The Freezing unit is
  marked like a unit that used a special action (`specialActed` and
  `handled`). Event `WATER_FROZEN { playerId, unitId, tiles, icebound }`.
  A Freeze over an own dock recomputes the live economy (an icebound
  blockader no longer blockades it), so `FREEZE` is on the blockade-event
  list.
- **Preview.** `previewFreezeV7(view, unitId, at)` returns null unless the
  command is offered, otherwise `{ unitId, tiles, mended, taken, icebound }`
  (`refreshed`, `turns`, and `permanent` are gone): exact.

**Crack Ice.** `CRACK_ICE { kind, unitId, at }`, a primary action of every
unit **not of the Ice Folk kind** (a kind rule like the slip, so a
mind-controlled Ice Folk unit never cracks) in land, naval, or embarked
form: every land role and every ship of the eight other factions. Free,
no technology, not an attack. Legality, in this order:

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                | Rejection                                           |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                             | the ordinary unit errors                            |
| 2   | It is not of the Ice Folk kind and is in `LAND`, `NAVAL`, or `EMBARKED` form.                              | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                        |
| 2a  | It is not icebound.                                                                                        | `CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`        |
| 3   | It is not Frozen or Crashed; it has not used a primary action; if it moved, its role may act after moving. | `UNIT_FROZEN`; `UNIT_CRASHED`; `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED` |
| 4   | `at` is one of the eight tiles next to the unit (never its own tile).                                      | `CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OUT_OF_RANGE" }`    |
| 5   | `at` is explored ice that is not an ally's (hostile, own, or an eliminated player's).                      | `CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NO_ICE" }`          |
| 6   | No land-form unit stands on it (an icebound ship may).                                                     | `CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OCCUPIED" }`        |
| 7   | No improvement stands on it (Pillage it instead).                                                          | `CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "BUILT" }`           |

An Egg and a burrowed unit are refused before these rows by the common
refusals (`UNIT_IS_EGG`, `UNIT_ALREADY_HANDLED`).

- **Result.** Thick ice (its owner has Glacier) that is not cracked
  becomes `cracked: true`: still ice in every way; the next Crack breaks
  it, and a Freeze of its owner mends it (`ICE_CRACKS_THICK_V7` 2). Any
  other ice **breaks**: the entry goes and the tile is open water again
  (its Fish, Pearls, or Wreck as before). An icebound unit on a broken tile
  floats free at once; its activation is untouched, so if it belongs to the
  active player and has not acted it may sail and act this turn. The
  cracking unit has used its primary action and is handled. Event
  `ICE_CRACKED { playerId, unitId, at, broken, freed }` (`freed` the freed
  unit IDs in ID order, empty for a crack), right after `WATER_FROZEN` in
  `DOMAIN_EVENT_KIND_ORDER_V7`; projected to every viewer that explored
  `at`, with `unitId` null when it cannot see the unit.
- **Preview.** `previewCrackIceV7(view, unitId, at)` returns null unless
  offered, otherwise `{ unitId, at, broken, freed }`: exact, since
  `thick`, `cracked`, and the occupants are public.
- **Why these limits:** a crack under a land unit would be a free kill by
  any Warrior; the Ice Folk economy on the ice must not be one free action
  from deletion (Pillage is the paid-for way); a navy must be able to cut
  its own lane; the Ice Folk make ice and never need to break their own.

**Slide.** A land-form unit of the Ice Folk kind whose role mechanic
`glides` is true (every Ice Folk land role but the Sabretooth) slides; it
is a body rule, so a mind-controlled Ice Folk unit slides for its
controller.

- When a step of its `MOVE` **enters an ice tile** in direction `d` (one of
  the eight), it continues in `d`, tile after tile, **at no cost**, while
  the next tile in `d` is on the board, explored by the mover before the
  command, an ice tile (read from the state before the command, like
  Snow), and holds no unit and no mound (the mover's own units included),
  and while the tile it is on is not in a hostile ZOC. It stops on the last
  tile so entered. With permanent ice the slide is the Ice Folk road
  network: a bridge built once is used for the rest of the match.
- **Runners** (the Sled, role mechanic `runners`, `7r100`): a Sled's slide
  **goes on through a hostile zone of control**; it still stops at a unit,
  a mound, and the end of the ice, and where its slide ends in a zone the
  Move ends there, as any step's. Slid tiles count for its Charge and its
  Bolas reach after the Move. A body rule (a mind-controlled Sled keeps
  it); public stat `iceFolk.runners`.
- Its Move then continues with the half-points it has left: another step
  (onto land, or onto ice in a new direction, which starts a new slide) or
  nothing. Entering ice costs the ordinary step cost (half from a usable
  Road node; no Glide discount, since ice is never Snow); a step that
  leaves an ice tile costs a full point; slid tiles cost nothing.
- **The slide is forced:** a `MOVE` path must follow every slide to its
  end; a path that stops or turns where a slide continues is rejected with
  `MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL { reason: "SLIDE_FORCED" }`, and the movement query
  offers only the tiles a Move can really end on.
- Slid tiles are part of the path: they reveal sight and count toward the
  Charge path length and a Wreck salvage at the end of the Move. A slide
  that meets a ZOC first seen during the Move stops there and the Move is
  interrupted (`ZOC`), as for any Move. A sliding unit never passes a unit
  on ice, its owner's included.
- The **Sabretooth** never slides: on ice it walks at the ordinary cost,
  and, being of the Ice Folk kind, it does not slip.

**Slip.** For a land-form unit of every other kind in movement mode
`GROUND`, **a Move ends on entering an ice tile** (`terrainStopsMoveV7`; a
path that continues past it is rejected with
`MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL { reason: "ICE_STOPS_MOVE" }`). No Road edge and no
Fieldcraft waives it. Martian walkers and flyers and the Dwarf Gyrocopter
are never stopped by terrain and cross ice like land. Leaving an ice tile
costs a full point, so any army may use an Ice Folk bridge, one tile per
turn. A slipping unit that steps onto ice on a tile it had not explored
before the command stops there, and its Move is interrupted with reason
`ICE`, as for Snow.

**Black Ice** (the redesign, `7r100`). With the capability `blackIce` (the
Ice Folk Seamanship), a land-form unit hostile to the seat that **ends its
own `MOVE`, a `DISEMBARK` landing, or a `BEAM_DOWN` on that seat's ice,
having started off that seat's ice**, is Frozen at once
([section 21.2](#212-frozen)): frozen during its owner's own turn, so it
gets `turnsLeft` 2 (Shatter-eligible on the next Ice Folk turn, Frozen
through its owner's next turn, thawed after it). One `UNITS_FROZEN`
(source `BLACK_ICE`, `sourceUnitId` null) right after the command's events
(before a Frost Giant's Cold Aura). A unit already on the seat's ice that
walks along it, a unit pushed, pulled, or knocked onto it, a unit that
advances onto it after an attack, and a unit standing on ice the seat
newly takes are not frozen, and **nothing happens at the Start Turn** (the
old step is deleted). So stepping onto the ice costs a unit about two
turns and a Shatter risk, and it is never trapped: once thawed it may
attack from the ice, walk on, or crack the ice in front of it. Black Ice
is read from the ice owner's own faction and research, so the ice of a
Martian controller never freezes units.

**Icebound and the crush.** An afloat unit (`NAVAL` or `EMBARKED`) standing
on an ice tile is **icebound** (`unitIsIceboundV7`), derived, never stored:
the only way an afloat unit is on ice is a Freeze of its tile with the
capability `icebound`.

- **Frozen solid.** An icebound unit cannot `MOVE`
  (`MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`), `ATTACK`
  (`ATTACK_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`), `BOARD`
  (`BOARD_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`), or `CRACK_ICE`
  (`CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ICEBOUND" }`), none of them offered,
  and it never retaliates (`noRetaliationReason: "ICEBOUND"`). It projects
  no ZOC and threatens no tile. An icebound embarked unit may still
  `DISEMBARK` (the crew climbs out, onto land or onto ice). It may Recover
  (a ship next to its own active dock), Wait, and Promote. No ram's shove,
  Push, Charge! push, Knockback, or Tractor Beam moves it, and an attack on
  it is never a Ram. An icebound Submarine is not submerged. It may be
  attacked, torpedoed, and boarded like any ship; a boarded prize stays
  icebound.
- **The crush.** At the Start Turn of the ice tile's owner, every icebound
  unit on that player's ice, whoever owns the unit, takes
  `ICE_CRUSH_DAMAGE_V7` **3**, in unit-ID order: fixed damage, not an
  attack; a Shield absorbs first; never reduced by Armoured; capped at its
  HP. Event `UNITS_CRUSHED { playerId, results }`; a death has cause
  `CRUSHED`, credits no unit, leaves no Grave, releases the controlled unit
  of a crushed Brain, never explodes a ship in `NAVAL` form, and an
  embarked exploding Goblin unit explodes on its tile.
- **Release** is only by Crack Ice (an own or allied unit or ship next to
  it cracks its tile; thick ice twice) or by the elimination of the
  freezing seat. An icebound ship cannot crack its own way out.
- A hostile dock never freezes, so a ship is icebound on a dock only on an
  own dock frozen over by its Ice Folk owner, where it blockades nothing.

**Glacier.** The capability `thickIce` (`7r100`; `iceTurns` before): the
seat's ice takes two Cracks to break, and a Freeze of the seat mends a
crack. And `iceCover`: a land-form unit of the Ice Folk kind on ice whose
own fortification level is 0 has the Snow cover, **× 1.25**
(`SNOW_COVER_V7`; the preview's `iceCover`, and the public `iceCover`
stat). **+1 Move on ice**: a `MOVE` of a land-form unit of the Ice Folk kind
whose capabilities have `iceCover` gets `GLACIER_ICE_MOVE_BONUS_V7` (1)
Move more when its path includes an ice tile. Glacier also grants Harbours
([section 14.4](#144-harbours)).

**Building on ice and the Ice Harbour.** An Ice Folk seat builds on its own
ice in its territory: the Ice Harbour (its Port; the Great Harbour its
Shipyard), the Fishing Hole, the Windmill, Sawmill, Forge, Workshop,
Market, and Monument ([sections 8.1 to 8.3](#81-common-placement-gates);
[section 14](#14-naval-rules)). An Ice Harbour built on open Shallow Water
freezes its tile first. A dock on ice is blockaded by a hostile land-form
unit standing on it and never by a ship; nothing trains, embarks, or
recovers on it. Built ice cannot be cracked; an enemy that wants a
building on ice gone stands on it and **Pillages** it (Raiding, as on
land), and the ice under it is then plain ice. A captured city's buildings
on ice keep working for the captor, and its ice becomes the captor's; the
captor builds no new ones on ice.

**No ships, no embarking.**

- The Ice Folk tree unlocks no naval role: `TRAIN_NAVAL` is never offered
  to an Ice Folk seat and is rejected with `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`.
- **A unit of the Ice Folk kind never embarks** (a body rule): a Move never
  ends embarked for it; it walks onto its own docks, which are ice.
- **Sea Dog** for an Ice Folk seat counts its land-form units standing on
  ice instead of its ships: 5 at once (`ICE_SEA_DOG_UNITS_V7`).
- **The Sunken Wreck:** on an ice tile, the first land-form unit that ends
  a `MOVE` on it salvages it; on cracked-open water it is a water Wreck
  again ([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)).

**The themed ships meet the ice** by the rules above, with no special
case: every ship may Crack Ice next to it, is icebound by an Icebound
Freeze, and takes the crush; a Plesiosaur and a Kraken are frozen at the
surface like any Submarine (an icebound Kraken does not Drag); Martian
Shields absorb the crush first and a Hover Pod never launches onto ice;
Dwarf Armoured does not reduce the crush and Sea Tunnels never pass under
ice; an icebound Fire Raft cannot Kaboom and an icebound Candy ship cannot
Rush (a crushed Dreadnought does not explode); Drowned Crews never raise a
ship on ice; a submerged Submarine may crack (cracking is no attack and
does not surface it).

**Why ice cannot wall off a sea.** Every unit of every other faction next
to the ice, and every ship, can open it, one tile per action (thick: two);
hostile docks never freeze, and a ship on a dock surrounded by ice cracks
its way out; ice is walkable by everyone (one tile per turn), and a
transport may land on its edge; Black Ice freezes once and never traps; an
icebound ship's owner can free it with any unit beside it. There is
deliberately no uncrackable ice, Ice Folk home waters included (the root's
decision on the redesign's open question): the counter is tempo and
technology (Freeze outpaces Crack; a unit on a tile or a building holds
it; Glacier's thick ice), not immunity.

**Interactions.**

| Rule                   | Interaction                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Graves, risings        | No death afloat or on ice leaves a Grave or rises, and Raise Dead never reaches the sea. A shattered unit on ice leaves nothing, as everywhere.                                                                                                                          |
| Plague, Bitten, Wail   | Unchanged on ships and on ice. A Black Ice freeze and a bite coexist.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Kaboom, blasts, bombs  | Hit ships, Submarines, icebound ships, and units on ice like any unit. A blast never cracks or makes ice (cracking is an action).                                                                                                                                        |
| Dinosaurs              | A Triceratops may Charge! onto ice (it slips there); its push moves a land-form target onto ice and never triggers Black Ice. Eggs are never on ice.                                                                                                                     |
| Martians               | Flyers and walkers cross ice like land; a machine that ends a Move on ice stands. Shields absorb the crush. A controlled Ice Folk unit slides and Freezes for its controller (its ice is the controller's: crush yes, Black Ice and building on it no) and never cracks. |
| Dwarves                | Tunnels never run under ice and a mound is never on ice; a burrowed unit cannot crack; a bomb run may land on ice; eruptions hit land-form units on ice.                                                                                                                 |
| Candy                  | A Candy unit that dies on ice leaves no Crumbs, and nothing is Re-baked onto ice. A Crashed unit cannot crack.                                                                                                                                                           |
| Push, Knockback, pulls | A land-form unit may be pushed, knocked back, or pulled onto ice; an afloat unit never; an icebound unit never moves; none of it triggers Black Ice.                                                                                                                     |
| Embarking, landing     | A transport may land on adjacent ice (Black Ice freezes the crew). A unit of the Ice Folk kind never embarks; nothing embarks at a dock on ice.                                                                                                                          |
| Blockade, sea links    | Hostile docks never freeze; a dock on ice is blockaded by land units only; sea links run under ice.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Capture, elimination   | The former owner's ice in the captured city's territory passes to the captor, uncracked (an Ice Folk captor with Rime then freezes that territory: the border freeze); an eliminated seat's ice stays, its icebound ships float free, and its cracks are gone.           |
| Land Grant             | Claims ice tiles as it claims water; with Rime an Ice Folk grant then freezes the city's whole territory (the border freeze: another seat's ice there is taken), otherwise their owner does not change.                                                                  |
| Map generation         | Unchanged; faction choice never affects any draw.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

**Worked examples** (full HP unless stated):

| Situation                                                                             | Result                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A Yeti on the shore freezes toward an island 4 Shallow tiles away                     | turn 1: tiles 1 and 2; turn 2: it steps on, slides to 2, freezes 3 and 4; turn 3: it slides to 4. The bridge stays for the rest of the match; nobody refreezes  |
| A Human Swordsman on the island shore cracks tile 4 (no Glacier)                      | tile 4 is water again; next Ice Folk turn a Yeti on tile 3 freezes 4 (and 5 if it is water)                                                                     |
| The same with Glacier                                                                 | tile 4 is cracked; the Ice Folk mend it with any Freeze over it before the second Crack                                                                         |
| A Patrol Boat is icebound; an allied Patrol Boat is next to it                        | the ally cracks its tile; the freed boat sails and attacks on the same turn                                                                                     |
| A Knight lands on Ice Folk ice from a transport (Black Ice)                           | Frozen at once; on the Ice Folk turn two hits Shatter it; if it lives, it thaws after its next turn and may then ride off, attack, or crack                     |
| An Ice Folk coastal city with five shallow tiles in its footprint, Rime, Milling      | the Witch freezes them in one action; three Fishing Holes (9 Coins, +3) and a Windmill on the ice beside them and one Frost Garden (5 Coins, +4): +7 population |
| A Sled on a long ice sheet, a Human Guard's zone of control between it and a Marksman | it slides through the zone (Runners) to the tile beside the Marksman and attacks with Charge                                                                    |
| The Ice Folk capture a Human port city                                                | its Port is theirs; any Freeze over it puts ice under it, making it an Ice Harbour their units can walk on                                                      |

**Commands, events, errors, and queries.**

- **Commands:** `FREEZE { kind, unitId, at }` right after `COLD_SNAP`,
  `CRACK_ICE { kind, unitId, at }` right after `FREEZE`, and
  `BUILD_FISHING_HOLE { kind, at }` right after `BUILD_LUMBER_CAMP` in
  `COMMAND_KIND_ORDER_V7`. `MOVE` validates slides, Runners, and slips. A
  pending city reward blocks them like every command.
- **Events:** `WATER_FROZEN`, `ICE_CRACKED`, `ICE_MELTED` (the
  elimination release only), and `UNITS_CRUSHED`, in that order right
  after `UNITS_FROZEN` in `DOMAIN_EVENT_KIND_ORDER_V7`; `PORT_BUILT` has
  `iceMade`; `ECONOMIC_BUILDING_BUILT` covers the Fishing Hole;
  `UNIT_DIED.cause` has `CRUSHED`; `UNITS_FROZEN.source` `BLACK_ICE` fires
  inside a Move, a landing, or a Beam Down; `UNIT_MOVE_INTERRUPTED.reason`
  has `ICE`. Projection: [section 15](#15-fog-and-observation).
- **Errors:** `FREEZE_NOT_LEGAL` (`OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NO_TARGET`);
  `CRACK_ICE_NOT_LEGAL` (`ICEBOUND`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NO_ICE`, `OCCUPIED`,
  `BUILT`); `MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL` reasons `SLIDE_FORCED`, `ICE_STOPS_MOVE`, and
  `ICEBOUND`; `ATTACK_NOT_LEGAL` and `BOARD_NOT_LEGAL` reason `ICEBOUND`.
- **Registration:** ability `FREEZE` on every Ice Folk land role; Crack Ice
  is a kind rule (`unitCracksIceV7`: every unit not of the Ice Folk kind in
  land, naval, or embarked form) rather than a role-table ability; role
  mechanic `runners` (the Ice Folk Sled); improvement `FISHING_HOLE`
  (appended to `IMPROVEMENT_IDS_V7`); unlock kinds `FREEZE { depth }`,
  `ICEBOUND`, `BLACK_ICE`, and `GLACIER` (no field), and the Ice Folk Rime's
  `COMMAND BUILD_FISHING_HOLE`; capabilities `freezeWater`, `icebound`,
  `blackIce`, `thickIce`, and `iceCover`; constants `ICE_CRACKS_THICK_V7` 2,
  `FISHING_HOLE_COST_V7` 3, `FISHING_HOLE_POPULATION_V7` 1,
  `FREEZE_LINE_V7` 2, `WITCH_FREEZE_RADIUS_V7` 1, `ICE_CRUSH_DAMAGE_V7` 3,
  `GLACIER_ICE_MOVE_BONUS_V7` 1, and `ICE_SEA_DOG_UNITS_V7` 5
  (`ICE_TURNS_V7` and `GLACIER_ICE_TURNS_V7` are gone).
- **Helpers:** `isIceAtV7` and `iceAtV7` read through an index of the
  immutable list (`iceEntryIndexV7`), `unitIsIceboundV7`, `unitSlidesV7`,
  `unitHasRunnersV7`, `unitCracksIceV7`, `iceIsThickV7`, `iceBuildableV7`,
  `freezeSetV7`, `crackIceResultV7`, `resolveBlackIceOnEntryV7`, and
  `releaseEliminatedIceV7` (`resolveThawV7`, `resolveBlackIceV7`, and
  `iceIsPermanentV7` are gone).
- **`queryPlayerCommandsV7`** offers `FREEZE` for every `at` that changes
  something, `CRACK_ICE` for every legal `at`, every build on own ice
  (`BUILD_FISHING_HOLE` among them), and `MOVE` endpoints after slides and
  Runners; `queryThreatenedTilesV7` follows them. Every offered command is
  accepted, and every preview equals the resolution.
- **Public unit stats:** `icebound` (on every unit, exactly in a match with
  an Ice Folk seat) and, in the `iceFolk` block, `onIce`, `slides`,
  `runners`, and `iceCover`.
- **Normal AI, presentation, and balance:** the Normal AI's rules for and
  against permanent ice are bead `pulp_wars-5ti.26`
  ([section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)), and the interface, art, and sound (the Crack Ice
  button, the snow pad under buildings on ice, the Fishing Hole and Ice
  Harbour sprites) bead `pulp_wars-5ti.27`
  ([section 25](#25-known-discrepancies)). The interface already shows ice
  without a countdown, thick and cracked ice, and the new Freeze labels;
  the frozen sea has not been balance-checked.

### 21.17 The Musk Ox: Frostbite

`pulp-wars-poc-7r55` (`pulp_wars-w49.17`). The **Mammoth is the Ice Folk
heavy line unit** (role `SWORDSMAN`, tactical label `LINE`, Metallurgy):
every number and rule it had as the `GUARD` role is unchanged (20 HP,
Attack 2.5, Defense 2, Move 1, Sweep, Trample, captures, Glides) except its
cost, 7 Coins since `pulp_wars-w49.37` (6 before), and its Stampede
([section 21.18](#2118-the-mammoths-stampede)). Where sections 21.1 to 21.16
call the Mammoth the `GUARD` role or a `DEFENDER`, read the `SWORDSMAN`
role.

The **Musk Ox** is the defender it left (role `GUARD`, `DEFENDER`; at
Fortification, shown as Deep Winter, since `7r56`; at Drill before): 4
Coins, 16 HP, Attack 1.5, Defense 2 (2.5 before `pulp_wars-w49.37`), Move 1,
melee, no attack after moving, captures, Glides, Freezes water with Rime,
builds no Field Defense. Its numbers are first guesses.

- **Frostbite** (`frostbite`). A land-form unit that attacks a land-form
  Musk Ox from the next tile and survives the exchange is Frozen
  ([section 21.2](#212-frozen)), whether or not the Ox survives. It is
  frozen during its own turn, so `turnsLeft` is 2: it stays Frozen for the
  rest of that turn and through its next one. The event is `UNITS_FROZEN`
  with the source `FROSTBITE`, and the preview says `frostbiteApplied`.
- A ranged attacker is not Frozen, nor is an embarked one, nor the
  Monster.
- An attack that Frostbite applies to grants no Escape. The Frozen attacker
  is a Shatter target for the Ice Folk ([section 21.4](#214-shatter)).

### 21.18 The Mammoth's Stampede

Ice Folk Freeze (`pulp_wars-w49.37`). `STAMPEDE { kind, unitId, at }` is a
primary action of the Mammoth (ability `STAMPEDE`; the revision-19
Dinosaur command of that name was removed in revision 20, and the name now
belongs to the Mammoth). It is not an Attack and costs no Coins.

**Legality**, in this order (all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                     | Rejection                                    |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board, not Frozen.                                                                                                                                      | the ordinary unit errors; `UNIT_FROZEN`      |
| 2   | Its role has `STAMPEDE`.                                                                                                                                                                        | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                 |
| 3   | It is in land form.                                                                                                                                                                             | `STAMPEDE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`  |
| 4   | It has not used a primary action (Attack, Recover, Capture, a special action) and has no pending continuation.                                                                                  | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                         |
| 5   | It has not moved this turn.                                                                                                                                                                     | `STAMPEDE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "MOVED" }`     |
| 6   | `at` is 1 to `STAMPEDE_RANGE_V7` (3) tiles away in one straight line, orthogonal or diagonal.                                                                                                   | `STAMPEDE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "DIRECTION" }` |
| 7   | Every tile of the line is on the board and explored by the actor, no settlement center, with no chest, mound, Barricade, or visible unit that is not hostile, and ground the Mammoth can enter. | `STAMPEDE_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "BLOCKED" }`   |

**Resolution.** The Mammoth charges along the line, tile by tile:

- A tile with a mound, a Barricade, or a chest stops it before that tile
  (rule 7 already refuses those the actor knows of).
- A unit on the tile that is not hostile stops it before the tile (own and
  allied units are always visible, so rule 7 already refuses such a line).
- A **hostile unit** on the tile takes `STAMPEDE_DAMAGE_V7` **3** fixed
  damage (not an attack: no cover, Defense, or HP ratio; Armoured reduces
  it and a Shield absorbs it first, as for the giants' fixed hits). A unit
  the hit kills is removed and the Mammoth goes on through its tile (a
  Bitten victim rises on its tile, and the Mammoth stops before it). A
  survivor is **shoved** to the first of the two side tiles of its tile,
  clockwise of the charge first (for a charge east, south first), that the
  Push rule allows ([section 13](#13-combat-and-fortification)), the actor
  has explored, and holds no chest; the Mammoth goes on. With no such tile the survivor stays, and the Mammoth stops before it (it
  still took the hit). A neutral unit (a Spider, a camp guard, Bigfoot) is
  hostile, so it takes the hit, but it is never shoved, and the hit provokes
  it ([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)).
- The Mammoth ends on the last tile it entered (its own tile when the first
  tile stops it).

Then the Mammoth has moved and used its primary action, and is handled; it
captures nothing this turn. There is **no retaliation**, Sweep and Trample
do not apply, and no unit shatters. Kills are credited to the Mammoth
(`UNIT_DIED` cause `STAMPEDE`, with the ordinary Grave or rising and death
blast). It destroys enemy Field
Defense on its end tile as any Move ending there would, and reveals from
its end tile. Event `MAMMOTH_STAMPEDED { playerId, unitId, from, to, path,
results: [{ unitId, at, damage, shieldDamage, dies, shovedTo }] }` (`path`
the tiles entered; `shovedTo` null for a dead or unshoved unit), followed
by the death and reveal events.

**Query and preview.** `queryPlayerCommandsV7` offers `STAMPEDE` for every
`at` that passes rules 1 to 7 from the viewer's knowledge, so every offered
command is accepted. **`previewStampedeV7(view, unitId, at)`** returns null
unless that command is offered, otherwise
`{ unitId, at, path, hits }`: the line's tiles and the fixed hit on each
visible hostile unit on them (as `splash` entries), assuming nothing stops
the charge; the result may differ when a hit unit cannot be shoved or a
hidden unit stands in the way.

## 22. Dwarf faction rules

Humans are sustain, Undead are attrition, Goblins are a reckless horde,
Dinosaurs are few, big, and growing, Martians are a small high-tech
invasion force, the Ice Folk are the things from the peaks, and the
Steampunk Dwarves are **heavy, slow, and built to last; they come from above
and below**: Hammerers hold their cities dug in, Gyrocopters fly over the
enemy line and drop a bomb on whoever stands behind it, Steam Moles drill
under the line carrying a Hammerer and burst out of the ground next to the
back line, Engineers wind up clockwork Gunners at the front and keep the
machines patched, and a clockwork Brass Titan hits as hard at the end of a
fight as at the start. They are strong at home, against a soft back line,
and wherever a visible two-turn blow lands; they are slow to expand, weak
against Shields and units that step away from a mound, exposed on the turn
after every surfacing, and they lose their clockwork for good if the
Engineers die. Every rule in this section applies only to units of a
`DWARF` seat, except where a rule names its target (an eruption and a bomb
hit other players' units, and a mound reserves its tile for everyone); in a
match without one the lists `burrowed`, `surfacedThisTurn`,
`bombedThisTurn`, and `barricades` are empty, no tile holds a mound or a
Barricade, no `TUNNEL`, `BOMB_RUN`, `ASSEMBLE`, `WHIRL`, `BUILD_BARRICADE`,
or `ATTACK_BARRICADE` is offered or accepted, every role has `construct` false, the
per-unit living test returns what the per-owner test returned, the two
per-unit stat flags and the `dwarf` stat block are absent, and the three
Dwarf combat-preview fields are false. Each rule resolves through the
owner's registration (`FACTION_RULES_V7`, `DWARF_ROLE_RULES_V7`,
`DWARF_ROLE_MECHANICS_V7`) and the helpers of `src/engine/v7/dwarf.ts`,
`src/engine/v7/dwarf-reducer.ts`, and `src/engine/v7/units.ts`. Human,
Undead, Goblin, Dinosaur, Martian, Ice Folk, and Candy units keep every
ability against the Dwarves, with the rulings of
[section 22.13](#2213-interactions-with-other-rules) (the Candy rulings are
in [section 23.9](#239-interactions-with-other-rules)). Specification,
per-unit battle analysis, decisions, root rulings, and the tuning record:
the [Dwarf overlay](RULESET_7_DWARVES.md) and the
[Dwarf balance report](../validation/RULESET_7_DWARF_BALANCE.md) (the `7r31`
coarse pass on Dry Land).

### 22.1 Roles, constructs, machines, and labels

| Mechanical role | Dwarf unit       | Kind                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FIGHTER`       | Hammerer         | rides the tunnel; Dig In                                        |
| `RAIDER`        | Gyrocopter       | machine; flies; Bomb Run; no `ATTACK`                           |
| `MARKSMAN`      | Clockwork Gunner | construct; machine; two shots standing still                    |
| `GUARD`         | Steam Mole       | machine; Tunnel and eruption; Dig In                            |
| `CAPTAIN`       | Engineer         | Repair; Assemble; Barricade (`w49.33`); no Rally                |
| `CATAPULT`      | Steam Cannon     | machine; Knockback; with Blasting Charges ignores fortification |
| `KNIGHT`        | Whirligig        | construct; machine; Whirl (`w49.33`; Three Hammers at `7r55`)   |
| `SWORDSMAN`     | Steam Tank       | machine; Plated 4; no Overrun (`KNIGHT` before `7r55`)          |
| `JUGGERNAUT`    | Brass Titan      | construct; machine; Push                                        |

- **Dwarf units** are the eight land roles in land form. The Dwarf rules
  never apply to a Dwarf boat (the Human Patrol Boat, Battleship, and
  Submarine) or to
  an embarked unit, except where a rule says so.
- **Constructs** (role mechanic `construct`) are the Clockwork Gunner and
  the Brass Titan: fully mechanical, no dwarf inside
  ([section 22.6](#226-clockwork)). Every other Dwarf unit is living.
  **Living** is read per unit (`isLivingUnitV7`): the owner's faction is not
  `UNDEAD` **and** the role is not a construct under the owner's
  registration. Plague, Bitten, Infect, Wail, and their previews read it;
  in a match without a Dwarf seat it equals the per-owner test.
- **Machines** (role mechanic `repairsAsMachine`, for Repair only,
  [section 22.8](#228-engineer-repair-and-assemble)) are every Dwarf land
  role but the Hammerer and the Engineer. This is not the Martian meaning
  of "machine" ([section 20.1](#201-roles-machines-and-labels)), which is a
  movement mode: of the Dwarf units only the Gyrocopter has a non-ground
  movement mode (`FLY`), and only it gets the flyer rules (no cover or
  fortification, no Port needed, self-launch on water).
- **Diggers** (role mechanic `digsIn`) are the Hammerer and the Steam Mole
  ([section 22.7](#227-dig-in)).
- Tactical labels are those of the same mechanical role (the registry
  requires it): the Gyrocopter is `SKIRMISHER`, the Clockwork Gunner
  `RANGED`, the Steam Mole `DEFENDER`, the Engineer `SUPPORT`, and the
  Steam Cannon `SIEGE`. The Normal AI judges them by their abilities, not
  by these labels.

### 22.2 The Tunnel and burrowed units

`TUNNEL { kind, unitId, to, rider }` is the Steam Mole's Move, made
underground; `rider` is `null` or `{ unitId, to }`. It is not an Attack and
costs no Coins.

A **tunnel tile for a unit `u`** is a tile on the board, explored by the
actor, land and not a Rift (Grass, Forest, or Mountain), enterable by `u`
under `canEnterTerrainV7` (a Mountain needs its owner's Engineering), with
no unit of any owner, no mound, and no treasure chest, that is not a
settlement site (a village, city, or capital center of any owner) and not
in territory allied to the actor (a cooperative partner's; own territory is
allowed).

Legality, in this order (all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Rejection                                                        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | the ordinary unit errors; a burrowed unit `UNIT_ALREADY_HANDLED` |
| 2   | Its role has `TUNNEL`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                                     |
| 3   | It has not moved, has not used a primary action, and has not landed this turn.                                                                                                                                                                                     | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                                             |
| 4   | It is in land form.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `TUNNEL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`                        |
| 5   | It is not in `surfacedThisTurn`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `TUNNEL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "SURFACED" }`                        |
| 6   | `to` is a tunnel tile for the Mole, and a sequence of at most `TUNNEL_RANGE_V7` (3) steps between Chebyshev neighbours leads from the Mole's tile to `to` with every tile after the first explored by the actor and land (Grass, Forest, Mountain, or Rift).       | `TUNNEL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "DESTINATION" }`                     |
| 7   | If `rider` is not null: `rider.unitId` is another own unit on the board whose role has `RIDES_TUNNEL` (a Hammerer), in land form, Chebyshev-adjacent to the Mole, that has not moved, used a primary action, or landed this turn and is not in `surfacedThisTurn`. | `TUNNEL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "RIDER" }`                           |
| 8   | If `rider` is not null: `rider.to` is a tunnel tile for the Hammerer, Chebyshev-adjacent to `to`, and not `to`.                                                                                                                                                    | `TUNNEL_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "RIDER_DESTINATION" }`               |

- **Sea Tunnels** (`7r96`, `pulp_wars-5ti.20`): for a Mole whose kind's
  capabilities under its controller have `seaTunnels` (the Dwarf
  Seamanship), the tiles of row 6's sequence after the first and before
  `to` may also be explored Shallow Water that is not ice
  (`seaTunnelPassableV7`); `to` and the rider's tile stay tunnel tiles
  (land), and Deep Water and ice are never passed. The range is unchanged,
  so a strait of one or two Shallow tiles is crossed.
- **Underground** units, zones of control, terrain stops, Snow, Roads, and
  territory do not matter along the way; each step costs one; passing under
  a Mountain needs no Engineering and passing under a Rift is allowed; water
  is never part of a tunnel (but Shallow Water with Sea Tunnels); nothing is revealed along the way. The command
  carries no path, so the command query offers one entry per destination
  and rider tile (and the rider-less entry).
- **A Frozen Mole cannot tunnel**, and a Frozen Hammerer cannot ride
  (`UNIT_FROZEN`, [section 21.3](#213-what-a-frozen-unit-cannot-do)).
- **Result.** The Mole leaves `units` and enters `burrowed` as
  `{ unit: { …mole, at: to }, moleUnitId: null }`; the rider, if any,
  enters as `{ unit: { …hammerer, at: rider.to }, moleUnitId: mole.id }`.
  Both records keep their HP, kills, home city, and every status entry
  (Plague, Bitten, Frozen) and get the exhausted activation and
  `captureEligible` false. The actor explores every tile within 1 of each
  mound. Nothing else changes on the board: Field Defense on a mound tile
  stays until the surfacing, and a siege the Mole or the rider was making
  ends because nobody stands on that center any more. Events:
  `UNIT_TUNNELLED` (the rider fields null without a rider), then
  `TILES_REVEALED`, then the ordinary economy, reward, and achievement tail.
  A tunnel never touches water, so `TUNNEL` is not on the blockade-event
  list. Every tile it reads is explored, so the command is exact.
- **State.** `GameStateV7.burrowed` is
  `readonly { unit: UnitStateV7, moleUnitId: UnitId | null }[]`, sorted by
  `unit.id`; `unit.at` is the **mound tile**. A Mole entry has `moleUnitId`
  null; a rider entry names a burrowed Mole of the same owner next to it.
  Entries exist only between a `TUNNEL` and the owner's next Start Turn.
  State parsing rejects a duplicate or unsorted entry, a unit ID that is
  also in `units`, an owner that is not a Dwarf seat, a Mole entry whose role
  lacks `TUNNEL` or whose `moleUnitId` is not null, a rider entry whose role
  lacks `RIDES_TUNNEL`, whose `moleUnitId` is not a burrowed Mole of the
  same owner, or whose tile is not next to that Mole's, two riders for one
  Mole, a form other than `LAND`, a mound tile that is off the board, water,
  a Rift, or a settlement site, that holds a unit or a chest, or that
  another entry shares, and any entry in a match without a Dwarf seat. Unit
  IDs are unique across `units` and `burrowed`, and the next entity ID is
  above all of them.
- **The two accessors.** `state.units` keeps its meaning (the board), and
  every reader of a unit list chooses between `boardUnitsV7` (what stands on
  the board) and `allOwnedUnitsV7` (the board plus the burrowed records): a
  checked-in classification of every reader, enforced by a test, fails when
  a reader appears without a class. Combat, targeting, adjacency abilities,
  splash, Pierce, Wail, blasts, Plague spread, movement, ZOC, siege,
  training spawn, capture, the activation reset and every other Start Turn
  step, idle recovery, Muster, the player view's `units`, the command
  query, and selection are board-only. Capacity and used slots, orphaning
  on a capture, the treasure unit's slot check, elimination, the status
  lists and the Frozen countdown, the leaderboard and headless metrics, and
  state parsing, hashing, saves, replays, and entity-ID uniqueness read all
  owned units. Victory and defeat still read cities only, so a seat with
  only burrowed units and a city is alive.

### 22.3 The mound, surfacing, and the eruption

- **Visible.** Each burrowed unit is a **mound** on its tile, public to
  every viewer who has explored that tile: owner, unit, HP, statuses, and
  whether it is the Mole or its rider
  ([section 15](#15-fog-and-observation)). The mound announces the exact
  tile and turn of the eruption.
- **Untouchable.** A burrowed unit is not in `units`, so no attack, bomb,
  splash, Pierce, Sweep, Kaboom or death blast, Wail, Plague spread, Bolas,
  Cold Snap, Cold Aura, Mind Control, Tractor Beam, Push, Charge! push,
  Knockback, or Overrun finds it. It exerts no ZOC, never besieges, and
  never blocks training, capture, or Land Grant. Every command naming it is
  rejected with `UNIT_ALREADY_HANDLED` and never offered.
- **Reserved.** The one occupancy predicate `tileOccupiedV7(state | view,
at)` is true when a unit stands on the tile **or a mound is on it** (or,
  since `pulp_wars-w49.33`, a Barricade stands there,
  [section 22.8](#228-engineer-repair-and-assemble)), and
  every rule that places a unit or ends a unit's step asks it
  ([section 12.1](#121-movement)). A Move may pass over a mound tile. A
  mound on a tile the mover has not explored can be met only on the last
  tile of a Move; the Move is accepted and interrupted there
  (`UNIT_MOVE_INTERRUPTED` reason `MOUND`, naming the mound tile), the
  mover staying on the last tile it entered on which it may end.
- **The tile** keeps its terrain, Road, improvement, resource, Field Defense,
  Grave, and Snow; tile actions on it are unaffected, and none changes a
  tile into water, a Rift, or a site. So a mound tile is never occupied when
  it surfaces (the surfacing asserts it).

**Surfacing.** At its owner's **Start Turn**, after the activation reset,
the city actions, the Mind Control cooldowns, the Shield recharge, and the
Cold Aura (which never runs in the same Start Turn: a seat has one faction)
and before Plague, each burrowed Mole of that seat surfaces, in unit-ID
order:

1. **Return.** The Mole, then its rider, leave `burrowed` and enter `units`
   on their mound tiles with the Start Turn activation (nothing moved or
   used) and `captureEligible` false; both join `surfacedThisTurn`.
2. **Eruption.** Every unit on the eight tiles around the Mole that is
   hostile to the Mole's owner and **on the ground** takes the owner's
   `eruptionDamage`: **2** (`ERUPTION_DAMAGE_V7`), **3** with Blasting
   Charges (`BLASTING_ERUPTION_DAMAGE_V7`). On the ground means a land-form
   unit whose movement mode is not `FLY` (foot units, walkers) or
   an Egg; never a flyer, a naval unit, or an embarked unit. The damage is
   fixed: no retaliation, Attack, Defense, cover, fortification, Walls,
   Snow, or Blizzard; Armoured takes 1 off, then Plated caps it, then a
   Shield absorbs first; it is capped at the victim's HP. Every victim is
   hit at once. The rider never erupts, and own and allied units are never
   hit.
3. **Undermining.** Field Defense on the Mole's tile and on the eight tiles
   around it is destroyed, whoever owns it and whether or not anything was
   hit (`FIELD_DEFENSE_DESTROYED` reason `UNDERMINED`).
4. **Deaths,** in `(y, x, id)` order: cause `ERUPTION`, kill credit to the
   Mole (Promotion and Slayer count it, a destroyed Egg too), then each
   death's Grave or Bitten rising under the ordinary rules (none on a Rift,
   none for a construct), and a dead Brain's controlled unit is released.
5. **Death blasts.** Exploding victims explode as a chain
   ([section 18.7](#187-where-chains-run-and-event-order)); the blasts hit
   everyone in their areas, the surfaced Mole and rider included, and a
   Goblin seat earns Plunder for its blasts' kills.
6. **Reveals.** Each surfaced unit (and rising) reveals its sight.

Events, one block per Mole, after `SHIELDS_RECHARGED` and before
`PLAGUE_DAMAGED`: `UNIT_SURFACED` (its `results`
in `(y, x, id)` order, `damage` being HP damage), `FIELD_DEFENSE_DESTROYED`
(`UNDERMINED`) per tile in `(y, x)` order, `UNIT_DIED` (cause `ERUPTION`)
with `GRAVE_CREATED`, `BITTEN_UNIT_RISEN`, and `BRAIN_LOST` collapses as
they apply, the chain events, `PLUNDER_AWARDED`, and `TILES_REVEALED`; then
the economy changes of the surfacing.

**On the surfacing turn** the Mole and the rider may Move overland and
attack as usual, but neither can capture (`captureEligible` false: they
began the turn underground), the Mole cannot tunnel
(`TUNNEL_NOT_LEGAL` reason `SURFACED`), and the rider is braked
([section 22.4](#224-the-rider)). `surfacedThisTurn` is emptied at its
owner's End Turn, and an entry leaves it when its unit leaves the board.
If the owner is eliminated, its burrowed units are removed with the rest of
its units (`UNIT_DIED` cause `ELIMINATION`, no Grave, no blast).

### 22.4 The rider

- The rider uses its own slot and keeps its home city; a capture of that
  city orphans it while it is underground, like any unit.
- It travels with the Mole: it needs no path of its own and ignores
  Mountains, Forests, units, and ZOC on the way; its destination must be a
  tile it could stand on (a Mountain needs Engineering). With no free rider
  tile next to the destination, the Mole tunnels alone.
- It surfaces right after its Mole, never erupts, and is in the blast of an
  exploding unit the eruption killed.
- **The rider brake** (root ruling 1). On its surfacing turn it never ends a
  Move, or advances, on a settlement center its owner does not own (a
  neutral village, or a center of a city its owner does not own):
  `MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL` reason `SETTLEMENT_FORBIDDEN`, never offered. Its own
  centers are allowed, and the Mole is not braked. It cannot ride again
  that turn. Abroad it is never dug in; at home it is dug in if it then
  stands still within 1 of an own center.
- A ride moves a Hammerer up to 5 tiles in one turn (one to the Mole, three
  under, one beside the destination); with the brake, a rider captures a
  village at the Raider's pace from 5 or 6 tiles out and a turn earlier from
  7 (the [Dwarf overlay's](RULESET_7_DWARVES.md#55-the-rider) village race).

### 22.5 Gyrocopters and the bombing run

- **Flight.** The Gyrocopter has the Martian `FLY` movement mode, unchanged
