(no event), so a status lasts until the end of the victim's next turn that
begins after the hit. A new application keeps the larger `endsLeft`.
Entries belong to units: they survive Mind Control and release and are
removed when the unit leaves the board (a Swallow included). Both are
public on visible units (the view's `stuck` and `toothache` and the unit
stats' `stuck` and `toothache` flags). Only a Top-Up cures them.

- **Stuck**: the unit's `MOVE` (an Escape Move included) has at most
  `STUCK_MAX_STEPS_V7` (1) step, whatever its Move, Rush, Roads, Glaze, or
  Glide (rejection `MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL { reason: "STUCK" }`); a slide on ice
  is not a step, and a hop is one step. It may attack, act, Wait, embark,
  land, and exert ZOC; Tunnel, Bomb Run, Beam Down, and displacement are
  not Moves. A Stuck Raider never Charges (Charge needs two tiles).
- **Toothache**: **−1 Attack** (`TOOTHACHE_ATTACK2_V7` 2 half-units, never
  below 0.5) on the unit's next `ATTACK` at any distance, applied after
  every other Attack modifier; the entry is removed after that attack's
  exchange (or when it expires). It never changes retaliation, Defense,
  fixed damage, or a Whirl. The combat preview carries `toothacheAttack`.

**Sticky Toffee** (Toffee Trooper, role mechanic `sticky`, ability
`STICKY`). After an `ATTACK` exchange in which a land-form Toffee Trooper's
damage was computed (to HP or wholly to a Shield), the unit it hit becomes
Stuck if it is still on the board after the exchange's deaths: its target
when it attacked, and the attacker when it struck back (a ranged attacker
is never struck back, so never Stuck). A Crashed Trooper still sticks what
it strikes back at. Event `UNIT_STUCK { playerId, sourceUnitId, unitId, endsLeft }`
(`playerId` the Trooper's owner). The combat preview carries `stuckApplied`:
`NONE`, `TARGET`, `ATTACKER`, or `BOTH` (a Trooper attacking a Trooper that
survives and strikes back).

**Glaze Trail** (Donut Racer, `glazeTrail`, `GLAZE_TRAIL`). After an
accepted `MOVE` of a land-form Donut Racer that moved at least one tile,
its start tile and every tile its path passed (not the final tile) that is
land join `glazedThisTurn` (sorted by `(y, x)`, emptied at the active
seat's End Turn), with event `TILES_GLAZED { playerId, unitId, tiles }`
after the Move's events and its Crumbs eating. For a land-form unit of the
active seat (its own and the units it controls), a step onto a Glazed tile
costs `GLAZE_STEP_COST_V7` (1) half-point, a Road step's cost; every stop
still applies (Forest, Mountain, deep snow, ice, ZOC, unexplored, occupied).
Other seats never read the Glaze. The Racer has no Escape.

**Ricochet** (Gumball Gunner, `ricochet`, `RICOCHET`). After an `ATTACK`
by a land-form Gumball Gunner from distance 2 whose main hit dealt `d` of at
least 2 (HP plus Shield), the unit hostile to the Gunner's owner on the
eight tiles around the target's tile, other than the target, that the
Gunner's owner saw before the attack (any form but submerged; never an Egg
or the Giant Spider), with the lowest HP and then the lowest unit ID, takes
`floor(d / RICOCHET_DIVISOR_V7)` fixed damage (Armoured −1, Plated cap,
Shield first; no cover, fortification, Snow, or retaliation), whether or not
the target died. Event
`RICOCHETED { playerId, unitId, targetUnitId, damage, shieldDamage, dies }`;
a death is cause `RICOCHET`, credited like a splash death (the Gunner's
owner, unit kill credit to the Gunner). The preview carries
`ricochet: { unitId, damage, shieldDamage, dies } | null`.

**Bunny Hop** (Chocolate Bunny, `hop`, `HOP`). A land-form Chocolate
Bunny's `MOVE` path may contain one hop: two consecutive path tiles two
apart in a straight line (`dx`, `dy` each in {−2, 0, 2}). The jumped tile
must be explored and not water or ice (`MOVEMENT_ILLEGAL { reason: "HOP_ILLEGAL" }`);
it may hold any unit, Egg, mound, or Barricade and any land terrain, and is
not entered (no cost, stop, ZOC, eating, chest, or reveal). The hop costs
one ordinary step (2 half-points, never the Road or Glaze cost), and the
landing follows every entering rule; a second hop in one path is
`NOT_ADJACENT`. A hidden unit on the landing interrupts the Move on the
take-off tile (`UNIT_MOVE_INTERRUPTED`, reason `OCCUPIED`). The movement
search, `previewSugarRushV7`, and `queryThreatenedTilesV7` include hops.

**Thump** (Chocolate Bunny, `thumpDamage` 2, `THUMP`). After every `ATTACK`
by a land-form Chocolate Bunny (never on retaliation), if it is still on
the board, every other unit hostile to its owner on the eight tiles around
its tile after the advance and Bounce (any form but submerged; never an Egg,
the Giant Spider, or the attack's target) takes `THUMP_DAMAGE_V7` (2) fixed
damage (Armoured −1, Plated cap, Shield first). Event
`THUMPED { playerId, unitId, hits: [{ unitId, damage, shieldDamage, dies }] }`
(sorted by unit ID; none when empty); a death is cause `THUMP`, credited
like a splash death. The preview carries `thump` (the hits) and
`thumpUncertain` (an estimate whose Bounce is unknown, or a tile around the
Bunny the viewer has not explored).

**Toothache** (Jawbreaker, `toothache`, `TOOTHACHE`). After an `ATTACK` from
distance 1 on a land-form Jawbreaker, the attacker gets Toothache if it is
still on the board after the exchange's deaths, whether or not the
Jawbreaker survived. Event
`TOOTHACHE_GIVEN { playerId, sourceUnitId, unitId, endsLeft }` (`playerId`
the Jawbreaker's owner); the preview carries `toothacheApplied`.

**`TOP_UP { kind, unitId, targetUnitId }`** (Confectioner, ability
`TOP_UP`) is a primary action that may follow a Move. Legality, in order
(all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                                     | Rejection                                      |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                                  | the ordinary unit errors                       |
| 2   | Its role, under its kind, has `TOP_UP`.                                                                         | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                   |
| 3   | It is not Crashed.                                                                                              | `UNIT_CRASHED { unitId }`                      |
| 4   | It has not used a primary action and has not landed this turn.                                                  | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                           |
| 5   | It is in land form.                                                                                             | `TOP_UP_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`      |
| 6   | `targetUnitId` is a unit on the board the actor sees, other than the Confectioner, in land form (never an Egg). | `HEAL_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`                        |
| 7   | The target is the actor's own unit.                                                                             | `HEAL_TARGET_NOT_OWNED`                        |
| 8   | The target is within Chebyshev distance 1.                                                                      | `TOP_UP_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OUT_OF_RANGE" }`  |
| 9   | The target is Crashed, damaged, plagued, bitten, Frozen, Stuck, or has Toothache.                               | `TOP_UP_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "NOTHING_TO_DO" }` |

The target's `CRASHED` entry is removed; it heals
`min(TOP_UP_HEAL_V7 (2), maxHp − hp)`; Plague and Bitten are cured, a
Frozen unit thaws (its entry is removed), and Stuck and Toothache are
removed. A Frozen Confectioner cannot Top Up (`UNIT_FROZEN`). Its activation
is untouched. The Confectioner has used its primary action and is handled.
Event
`UNIT_TOPPED_UP { playerId, unitId, targetUnitId, crashEnded, amount, hpAfter, cured }`.
There is no per-target limit. `previewTopUpV7(view, unitId)` →
`{ unitId, targets: [{ unitId, crashEnded, amount, hpAfter, cured }] }`.

**`SUGAR_TOSS { kind, unitId, targetUnitId }`** is a primary action of the
Gumball Gunner. `tossedThisTurn` holds the units healed by a Sugar Toss
during the active seat's turn; it is emptied at that seat's End Turn.
Legality, in order (all rejections atomic):

| #   | Requirement                                                                                               | Rejection                                           |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `unitId` is the actor's own unit on the board.                                                            | the ordinary unit errors                            |
| 2   | Its role, under its kind, has `SUGAR_TOSS`.                                                               | `UNIT_ROLE_INVALID { role }`                        |
| 3   | It is not Crashed.                                                                                        | `UNIT_CRASHED { unitId }`                           |
| 4   | It has not used a primary action and has not landed this turn.                                            | `UNIT_ALREADY_ACTED`                                |
| 5   | It is in land form.                                                                                       | `SUGAR_TOSS_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "EMBARKED" }`       |
| 6   | `targetUnitId` is a unit on the board the actor sees, other than the Gunner, in land form (never an Egg). | `HEAL_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`                             |
| 7   | The target is the actor's own unit.                                                                       | `HEAL_TARGET_NOT_OWNED`                             |
| 8   | The target is within Chebyshev distance `SUGAR_TOSS_RANGE_V7` (2).                                        | `SUGAR_TOSS_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "OUT_OF_RANGE" }`   |
| 9   | The target is not in `tossedThisTurn`.                                                                    | `SUGAR_TOSS_NOT_LEGAL { reason: "ALREADY_TOSSED" }` |
| 10  | The target is damaged.                                                                                    | `HEAL_TARGET_FULL`                                  |

The target heals `min(SUGAR_TOSS_HEAL_V7 (2), maxHp − hp)` and joins the
list; nothing is cured, the target's action is not used, and a Shield is
never healed. The Gunner has used its primary action and is handled. Event
`SUGAR_TOSSED { playerId, unitId, targetUnitId, amount, hpAfter }`.

### 23.8 Resolution order

**An attack** is the resolution of
[section 13](#13-combat-and-fortification) with these Candy steps: the Rush
bonus and then the attacker's Toothache in the Attack value; no retaliation
from a Splatted defender; each death with its Grave or rising and then its
Crumbs; then the Splat of a Pie Launcher's surviving target, Stuck
(`UNIT_STUCK`), Toothache given (`TOOTHACHE_GIVEN`), and the attacker's own
Toothache used up; the Push and Knockback, the advance, and the Charge!
follow; then the Bounce; then the death-blast chains (each death with its
Crumbs), Plunder, and reveals; then a Juggernaut's crush; then the Ricochet
(`RICOCHETED`) and the Thump (`THUMPED`), each with its deaths, Graves,
risings, Crumbs, and blasts; then the ordinary tail. (The redesign orders
Ricochet and Thump before the death-blast chains; see
[section 25](#25-known-discrepancies).)

**A Move** of a Donut Racer: the Move's own events, eating Crumbs, then
`TILES_GLAZED`, then the tail.

**End Turn**, for the active seat, after the Dwarf per-turn lists are
emptied ([section 3](#3-players-turns-and-victory)): the Crash step
(`UNITS_CRASHED`), the Crumbs countdown (`CRUMBS_STALE`), the Stuck and
Toothache countdown of the active seat's units (no event), then
`splattedThisTurn`, `tossedThisTurn`, and `glazedThisTurn` are emptied. The
two events come after the idle-recovery events and before
`INCOME_PREVIEWED`. Start Turn has no Candy step.

### 23.9 Interactions with other rules

| Other rule                    | Ruling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field Defense, Walls, Dig In  | Count fully against Candy attacks; only Splat removes the retaliation. No Candy unit builds Field Defense; Field Defense in territory a Candy seat captures fortifies its units as usual.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Push, Knockback, Tractor Beam | Move a Candy unit like any; it keeps its `sugarRush` entry and eats nothing. A `JUGGERNAUT` body is never bounced.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Overrun, Ram, Rampage         | A Knight, Scrap Buggy, Steam Tank, T-Rex, Vampire, Mammoth, or Mole that hits a Marshmallow without killing it is bounced and has no continuation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Roads, Forest, Mountain, ice  | Glaze halves only the cost of a step onto it; every stop applies. A Stuck unit moves one step even along a Road. A hop may jump a Forest, a Mountain, a Rift, a unit, an Egg, a mound, or a Barricade, never water or ice; its landing is an ordinary entry.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Flyers                        | A flyer can be Stuck and get Toothache, and is hit by Ricochet and Thump; a Bunny may hop over one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Martian Shields, Shock Field  | A Shield absorbs Ricochet and Thump first; a hit wholly on a Shield still sticks. A Bunny or Trooper attacking a Shock Trooper takes its Shock Field as usual.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Armoured, Plated              | Reduce and cap Ricochet and Thump like any fixed damage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Giant signatures              | A swallowed unit has left the board, so its Stuck, Toothache, Rush, and Crash entries go, and a `DIGESTED` Candy unit leaves no Crumbs. Goblin Toss, Thunder Stomp, Swallow, and Break Off are not Moves or attacks: Stuck and Toothache do not touch them; a crush rides on an `ATTACK`, so its attacker's Toothache lowers that hit, never the fixed crush. Ricochet and Thump hit giants; a Bunny may hop over one; a Top-Up ends a Gingerbread Giant's Crash.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Whirl                         | A Whirligig's Whirl is not an `ATTACK`: Toothache never lowers it and is not used up by it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Charge!                       | A Triceratops is bounced after its push and follow, back to the tile its follow started from.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Graves, Raise Dead, Devour    | A Candy death leaves a Grave where the Grave rules allow and its Crumbs. A raised Skeleton stands on Crumbs without eating them; a Ghoul that ends its Move on the tile eats them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Infect, Bitten, Plague, Wail  | A Candy unit that rises leaves no Crumbs; Plague, Wail, and splash deaths leave Crumbs; Top-Up cures Plague and Bitten on one adjacent own unit (Sugar Toss cures nothing).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Kaboom, death blasts, Plunder | Blast deaths of Candy units leave Crumbs; a Peppermint, Ricochet, or Thump death of an exploding unit explodes with its chain. A Goblin seat earns Plunder for the Candy units its units and blasts kill; a Peppermint death credits the Candy seat, which has no Plunder.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Eggs                          | Targets for every Candy unit; never Stuck, given Toothache, or hit by a Ricochet or a Thump. A Re-bake scoops Crumbs from under an Egg, and a Bunny may hop over one; laying and hatching eat nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Armoured, Plated, Shields     | Reduce, cap, and absorb a Peppermint Surprise as they do fixed damage. Splat applies when a Shield took the whole hit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Flyers and walkers            | Saucers, Motherships, and Gyrocopters never eat Crumbs; Tripods and Colossi do. A flyer bounced off a Marshmallow may land on a Rift; a ground unit is never bounced onto one, and neither onto water.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Beam Down, Tunnel, surfacing  | Placements: they eat nothing. A Re-bake scoops Crumbs from under a mound; a burrowed unit is off the board, so it is never Stuck, given Toothache, or hit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Mind Control                  | Any Candy unit beside the Brain is a target since `7r99` (the Golem too; 6 HP or less and never the Golem before) and keeps its `sugarRush`, `stuck`, and `toothache` entries. A controlled Candy unit follows the body rules for its controller (it Rushes, Crashes, Bounces, Splats, sticks, glazes for its controller, ricochets, hops, thumps, gives Toothache, Tosses to and Tops Up its controller's units) and the seat rules of its controller: it eats Candy Crumbs, leaves none when it dies, and cannot Re-bake (`REBAKE` is in `MIND_CONTROLLED_LOST_ABILITIES_V7`). Psychic Command gives Inspired, and then the Rush bonus does not add; Toothache still applies after it. |
| Snow, Frozen, Shatter         | Deep snow stops a Rushed Candy ground unit like any; a Frozen unit cannot Rush, Top Up, or Re-bake; a Frozen unit may be Stuck or given Toothache, which it keeps while Frozen; Top-Up thaws a Frozen own unit; a shattered Candy unit leaves Crumbs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Rift                          | No Candy unit enters a Rift, so no Crumbs lie on one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Curiosities, the Giant Spider | Crumbs are never left on a Fountain or a Shrine. The Spider's kills leave Crumbs; it is never Splatted, Stuck, given Toothache, hit by a Ricochet or a Thump, or bounced, and never eats Crumbs; a Re-bake scoops Crumbs from under it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Missions                      | A `MISSION` setup accepts a Candy seat and starts the seven lists empty; the teaser chapter does not use the Candy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Capture, siege, capacity      | Capture is a primary action: a Crashed unit cannot capture, and still besieges. A re-baked unit takes a slot of the Confectioner's home city, which may go one unit over capacity.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Boats and embarking           | Candy boats are the Sugar Sails fleet (`7r97`: Gumdrop Tug, Pie Galleon, Choco Sub): with Sugar Sails they Rush and Crash; the Pie Galleon Splats; no Crumbs, no redesign ability. An embarked unit cannot Rush; a Rushed unit that embarks still Crashes; a Crashed embarked unit may land. A boat attacking a Marshmallow from distance 1 is bounced onto water. Splat, Stuck, Toothache, Ricochet, and Thump apply to boats and embarked units (a Stuck boat moves one step); a copy is never baked onto water or ice, and Glaze is land only.                                                                                                                                        |
| Achievements                  | Unchanged. Muster counts the Candy trainable roles (a re-baked unit at once); Slayer never counts a Peppermint death.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### 23.10 Commands, events, errors, and queries

- **Commands.** `SUGAR_RUSH`, `REBAKE`, and `SUGAR_TOSS` follow
  `ATTACK_BARRICADE` in `COMMAND_KIND_ORDER_V7`, and the redesign's
  `TOP_UP` follows `SUGAR_TOSS` (before `RECOVER`). `REBAKE` carries
  `from`; a `REBAKE` without it is not a command. `MOVE` uses the Rushed
  budget, Stuck's one step, the Glaze, and the hop; every primary action is
  refused for a Crashed unit; `ATTACK` applies the Rush bonus, Toothache,
  Splat, Stuck, Toothache given, Bounce, Ricochet, and Thump; and
  `TEND_WOUNDED`, `RALLY`, and `BUILD_FIELD_DEFENSE` are never offered to a
  Candy unit or seat.
- **State.** `sugarRush`, `crumbs`, `splattedThisTurn`, and
  `tossedThisTurn` follow `tractorUsedThisTurn`, and the redesign's
  `stuck`, `toothache`, and `glazedThisTurn` follow `tossedThisTurn`. State parsing rejects an unsorted list or a duplicate
  entry and any entry in a match without a Candy seat; a `sugarRush` entry
  whose unit is not on the board, is not of kind `CANDY`, or is not in land
  or embarked form; a `splattedThisTurn` entry whose unit is not on the
  board or is neutral; a `tossedThisTurn` entry whose unit is not on the
  board or not in land form; a `stuck` or `toothache` entry whose unit is
  not on the board, is an Egg, or is neutral, or whose `endsLeft` is not 1
  or 2; a `glazedThisTurn` tile that is not land; and a `crumbs` entry
  whose tile is not land or is a Rift, a chest tile, or a curiosity tile
  (a settlement site is accepted), whose owner is not an active Candy seat,
  whose role leaves no Crumbs, or whose `turnsLeft` is outside 1 to 3. A
  unit's Overrun or Escape flag is read only from its role's abilities.
- **Events.** `UNITS_CRASHED` and `CRUMBS_STALE` come before
  `INCOME_PREVIEWED`; `UNIT_REBAKED` follows `UNIT_ASSEMBLED`,
  `UNIT_SUGAR_RUSHED` `UNITS_FROZEN` (then named `UNITS_CHILLED`), `SUGAR_TOSSED` `WOUNDED_TENDED`,
  `CRUMBS_EATEN` `UNIT_MOVE_INTERRUPTED`, and `CRUMBS_LEFT`
  `GRAVE_CREATED`. The redesign adds `UNIT_TOPPED_UP` after
  `SUGAR_TOSSED`, `TILES_GLAZED` after `CRUMBS_EATEN`, and `UNIT_STUCK`,
  `TOOTHACHE_GIVEN`, `RICOCHETED`, and `THUMPED` after
  `BARRICADE_ATTACKED`; `UNIT_REBAKED` gains `from`. `UNIT_DIED.cause`
  gains `PEPPERMINT`, `RICOCHET`, and `THUMP`. Bounce reuses `UNIT_PUSHED`,
  and Splat and the status countdowns have no event.
- **Combat preview.** `sugarRushApplied` (false), `splatApplied` (false),
  `bounce` (`NONE`), `bounceTo` (null), `stuckApplied` (`NONE`),
  `toothacheApplied` (false), `toothacheAttack` (false), `ricochet` (null),
  `thump` (empty), and `thumpUncertain` (false) are neutral for every
  attack with no Candy unit or status; `noRetaliationReason` gains
  `SPLATTED`; `escapeAvailable` and `overrunAdvance` are never set for a
  Candy unit. `CombatOptionsV7` gains `assumeSugarRush` and
  `ignoreToothache` (the Whirl).
- **Errors.** `UNIT_CRASHED { unitId }`, `SUGAR_RUSH_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`,
  `RUSHED`), `REBAKE_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `NO_HOME`, `NO_CRUMBS`,
  `TILE`), `SUGAR_TOSS_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`,
  `ALREADY_TOSSED`), `TOP_UP_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`,
  `NOTHING_TO_DO`), and the movement reasons `STUCK` and `HOP_ILLEGAL`.
- **Fog.** Crumbs are public on every explored tile, with their owner's
  `bite`; `CRUMBS_LEFT` and `CRUMBS_STALE` (its tiles filtered) are
  projected like `GRAVE_CREATED`. The `sugarRush`, `splattedThisTurn`,
  `tossedThisTurn`, `stuck`, and `toothache` entries are public for
  visible units, and `glazedThisTurn` for explored tiles.
  `TILES_GLAZED` goes to the Racer's owner and to viewers who see the
  Racer, with its tiles filtered to those the viewer sees (none when no
  tile is left); `UNIT_STUCK`, `TOOTHACHE_GIVEN`, `RICOCHETED`, and
  `UNIT_TOPPED_UP` to viewers who see both units they name; `THUMPED` to
  viewers who see the Bunny, with its hits filtered to the units they see
  (none when no hit is left). `UNIT_SUGAR_RUSHED` goes to viewers who see the unit,
  `UNITS_CRASHED` to viewers who own or see one of its units (filtered),
  and `UNIT_REBAKED` and `SUGAR_TOSSED` to the acting seat. `CRUMBS_EATEN`
  goes to every viewer who sees the eater, and to the Crumbs' owner and
  every viewer who explored the tile with `unitId`, `damage`,
  `shieldDamage`, and `dies` null when they cannot see the eater.
- **Queries.** `unitIsRushedV7`, `unitIsCrashedV7`, `unitIsSplattedV7`,
  `crumbsAtV7`, `crumbsBiteV7`, `homeSweetHomeSparesV7`, `unitIsStuckV7`,
  and `unitHasToothacheV7` read canonical state or a view.
  `queryPlayerCommandsV7` offers a Candy seat `SUGAR_RUSH` for every legal
  unit, `REBAKE` for every legal `(Confectioner, from, at)`, `SUGAR_TOSS`
  for every legal `(Gunner, target)`, and `TOP_UP` for every legal
  `(Confectioner, target)`, and never a primary action or `SUGAR_RUSH` for
  a Crashed unit; every offered command is accepted. The movement search
  offers hop paths and reads the Glaze and Stuck. `previewSugarRushV7(view, unitId)` →
  `{ unitId, move, destinations, newDestinations, homeSweetHome }`,
  `previewRebakeV7(view, unitId)` →
  `{ unitId, cityId, usedSlots, capacity, rebakeCapacity, options: [{ from, at, role, cost, hp }] }`
  (options in `(from, at)` order), `queryRebakeBlockerV7(view, unitId)` →
  why the viewer's own Confectioner has no `REBAKE` (`NOT_YOUR_TURN`,
  `CRASHED`, `ACTED`, `EMBARKED`, `NO_HOME`, `NO_CRUMBS`, `TILE`,
  `CITY_CAPACITY_FULL`, or `INSUFFICIENT_COINS`) or null (the "why not"
  query of `pulp_wars-jdb.9`), `previewTopUpV7(view, unitId)`
  ([section 23.7](#237-the-redesign-abilities)),
  `previewSugarTossV7(view, unitId)` →
  `{ unitId, targets: [{ unitId, amount, hpAfter }] }`, and
  `previewCrumbsEatV7(view, unitId, to)` →
  `{ at, ownerId, role, damage, shieldDamage, dies }`, each null unless the
  command is offered. `queryCombatPreviewV7` and `estimateCombatV7` include
  the Rush bonus, Toothache, Splat, Stuck, Toothache given, Bounce,
  Ricochet, and Thump; every preview equals the resolution.
  `queryThreatenedTilesV7` gives a visible Candy unit that is neither
  Rushed nor Crashed its reach as if Rushed (a Bunny's with its hops), and
  a Crashed one, or a Rushed one that Home Sweet Home will not spare where
  it stands, no attack reach for the next turn.
- **Public unit stats** carry, for every unit when the match has a Candy
  seat, `rushed`, `crashed`, `splatted`, `tossedThisTurn`, `stuck`, and
  `toothache` (booleans), and for Candy units the `candy` block:
  `sugarRush`, `sticky`, `glazeTrail`, `ricochet`, `hop`, `thumpDamage`,
  `givesToothache`, `bounces`, `splats`, `rebake` (`{ cost, hp }` or
  null), and the owner's `homeSweetHome` and `crumbsBite`. A Rushed unit's Attack stat carries the
  modifier `SUGAR_RUSH` (+1) while its first attack is unused and neither
  Charge nor Inspired applies, and its Move stat carries the same modifier
  (+1) while it is Rushed in land form, the number the movement query and
  `previewSugarRushV7` use (`pulp_wars-jdb.9`; a derived breakdown, no
  shape or identity change). The Normal AI reads a Rushed unit's Move
  without that term, as before.
- `PublicPlayerV7` and the leaderboard carry `CANDY` and
  `CANDY_BASELINE_V1`. The headless metrics carry the block `candy`
  (`src/headless/candy-telemetry-v7.ts`), match totals of every Candy
  ability, all zero without a Candy seat; the redesign replaced the Frosting
  and Rush-perk counters with Stuck, Toothache, Glaze steps, Ricochet and
  Thump damage and kills, hops, Top-Ups (and Crashes they ended), Re-bakes
  by distance, and stale Crumbs by reason.
- **Pruning.** Every accepted command drops the `sugarRush`,
  `splattedThisTurn`, `tossedThisTurn`, `stuck`, and `toothache` entries of
  units that left the board, the `tossedThisTurn` entries of units that
  left land form, the `stuck` and `toothache` entries of Eggs, and the
  Crumbs of a Candy seat that is no longer active.
- **Text harness.** `scripts/play-text-v7.ts` offers a Re-bake as
  `u<id>.rebake.<x>,<y>><x>,<y>` (from, then at) and a Top-Up as
  `u<id>.topup.u<id>`, and prints Stuck and Toothache among a unit's
  statuses.

### 23.11 Normal AI, presentation, and balance

- **Normal AI** (`pulp_wars-jdb.4`): the Candy play of
  [section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary). The redesign keeps it legal with a
  basic Top-Up and the new Re-bake shape; using the other new abilities is
  `pulp_wars-jdb.13`.
- **Presentation** (`pulp_wars-jdb.6`, with the production art of
  `pulp_wars-jdb.5`; every number and legal choice comes from the public
  view, the offered commands, and the public previews). Every seat's
  faction select offers the Candy; their owner colour is cotton-candy pink
  (`#ffb8d8`), and their units, portraits, cities, and ships have their own
  art. A Rushed unit carries a chip, a Crashed unit a swirl over a faded
  sprite, a Splatted unit a pie, and, on its owner's view, a Rushed unit
  that Home Sweet Home will spare a small house. Crumbs are a token with the fallen
  unit's head, a pip per turn left, and a peppermint dot when they bite.
  The Sugar Rush button arms the Rush: the board shows the Rushed reach,
  and choosing a destination or a target sends `SUGAR_RUSH` and then the
  Move or the attack; Back, Escape, or another selection sends nothing. A
  Re-bake tile (the dearest Crumbs in reach for that tile) and a Sugar Toss
  target are picked on the board, and each Top-Up target has its own
  "Top-Up {unit}" button. The redesign's markers, effects, and preview
  lines (Stuck, Toothache, the Glaze, hops, Ricochet, Thump) are
  `pulp_wars-jdb.14`; Help and the glossary already name every new
  ability. The attack preview names a Rush
  ("Sugar Rush +1"), a Splat, a Splatted target, and a Bounce, and a Move
  onto hostile Crumbs says "Eats Crumbs" with the Peppermint damage. Help
  has one sentence per Candy rule, and the technology tree shows Home Sweet
  Home and Peppermint Surprise to a Candy viewer. The exact texts are in
  the overlay's [section 15](RULESET_7_CANDY.md#15-ui-requirements), with
  the differences of its
  [section 24](RULESET_7_CANDY.md#24-implementation-notes-pulp_wars-jdb6).
  The Classic and LEGACY looks draw Candy units as Human sprites with the
  Candy badge, a wrapped sweet (`pulp_wars-jdb.9`), on the board and on the
  unit's portrait, as does a Candy raster that fails to load.
- **Balance** (`pulp_wars-jdb.7`). The roster and every Candy constant are
  the overlay's contract values: the coarse balance changed none. It was
  closed on a small sample at `pulp-wars-poc-7r38` (Dry Land, 11 x 11,
  Normal against Normal, six games against each other faction): the Candy
  won 20 of 42 (Humans 2, Undead 5, Goblins 2, Dinosaurs 3, Martians 2,
  Ice Folk 3, Dwarves 3). The sample predates the Grunt's 8 HP (`7r39`),
  the village density (`7r40`), and the 3 starting Coins and tier 3 base
  cost of 9 (`7r41`), and it is a sanity check, not a measurement
  ([balance record](RULESET_7_CANDY.md#195-balance-record-pulp_wars-jdb7)).

### 23.12 The Jawbreaker: Rock Hard

`pulp-wars-poc-7r55` (`pulp_wars-w49.17`). The **Jawbreaker** is the Candy
heavy line unit (role `SWORDSMAN`; 6 Coins, 16 HP, Attack 3, Defense 2.5,
Move 1, melee, captures; Metallurgy, which a Candy player sees as
Jawbreakers). It has Sugar Rush and the Crash, leaves Crumbs, and can be
re-baked for 3 Coins at 8 HP like any Candy land unit
([sections 23.2](#232-sugar-rush-and-the-crash) to
[23.4](#234-eating-crumbs-and-the-peppermint-surprise)). Its numbers are
first guesses.

- **Rock Hard** (`immovable`). In land form a Jawbreaker is never moved by
  another unit's rule: not by a Push (a Juggernaut-role attack), a Charge!
  push, a Steam Cannon's Knockback, or a Tractor Beam (the beam reports
  `TARGET_IMMUNE`), and it is not bounced when it attacks a Marshmallow or
  the Gingerbread Giant. The damage of the attack applies in full; only
  the move is cancelled.
- An embarked Jawbreaker's transport is shoved like any boat, and a reward
  unit that appears on its own city's center still displaces it.
- The rule is the unit's kind's: a mind-controlled Jawbreaker keeps it.

**Documentation parity (2026-09-28, no ruleset or identity change):** where
older documents disagreed with the code, the code's behavior was adopted as
the rule and is now stated in the ordinary sections: Field Defense
destruction by attack regardless of tile owner
([section 13.4](#134-after-combat)); sea trade for a captured foreign capital
([section 9.5](#95-sea-links); sea trade itself was removed with `7r76`); the capital +1 income following a captured
capital to its new owner ([section 4.3](#43-income)); settlement counts on
widths 11–16 following the AI count ([section 2.2](#22-settlements-and-treasures));
and Windmill healing without Milling ([section 10](#10-recovery-and-support)).

**Undead release fold (2026-09-30, `pulp_wars-vkq.16`, no ruleset or identity
change):** revisions 13–16 were folded into this document for both factions,
and the `?undead=1` development flag was removed, so faction choice is part of
every match setup. Where the older text of this document or an overlay
disagreed with the code, the code's behavior is stated:

- retaliation needs the `ATTACK` ability and an Attack above 0, not merely an
  Attack stat (the Banshee has Attack 1 for Wail but never retaliates), and
  the attacker must not be `UNANSWERED` ([section 13.2](#132-damage));
- Rally and Frenzy targets are own land-form units that are not `SUPPORT` or
  `SIEGE`, have the `ATTACK` ability, and are not already Inspired (for Human
  units this equals the former "not a Captain or Catapult";
  [section 10](#10-recovery-and-support));
- Charge applies only at range 1 (no Human or Undead Charge unit has a longer
  range; [section 13.2](#132-damage));
- stale revision-12 values replaced by later revisions: the 7r12 identity and
  obsolete-key list, the eight-neighbour Shallow rule, the village table,
  research tiers `7 + 2(C - 1)` and `9 + 3(C - 1)`, the uncapped level term,
  the Commerce-doubled Market paying up to 4 (8), Patrol Boat and embarked
  Move 3, and "Only the `ORIGINAL` faction exists";
- "living unit" meaning a unit on the board was reworded to "on the board"
  (Muster, capacity, occupancy, legality, endgame siege), because "living"
  now means non-Undead.

**Goblin release fold (2026-10-01, `pulp_wars-0ao.9`, no ruleset or identity
change):** revision 17 (`pulp-wars-poc-7r17`, implemented by
`pulp_wars-0ao.2`–`0ao.8` and `0ao.11`–`0ao.17`) was folded into this document
for three factions, with a Goblin roster table, the Goblin technology
differences, [section 18](#18-goblin-faction-rules), and the Goblin
interactions in the shared sections; the former sections 18 (revision
history) and 19 (known discrepancies) became 19 and 20. Every Goblin value
was checked against `GOBLIN_ROLE_RULES_V7`, `GOBLIN_ROLE_MECHANICS_V7`,
`FACTION_RULES_V7`, `STARTING_FIGHTERS_V7`, `MILITIA_FIGHTERS_V7`, and
`explosions.ts`. Where the revision-17 overlay and the code differed, the
code's behavior is stated:

- the `pulp_wars-0ao.7` tuned values replace the contract's (one starting
  Goblin; Goblin Attack 1.5, Defense 0.5, Kaboom 5; death blasts 2, 4, and
  4); Militia stays two Goblins;
- the chain bound counts the units on the board at chain start plus the
  wave-1 exploders that just died;
- `previewAttackExplosionsV7` returns null (not an empty chain) for an attack
  that is not offered; explosion preview results may carry a null `unitId`
  for a would-be rising; `touchesUnexplored` also covers the splash ring and
  an unknown Push destination;
- the naval events of a command precede its `PLAGUE_CLEARED`;
- technology display names are resolved in the UI helper `technologyNameV7`,
  not by the technology tree query, which returns IDs only (root decision;
  `pulp_wars-0ao.16` removed the engine's duplicate Title Case helper, so
  `technologyNameV7` is the single name helper);
- Goblin cities use the shared settlement art with no Goblin city tint (root
  decision on `pulp_wars-0ao.4`; presentation, not a rule).

The fold also records two code changes made while it was prepared. Landing
ends the unit's activation for every faction (`pulp_wars-0ao.15`, root
decision, as revisions 6 and 16 specify; [section 14](#14-naval-rules)):
before it, `DISEMBARK` set only `moved` and `handled`, so a landed unit was
still offered and allowed Attack, Kaboom, Disband, and other primary actions,
and the public threatened-tiles query and the Normal AI counted an embarked
goblin-crewed unit's landing-then-Kaboom reach (`pulp_wars-0ao.11`); that
reach is gone. Cure text is faction-aware (`pulp_wars-0ao.16`): Goblins have
no cure for Plague or Bitten, and their Help and status sentences say so.

**Dinosaur release fold (2026-10-03, `pulp_wars-c87.9`, no ruleset or identity
change):** revision 19 as amended by revision 20, revision 21, and the
`pulp_wars-0hi.3` numbers (`pulp-wars-poc-7r23`) were folded into this
document for four factions, with a Dinosaur roster table, the Dinosaur
technology differences, the seven achievements of
[section 5](#5-achievements-and-monuments), the slot sum and the Nesting
term of [section 4.4](#44-unit-capacity), the hatch step of Start Turn, the
full-heal Promotion, [section 19](#19-dinosaur-faction-rules), and the
Dinosaur interactions in the shared sections; the former sections 19
(revision history) and 20 (known discrepancies) became 20 and 21. Every
value was checked against `ORIGINAL_ROLE_RULES_V7`,
`DINOSAUR_ROLE_RULES_V7`, `DINOSAUR_ROLE_MECHANICS_V7`, the Dinosaur tree
and `technologyCapabilitiesV7`, `cityUnitCapacityForV7`,
`FACTION_RULES_V7`, `STARTING_FIGHTERS_V7`, `MILITIA_FIGHTERS_V7`, the
constants of `ruleset-v7.ts` and `achievements.ts`, `eggs.ts`, `growth.ts`,
`combat.ts`, and the reducer. Where an overlay and the code differed, the
code's behavior is stated:

- revision 19's text that revision 20 did not mark as superseded but that no
  longer holds: the "2 slots for the T-Rex and Brontosaurus" of its section
  5.1 (the Triceratops uses 2 again since revision 20), its section 2.4
  Showcase capital at 7 of 7 (8 of 8 with the Nesting slot,
  [section 2.5](#25-showcase-setup)), and its hatch times of at most 3 (the
  T-Rex hatches in 4);
- the Caveman has 10 HP (`pulp_wars-0hi.3`); revision 20's implementation
  note keeping it at 12 describes `7r20`–`7r22`;
- revision 20 section 4.2's Ankylosaurus row: the engine applies the
  Ankylosaurus's own Armoured reduction to the retaliation it takes, 3 / 11
  without Wallbreaker and 5 / 4 with it (revision 20 implementation note 2;
  [section 19.10](#1910-wallbreaker));
- revision 20 section 2.2's Push for a Charge!: the preview reads the
  explored tile behind the target as resolution does, and only a Mountain or
  Deep Water behind another player's unit stays `UNKNOWN_BEHIND_FOG`
  (revision 20 implementation note 3; [section 19.11](#1911-charge));
- revision 19 section 10's "existing reason" for an attack on an Egg is
  `noRetaliationReason: "OUT_OF_RANGE"`, the reason the engine reports for
  every surviving defender that cannot retaliate other than an `UNANSWERED`
  attack ([section 13.2](#132-damage));
- revision 21's "No achievement counts kills" was removed from this document
  (Slayer counts them), as its decision 8 asked;
- the Normal AI document's "lane blocking" bullet (an own unit stepping into
  a hostile Triceratops's Stampede lane) described a heuristic that
  `pulp_wars-0hi.2` deleted with Stampede; it was removed from
  [Normal AI](../architecture/NORMAL_AI.md#revision-19-dinosaur-play-pulp_wars-c875).

**Martian release fold (2026-10-03, `pulp_wars-t6s.7`, no ruleset or
identity change):** the [Martian overlay](RULESET_7_MARTIANS.md)
(`pulp-wars-poc-7r22`, implemented by `pulp_wars-t6s.2`, with the Normal AI
of `pulp_wars-t6s.3`, the UI of `pulp_wars-t6s.4`, and the production art of
`pulp_wars-t6s.6`), including its implementation notes (section 19) and the
`pulp_wars-t6s.5` tuning record (`pulp-wars-poc-7r25`: Colossus Defense 2.5),
was folded into this document for five factions, with a Martian roster
table, the Martian technology differences,
[section 20](#20-martian-faction-rules), the Shield, Cooling, and Mind
Control cooldown steps of Start Turn and End Turn, and the Martian
interactions in the shared sections; the former sections 20 (revision
history) and 21 (known discrepancies) became 21 and 22. Every value was
checked against `MARTIAN_ROLE_RULES_V7`, `MARTIAN_ROLE_MECHANICS_V7`, the
Martian tree and `technologyCapabilitiesV7`, `FACTION_RULES_V7`, the
Martian constants of `ruleset-v7.ts`, the shared terrain rules
(`canEnterTerrainV7`, `terrainStopsMoveV7`, `canCrossWaterV7`,
`flyerMayStandOnSiteV7`), `martian.ts`, `combat.ts`, `movement.ts`, the
reducer, and the public queries. Where the overlay and the code differed,
the code's behavior is stated:

- the overlay's own precise readings of section 19.2 are the rule: the
  whole hit for Pierce and splash is capped at the target's Shield plus HP;
  a hit a Shield absorbs completely plagues nobody, while an unshielded hit
  of 0 still plagues; a Tractor Beam on another player's unit reads the
  board, not that player's Engineering or Navigation
  ([section 20.10](#2010-tractor-beam)); an unexplored foreign center
  interrupted a flyer's Move with `SETTLEMENT_FORBIDDEN` (until
  `pulp_wars-ke95`, after which a flyer may end there); an eliminated
  seat's Thralls are removed with cause `ELIMINATION`; `PLAGUE_DAMAGED`
  carries no `shieldDamage`; the Thrall's HP is the victim's;
- the overlay's Rift rules (sections 7.4, 8.1 row 7, 8.2 row 9, 10.1, and
  the Rift parts of 7.2 and 8.4) are implemented by `pulp_wars-9s0.5`
  (`7r28`) as written, with the rest of the Rift's rules in the
  [Rift overlay](RULESET_7_RIFT.md); the Rift left the map revision at
  `REGIONAL_BIOMES_NAVAL_V2` (it is `V3` since the village density of
  `7r40`);
- the blockade recompute after `DISBAND` (overlay 10.7 and 19.2 note 8)
  runs after every `DISBAND` while the state has any Thrall, not only after
  one that collapsed a Thrall; the events are emitted only on a change, and
  no other Disband can change a dock, so the reported events are the same;
- overlay 10.8 says the public preview flags `touchesUnexplored` for a
  Pierce tile that is unexplored: `queryCombatPreviewV7` has no such flag
  (it lists only a visible Pierce victim); `previewAttackExplosionsV7` sets
  its `touchesUnexplored` for that tile;
- details the overlay leaves open: a flyer's Pillage is rejected with
  `PILLAGE_INVALID_TARGET`; a Thrall's public `martian.capacitySlots` is 0;
  a full-power ray leaves no Cooling when the shooter dies in the exchange;
  the treasure unit's placement and reward displacement use the unit's own
  movement mode (a Saucer is placed on a Mountain without Engineering); the
  End Turn order is recovery, the expiry of Inspired and Overrun, Cooling,
  then the Force Fields recharge;
- the overlay's examples were computed with 10-HP Human Fighters, Raiders,
  and Marksmen and 15-HP Guards; the damage values are unchanged at full HP,
  and the examples here state the current HP (a full-power Tripod ray on a
  12-HP Fighter is a whole hit of 12 and pierces for 6, the value overlay
  6.4 gives, which its note 19.2.1 corrected for a 10-HP Fighter);
- the overlay's identity numbers predate the Ice Folk engine: its 48
  command kinds and 76 event kinds are 50 and 77 at `7r25`, with the Ice
  Folk kinds after the Martian ones; its status text ("No bead of the
  Martian epic folds this overlay") and placeholder-art plan (section 13.4)
  are superseded;
- this document's own stale values were corrected: the prior-identity list
  and the obsolete autosave keys run through `7r24` (not `7r23`), and the
  Tend Wounded cure of Plague and Bitten names the Dinosaur Shaman beside the
  Human Captain.

## 25. Known discrepancies

As of `pulp-wars-poc-7r53` the rules in this document match the code for
the eight factions it describes, including the Dinosaur faction of revisions
19 and 20, the achievements of revision 21, the Martian faction of the
Martian overlay with the engine of the Mind Control overlay, the Ice Folk
faction of the Ice Folk overlay, the Dwarf faction of the Dwarf overlay,
the Candy faction of the Candy overlay,
the mission setup of [section 2.6](#26-mission-setup), the map
curiosities of [section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities), and the Martian and Ice
Folk balance round of `7r37` with the Grunt's 8 HP of `7r39`, and the
village density of `7r40`, and the starting Coins and tier 3 technology base
cost of `7r41`, and the many seats of `7r42`, and the naval branch of
`7r43` and `7r44` with the ice fortification fix of `7r45`, and
[tuning 1](RULESET_7_TUNING_1.md) of `7r46` and its round 2 of `7r47`,
and [round 5 of the Human tuning](RULESET_7_TUNING_HUMAN.md#12-round-5) of `7r48`
and [round 6](RULESET_7_TUNING_HUMAN.md#13-round-6) of `7r49`,
and [the Goblin pass](RULESET_7_TUNING_GOBLIN.md) of `7r50`,
and [the Undead pass](RULESET_7_TUNING_UNDEAD.md) of `7r51`,
and [the Martian pass](RULESET_7_TUNING_MARTIAN.md) of `7r52`,
and [the Dinosaur pass](RULESET_7_TUNING_DINOSAUR.md) of `7r53`,
with these
open items: what is left of the naval branch after the fold, the Candy
items left after the fold, and the pending balance steps below.

**Open.**

- **The frozen sea redesign: what is open** (`pulp_wars-5ti.25`, `7r100`;
  [RULESET_7_ICE_REDESIGN.md](RULESET_7_ICE_REDESIGN.md)). The engine and
  rules are built, and the Normal AI plays for and against permanent ice
  (`pulp_wars-5ti.26`, [section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)), proven on
  hand-built states only. No
  interface offers Crack Ice yet (`CRACK_ICE` is classed bar-only in
  `TILE_ACTION_COMMAND_CLASSES_V7` until bead `pulp_wars-5ti.27` gives it
  its dock button and icon), buildings on ice have no snow pad, and the
  Fishing Hole draws the Fish resource art until its own sprite lands. No
  game was played or simulated (the standing rule): every number of the
  redesign is a first guess, and Frontier 7 is replayed by hand in bead
  `pulp_wars-v642.10`.
- **The Human tuning, round 6: what is open** (`pulp_wars-w49.6`, `7r49`;
  [round 6](RULESET_7_TUNING_HUMAN.md#13-round-6)). Nothing of round 6 was
  played by hand yet; its forks for the user are in its section 13.8 and

**Resolved by implementation** (`pulp_wars-737.6`, `pulp_wars-737.7`):

- **Map curiosities: the board (resolved).** Engine steps I and II of the
  [map curiosities spec](RULESET_7_MAP_CURIOSITIES.md) (`7r35`, `7r36`)
  landed before their art and UI, so for a while the browser offered the
  "Curiosities" checkbox but drew no curiosity marker and showed the Spider
  with the Juggernaut's art. The art (`pulp_wars-737.5`) and the UI
  (`pulp_wars-737.6`) are now live with no identity change
  ([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities) "Presentation"), the Normal AI plays
  the curiosities (`pulp_wars-737.4`), and `pulp_wars-737.7` ran the coarse
  check and folded the spec.

**Map curiosities spec against the code** (`pulp_wars-737.7`; resolved by
stating the code's behavior):

- **Event order of the neutral turn.** The spec's section 8.5 step 4 puts
  the naval blockade and sea-network events of a blockader the Spider
  killed before `NEUTRAL_TURN_ENDED`. The code reports them where every
  `END_TURN` reports them, at the end of the command, after
  `NEUTRAL_TURN_ENDED` and the next seat's Start Turn events
  ([section 3](#3-players-turns-and-victory)).
- **Claims.** A Shrine or Wreck is claimed only by a `MOVE` that steps
  onto its tile (a unit already standing there, for example after a Push,
  claims nothing until it leaves and returns). The spec's "not a Thrall" is
  moot since `7r33`: a mind-controlled unit may claim a Shrine. A Shrine
  veteran may have fewer than three kills, which the state schema allows
  only with the option on.
- **Missions.** The `MISSION` map type postdates the spec: a mission setup
  must carry `curiosities: false` and the headless CLI refuses the flag
  with `--map-type mission`.
- **Wail credit.** A Wail credits no kill; a Spider it kills pays its
  bounty to the Banshee's owner and counts for no unit.
- **Previews.** `monsterRetaliates` is an optional field, present only
  when the target is a visible Spider, and true when neither side dies and
  the attacker stands in the Spider's reach. `queryThreatenedTilesV7` is a
  per-unit query, so the provoke tiles are the answer for a Spider unit,
  not an addition to every answer. `previewMonsterV7`'s area ignores
  occupancy, and its reach counts an unexplored tile of the area as a
  possible step.
- **UI text.** The Spider's dock chip is "Neutral" (the spec's "Owned by
  nobody"), the provoke warning is a marker with its sentence as the tile's
  cursor description, and "The wilds stir" is a log line (a toast only when
  the Spider attacked the viewer's unit), under the standing "minimal text,
  no coordinates" rule.
- **Normal AI.** The spec's rule (a), "this turn's offered attacks", also
  counts the units that can move in and attack this turn; "with no attack"
  and "no better target" mean no offered attack on a unit that is not a
  Spider; a capturer within 2 of a center it can take runs no Shrine
  errand; the Fountain "counts as recovery" as a priority over `RECOVER`
  (the campaign has no retreat by HP); and incidental damage to the Spider
  (splash, Wail, Kaboom, a Bomb Run, an eruption) is not filtered (spec
  section 20; [section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)).
- **Acceptance criterion 7** of the spec asked for a win-rate and
  match-length comparison on a larger matrix and for the Spider to be slain
  in most of its matches by round 60. At the user's direction the coarse
  check stayed small (40 matches), so it is a sanity check, not a
  measurement at that precision, and it changed no rule or number: no
  error or stall, the same winner in 19 of 20 pairs, and a Spider that the
  Normal AI mostly leaves alone (slain in 1 of its 8 matches, which the
  criterion did not foresee). Its findings and the rarity recommendation
  are in the
  [curiosities check](../validation/RULESET_7_CURIOSITIES_CHECK.md).
- **Superseded spec text:** its former status ("design spec", an overlay at
  `7r31` with the Dwarf and Mind Control overlays pending), the `7rNN`
  identities (`7r35` and `7r36`), the weights without the Monster of its
  section 17 (`7r35` only), the "LEGACY markers first" plan of its section
  12.2 (the production art is wired into the live look; the code markers
  remain in the Classic and legacy looks), its open questions (the root's
  defaults stand: 12 HP, a Giant Spider, the count table as written), and
  its tuning bounds, which the check did not use.

**Resolved by a code change** (`pulp_wars-7g3.9`):

- **An inexact Wail preview without a flag (resolved).** The Ice Folk overlay's section
  11 says every preview equals its resolution except one flagged
  `hiddenBlizzardPossible` or `touchesUnexplored`, and the Dwarf overlay's
  section 14 says every Dwarf-related preview is exact (a Wail reads Dig In,
  its section 13.2). The canonical Wail (`wailTargetsV7`) reads each
  target's cover and fortification with the combat helpers, Snow cover and
  Dig In included, but the public `previewWailV7` (`publicWailTargetsV7`)
  reads cover only from Forest and Mountain and fortification only from the
  view tile's `fortificationLevel` (Walls and Field Defense in the target's
  own territory). So for an Ice Folk target with Snow cover, and for a
  dug-in Dwarf Hammerer or Steam Mole, the preview shows more damage than
  the Wail deals (a fresh Banshee on a fresh dug-in Hammerer, or on a fresh
  Yeti on its Snow: preview 2, Wail 1), with no flag. The Ice Folk engine bead recorded
  a narrower form of this (overlay section 19.3 note 6: a hidden Witch's
  Blizzard), and the Ice Folk fold stated it as a reading of the viewer's
  `snow` flags, which the code does not do; this fold measured both cases
  against the code. `pulp_wars-7g3.9` resolved it: the preview now computes
  each target with the reducer's own `wailTargetV7` from public facts (Snow
  cover and Dig In included) and flags a target a hidden Witch's Blizzard
  could change with `hiddenBlizzardPossible`; the Wail itself is unchanged
  ([section 17.9](#179-wail)).

**Ice Folk overlay against the code** (`pulp_wars-7g3.8`; resolved by
stating the code's behavior):

- **Numbers.** The `7r27` Yeti (9 HP, Defense 1.5) replaces the contract's
  10 and 2, which the overlay keeps in its tuning bounds. The overlay's
  worked examples (section 5.6), per-unit analysis (section 9), and
  interaction examples (section 10) were computed with that Yeti and with
  10-HP Human Fighters, Raiders, and Marksmen, 15-HP Guards, and a 12-HP
  Caveman; the examples here are recomputed at current HP. The overlay's
  values that change are: a Caveman (10 HP) is no longer shattered by a
  second Yeti hit (it dies by plain damage), a charging Sled or a
  Sabretooth no longer shatters a full-HP Fighter (12 HP) without Brittle,
  the overlay's Walled-Guard example ends without a Shatter (two Mammoth
  hits leave the 17-HP Guard at 9, a Yeti's 4 leaves it at 5, and its
  retaliation of 13 kills the Yeti), a
  Lich on a Yeti on Snow deals 8 (halved 4; the overlay has 7), a Goblin
  with two helpers deals a Yeti 11 in the open and 10 on Snow (the overlay
  has 10 and 8), a Vampire deals a Yeti on Snow 8 (the overlay has 7), and
  a full-power Tripod deals a Yeti in its Witch's Blizzard 6 (the overlay
  has 5). Overlay section 19.1 and its tests (19.3 note 10) already record
  the HP substitution.
- **The Ice Witch always has Snow cover** unless she is fortified: her own
  tile is in her Blizzard, so it is Snow. The overlay's section 10.1 example
  "a Vampire deals a Witch 10" is the open-ground value; she takes 9.
- **Setup.** The overlay's section 2.2 ("every combination is legal") and
  section 13.1 ("default all Human") are superseded by the one faction per
  seat rule of `7r29` (`DUPLICATE_FACTION`, distinct defaults Human, Undead,
  Goblin, Dinosaur; [section 2.1](#21-match-setup)); a mirror match, such as
  the overlay's `II` balance pairing, is legal only in headless and test
  setups with `allowDuplicateFactions`. The setup offers seven factions,
  the Dwarves included.
- **Normal AI.** The overlay's section 12 asks for Scouting as the free
  opening technology (Drill with a hostile unit in sight); the policy keeps
  the ordinary opener scorer, as the same section's last paragraph allows,
  and puts Drill and Scouting first in its research plan. Its Goblin Kaboom rule is not
  implemented, and Glide in the city-threat test and Rockfall from a

- **Projection.** `UNITS_FROZEN` (`UNITS_CHILLED` before

  owns a target (overlay section 6.5); its results are the units the viewer
  owns or can see before or after the command.
- **Readings of the engine bead** (overlay section 19.3), stated in this
  document: the `snow` and `blizzard` tile flags are optional in the
  `PlayerTileViewV7` type and always set on an explored tile; a Move that

  `iceFolk.inBlizzard` is the Blizzard the reader knows of; only `PLANTED`

- **Superseded overlay text:** its status line and section 15 ("no bead of

**Dwarf overlay against the code** (`pulp_wars-78i.8`; resolved by stating
the code's behavior):

- **Numbers.** The `7r31` bomb (5, and 6 with Dive) replaces the root's

- **Normal AI.** The overlay's section 15 asks for Scouting as the free

  [section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary)).

## 26. Cultist faction rules

The Cultists of the Ancient Ones are **a terrible bargain**: since the Cult
redesign **the summons are their army and the robed cultists the
casters**, frail bodies of 7 HP (the Idol Bearer, the warden, excepted)
who channel, chant, and hold, and what they buy is stronger than anything
else in the game. Units are turned into **Favour** (a Sacrifice, a
Seizure, an Offering, a bound daemon's kill, a Summoner's trickle), up to
30, and Favour into **daemons** (the Imp, the Horror, the Gibbering Mass,
and the Herald, which is far above every other unit), and every daemon
must be **channelled** by cultists every turn (an Imp's Brood and a Mass's
Doorstep excepted) or it is **Unbound**: it belongs to nobody and attacks
a cultist close by first, then anyone near it. They are strong for as long as the channel holds and with a
Herald on the board; they are weak wherever an enemy can hurt, move, or put
a status on the cultists that hold a daemon or chant a rite, which any
faction can do. Every rule in this section applies only to units of the
Cult kind, to a Cult seat, or to the units the Cult summons, except where a
rule names its target (a frog, a swapped unit, a Cowed city, a unit a
Tentacle holds). In a match without a Cult seat
the `cult` block is empty (`favour`, `strands`, `grips`, `rituals`,
`cowed`, `frogs`, `hexCooldowns`, `tentacles`), no
Cult command is offered or accepted, and no unit carries `summoned`. Each
rule resolves through the unit's kind's registration (`FACTION_RULES_V7`,
`CULT_ROLE_RULES_V7`, `CULT_ROLE_MECHANICS_V7`,
`CULT_SUMMONED_ROLE_RULES_V7`) and the helpers of `src/engine/v7/cult.ts`,
`cult-channel.ts`, `cult-unbound.ts`, `cult-rituals.ts`, `cult-hexes.ts`,
and `cult-tricks.ts`. The other eight factions keep every ability against
the Cult, with the rulings of
[section 26.14](#2614-interactions-with-other-rules).

Design, the reasons for every rule, the validation on paper, and the notes
of each implementation step: [the Cultists spec](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md),
kept as the design record, and [the Cult redesign](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md)
(approved by the user on 2026-10-16, and built: its steps folded in here
as they landed, and `pulp_wars-mch9.47` checked the whole section against
the code at `7r91`; `7r85`, `pulp_wars-mch9.31`: the roster, the robed casters'
numbers, the vacant slots, the Summoner's Tentacle, starting Favour, and
Martyr and Pick Me! removed; `pulp_wars-mch9.34`: Star-fall alone with
Join the chant, and Switcheroo at 4; `pulp_wars-mch9.35`: every daemon
advances after a kill, bound or Unbound, and the Unbound target order;
`pulp_wars-mch9.32`: the Favour cap of 30, the Offering's 6, the prices 4
and 18, the Summoners' trickle, and the Herald's Hunger;
`pulp_wars-mch9.33`: the Idol Bearer's Behold! as the warden's lasting
aura, with the shield wall and Awestruck; `pulp_wars-mch9.36`: the Imp,
with Brood and Swarm; `pulp_wars-mch9.37`: the Gibbering Mass, with
Doorstep and Drag); where it
differs from this section, this
section is the rule, and the differences the fold found are listed in
[its section 22](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md#22-fold-notes-pulp_wars-mch921), and
those of the redesign in
[its section 23](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md#23-the-cult-redesign-folded-pulp_wars-mch947)
and [the redesign's section 19](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md#19-as-built). The
Cult's numbers were checked against the engine code at
`pulp-wars-poc-7r78` (`pulp_wars-mch9.21`) and at `pulp-wars-poc-7r91`
(`pulp_wars-mch9.47`). The Cultists are an ordinary
faction offered in every setup. (This section follows the revision history
and the known discrepancies, and is numbered 26, so that the links to
sections 24 and 25 from every other document still hold.)

**The variance rules.** Seven design rules of the faction bind every later
balance, tuning, and AI pass
([the spec, section 2](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md#2-the-variance-rules); the
user, 2026-10-09). In short: the Herald is truly overpowered and is never
brought nearer to a giant; the daemons are paid for by Favour and by the
channel, never by weaker numbers; there is no cap on daemons, and Favour
is capped at 30 (the Cult redesign's revision of rule 3, by the user's
approval, `pulp_wars-mch9.32`; a bound Herald's Hunger is an upkeep paid by
a winning and a losing Cult alike, no catch-up rule);
a failure is never softened (nothing is refunded, an Unbound daemon never
fades, there is no way to dismiss one); nothing helps a Cult that is
losing or slows one that is winning; the only fairness rule is that the
counterplay is on the board for everyone (the channellers and the
chanters); and control is never decided by a random draw. A later pass may
change a number only to restore counterplay that was shown to be missing.

### 26.1 Roles, robed cultists, and labels

| Mechanical role | Cult unit           | Its own thing                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FIGHTER`       | Initiate            | Pamphlets; channels; the start unit and the Militia (two of them)       |
| `GUARD`         | Idol Bearer         | Behold! (the warden's aura); channels                                   |
| `RAIDER`        | Familiar            | Switcheroo; Charge; the Scouts unit and the treasure unit               |
| `MARKSMAN`      | Hexer               | Ribbit; channels                                                        |
| `CAPTAIN`       | Summoner            | Sacrifice, Seize, Summon, Tentacle; leads the Great Summoning; channels |
| `CATAPULT`      | Stargazer           | no attack of its own; leads Star-fall; channels                         |
| `KNIGHT`        | (vacant)            | the Caller retired (`7r85`); nothing fields the role                    |
| `SWORDSMAN`     | (vacant)            | the Chosen retired (`7r85`); nothing fields the role                    |
| `JUGGERNAUT`    | Thing in the Cellar | Anchor; the giant reward                                                |
| `PATROL_BOAT`   | Patrol Boat         | the Human boat                                                          |
| `BATTLESHIP`    | Battleship          | the Human boat                                                          |
| `SUBMARINE`     | Submarine           | the Human boat                                                          |

Summoned, never trained, hired, found, or rewarded:

| Summoned unit  | From                                               | Its own thing                                                                           |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Imp            | a Summoner's Summon, alone, 2 Favour               | a daemon, Control 1; Brood; Swarm; never captures                                       |
| Horror         | a Summoner's Summon, helped, 4 Favour              | a daemon, Control 1; Boo!                                                               |
| Gibbering Mass | a Summoner's Summon, helped, 5 Favour (Metallurgy) | a daemon, Control 1 (none on its Doorstep); Drag; immovable; never advances or captures |
| Herald         | the Great Summoning, 18 Favour                     | a daemon, Control 3; Ravage, Unstoppable, Proclaim                                      |
| Tentacle       | a Summoner's Tentacle                              | nobody's from birth; slaps and Grabs; sinks                                             |

A **Cult unit** is a unit whose kind is `CULT`; a **Cult seat** is a player
whose faction is `CULT`. A **robed cultist** is one of the five trained
land units other than the Familiar (Initiate, Idol Bearer, Hexer, Summoner,
Stargazer; role mechanic `robed`), in land form. Only a
robed cultist channels, chants in a ritual, helps a summoning, or holds
down a Seizure. A **daemon** is an Imp (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`), a Horror,
a Gibbering Mass (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`), or a Herald; a **summoned unit**
is a daemon or a Tentacle (the unit key
`summoned`). The stats are in
[section 11](#11-unit-roster) and the technology in
[section 6.2](#62-technology-tree).

A Cult seat starts with one Initiate. Its Militia reward is **two
Initiates** (`MILITIA_FIGHTERS_V7`), its Scouts reward a Familiar, its
giant reward the Thing in the Cellar at every level from 5, and its
treasure unit a Familiar ([section 4.8](#48-city-rewards)). No reward,
chest, or Market hire ever gives Favour or a daemon. Faction rules:
`restless` false, `cityCapacityBonus` 0, `gangUpMaximum` 0,
`treasureUnitRole` `RAIDER`, `snow` false. No Cult unit builds Field
Defense, and the Summoner has neither Rally nor Tend Wounded.

**The vacant slots (`7r85`).** The registry needs every role in every
faction's table, so the Cult's `KNIGHT` and `SWORDSMAN` stay registered
(`CULT_VACANT_ROLES_V7`) with no cost, no technology, no ability, and the
tactical role the registry needs, but no technology, reward, chest, hire,
Showcase, mission, or lab places a unit of either: one helper,
`factionFieldsRoleV7`, answers whether a faction fields a role (false for
these two and for the Ice Folk ships), and every reader that lists roles
reads it (training, the Showcase, the Gallery's empty cells, mission
validation). Chivalry (shown as **Tentacles**) gives the Summoner its
Tentacle, and Metallurgy (shown as **Gibbering Masses**) keeps the Forge
and Arms Industry and, since `pulp_wars-mch9.37`, lets the Summoner
summon a Gibbering Mass (the capability `summonMass`).

**Needs a Cult seat.** A mind-controlled Cult unit keeps the tricks that
belong to the unit (Behold!, Ribbit, Switcheroo, Pamphlets) and
loses everything that calls on the Ancient Ones: it has no Sacrifice,
Seize, Summon, Channel, Anchor, Star-fall, or Tentacle, it leads and chants
in no ritual (`MIND_CONTROLLED_LOST_ABILITIES_V7`).

### 26.2 Favour

"The Ancient Ones pay in Favour, up to 30. Feed them, and summon."

Every Cult seat has **Favour**: a whole number, **2 at the start** of a
match (`CULT_STARTING_FAVOUR_V7`, `7r85`; 0 before; a mission seat's own
`favour` replaces it, clamped to the cap), **at most 30**
(`FAVOUR_CAP_V7`, the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.32`; uncapped
before), and **public** (every player sees every Cult seat's Favour). Any
gain above the cap is **lost**: the seat banks up to 30 and the rest is
the `forfeited` part of its `FAVOUR_GAINED`; a gain at the cap is still
legal and banks nothing (a Seizure at 30 still kills its victim). It is
not Coins: it is never bought or traded, and it is spent only on
summoning and on a Herald's Hunger. It is not a Score factor (Favour lost
to the cap or to Hunger neither). An eliminated seat's Favour is gone.

| Source                        | What happens                                                                                       | Favour                                |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Sacrifice                     | A Summoner removes an own unit beside it                                                           | the unit's value                      |
| Seize                         | A Summoner removes a broken living enemy beside it that a second cultist holds down                | twice its value                       |
| Offering                      | A city gives up 2 population                                                                       | 6 (3 before `pulp_wars-mch9.32`)      |
| A bound daemon's kill         | An Imp, Horror, Mass, or Herald the seat commands kills a hostile unit that is not a summoned unit | the victim's value                    |
| Offering to the Deep (`7r98`) | With Offerings to the Deep, a Cult ship's attack or retaliation kills a hostile unit afloat        | half the victim's value, rounded down |
| Consumed                      | The unit on the Great Summoning's mark is eaten when the Herald arrives                            | as a Sacrifice or a Seizure           |
| The trickle                   | At the check, each own Summoner whose strand held, for a daemon still bound (section 26.5)         | 1 each                                |

| Spent on                                        | Favour |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -----: |
| Summon an Imp (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`)             |      2 |
| Summon a Horror                                 |      4 |
| Summon a Gibbering Mass (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`)   |      5 |
| Begin the Great Summoning (never refunded)      |     18 |
| Hunger: each bound Herald, at each check (26.5) |      2 |

(The prices were 5 and 20 before `pulp_wars-mch9.32`.)

A unit's **value** is the Score's unit value
([section 3.1](#31-score-play-modes-and-stars)): the printed cost of its
role under its kind (an Initiate 2, a Knight 9), 12 for a reward giant, a
