neutral monster its bounty (the Giant Spider 10), and a summoned unit its
own value (an Imp 2, a Horror 6, a Gibbering Mass 6, the Herald 24, a
Tentacle 0). A free unit is worth
its role, and Arms Industry lowers a price, never a value.

### 26.3 Sacrifice, Seize, and the Offering

**Sacrifice.** "The Summoner offers a unit beside it to the Ancient Ones:
it is gone, and you gain its value in Favour." A primary action of a
Summoner in land form, which may follow its Move. The victim is an own unit
in land form on one of the eight tiles around the Summoner, of any role
(the Thing in the Cellar pays 12; another Summoner may be offered), hurt,
Frozen, or exhausted or not; never a daemon, a mind-controlled unit, an
Egg, or a Plagued or Bitten unit (so a Sacrifice never dodges a bite). The
victim is removed: nobody gets a kill, and it leaves no Grave, rising,
death blast, Crumbs, Plunder, or growth; its unit slot is free. In the
Score it is no Loss (like Disband), it lowers the Army, and it ends a
flawless game. There is no limit but the Summoner's one action a turn; the
last unit of a city may be offered.

**Seize.** "Two cultists hold down a broken enemy; the Summoner offers it.
Twice its value in Favour." A primary action of a Summoner in land form,
which may follow its Move. The victim is a hostile unit in land form on one
of the eight tiles around the Summoner that the actor sees, and it must be:

- **living** (not of the Undead kind, not a construct, not a summoned
  unit), a player's unit, not a reward giant, and not a two-slot unit;
- **broken**: at **5 HP or less** (a Shield does not count), or a **frog**
  at **half its maximum HP or less** ([section 26.12](#2612-hexes-and-tricks));
- **held**: another robed cultist of the actor stands on one of the eight
  tiles around the victim. The holder spends nothing and may have acted.

The victim dies as a kill of the Summoner (its kill count, Promotion,
Slayer, the Score's Kills; a Loss for the victim's seat), and leaves no
Grave, rising, death blast, Crumbs, or Plunder. A Seized Brain releases the
unit it controls. The seat gains twice the victim's value: a Fighter 4, a
Guard 6, a Raider 8, a Champion 12, a Knight 18.

**Offering.** "A city gives up 2 population to the Ancient Ones for 6
Favour." The city action of an own city, with **Harvest Rites** (the
Cult's Farming). The city is level 2 or more, not besieged and not Cowed,
has no reward waiting to be chosen, and has **2 population or more**. Its
population drops by 2 for good (the city's `offeredPopulation`, subtracted
in the population of [section 4.2](#42-population-growth-and-levels)), so
it is 2 further from its next level; a level is never lost and a reward
never repeats. What a city gave up stays with the city through a capture.

### 26.4 Daemons, and Summon

A daemon is a land unit of a Cult seat with these rules of its own:

- **Not living.** No Plague, bite, Infect, Wail, Seizure, or Boo! takes it;
  it is immune to Swallow (a Brain takes it since `7r99`); it leaves no Grave.
- **It never heals:** no recovery, Windmill, Fountain of Youth, or Wishing
  Well, and it tosses no Coin.
- **It belongs to no city.** It has no home city and fills no unit slot,
  also after a capture it makes. It is never promoted (also not at a
  Shrine), disbanded, or Sacrificed, and it is never a veteran.
- **It strides.** Forest and Mountain neither stop nor refuse it, with or
  without Engineering. It never enters water and never embarks. Like a
  Martian walker it is never fortified and takes no cover.
- **While bound** it attacks and **captures** like any land unit, except
  the Imp and the Gibbering Mass (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`), which **never
  capture** (on a hostile center each besieges, as any unit does). A Horror
  and an Imp
  advance after a kill and may Pillage; so does the Herald since the Cult
  redesign (`pulp_wars-mch9.35`; it never advanced before); the Gibbering
  Mass never advances. An advance can
  carry a daemon more than 3 tiles from its channellers, which breaks it at
  the next check: the player chooses the kill knowing it.
- **Its kills feed.** A kill by a bound daemon's attack or retaliation of a
  hostile unit pays its seat the victim's value in Favour, and a neutral
  monster's bounty Coins as to anyone. A summoned unit of any seat, bound
  or Unbound, pays nothing.
- **Its value** (Imp 2, Horror 6, Gibbering Mass 6, Herald 24) is in its
  seat's Army while the seat commands it, and is what its kill is worth.

**Summon** (`SUMMON`, naming the daemon: `IMP`, `HORROR`, or `MASS`).
Since the Cult redesign (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`, `pulp_wars-mch9.37`) a
Summoner calls one of three daemons; the Imp is the Summoner's alone, the
Horror and the Gibbering Mass need a helper, and the Mass needs
**Gibbering Masses** (the Cult's Metallurgy; refused `SUMMON_NOT_LEGAL`
reason `TECHNOLOGY` without it, checked through the Summoner's own tree).
Each is a primary action of a Summoner in land form, which may follow its
Move, on the same tiles, and each summoner holds a strand to what it
called.

**Summon an Imp** (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`). "The Summoner alone summons an
Imp for 2 Favour and channels it this turn." No helper: the command names
none. It appears on a tile as a Horror does (below), at full HP, and cannot
act until the next turn; the Summoner holds one strand to it and has used
its action. Every Cult seat starts with 2 Favour, so its first Summoner can
summon an Imp the turn it is trained.

**Summon a Horror.** "The Summoner and a cultist beside it summon a Horror
for 4 Favour. Both channel it this turn." A primary action of a Summoner in
land form, which may follow its Move. It needs a **helper**: another own
robed cultist on one of the eight tiles around the Summoner that has not
used its action (it may have moved) and is neither Frozen nor a frog. The
Horror appears on a tile next to the Summoner that the seat has explored:
land, never water, ice, or a settlement center, with no unit, mound,
Barricade, treasure chest, or curiosity, and not in an ally's territory (a
Mountain is fine). It stands there at full HP and cannot act until the next
turn. The Summoner and the helper each hold a strand to it and have used
their actions. There is no limit: a Summoner may summon every turn it has a
helper and 4 Favour.

The Horror: 18 HP, Attack 4, Defense 2, Move 2, Sight 1. A bound Horror can
be pushed, knocked back, Stuck, and Frozen like an ordinary unit.

**The Imp** (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`): 6 HP, Attack 2, Defense 1, Move 3,
Range 1, Sight 1, worth 2, Control 1; its stored mechanical role is
`RAIDER` (no rule of it reads the role: it has no zone-of-control slip, no
Charge, and no Escape). Like a Horror it can be pushed, knocked back,
Stuck, and Frozen. Its own rules:

- **Brood.** "One strand holds an Imp and the Imps beside it, three at
  most." At the check a holding strand to an Imp also holds up to two
  other own bound Imps beside it
  ([section 26.5](#265-the-channel-strands-and-the-check)).
- **Swarm.** "A unit beside two or more of your Imps cannot strike back at
  them." When a bound Imp attacks a unit that has, at that moment, two or
  more bound Imps of the attacker's seat on the eight tiles around it (the
  attacker counted), the defender does not retaliate (the combat preview's
  `noRetaliationReason` `SWARMED`). Only an Imp's attack goes unanswered;
  every other attacker meets retaliation as usual, and an Unbound Imp has
  no Swarm. A lone Imp attacking a Fighter deals 5 and takes 5; with a
  second Imp beside the Fighter it takes nothing.
- **It never captures**, so it takes no village and no city (a 2-Favour
  unit of Move 3 that captured would replace the Initiate's Pamphlets).

**Summon a Gibbering Mass** (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`). "The Summoner and a
cultist beside it summon a Gibbering Mass for 5 Favour." As a Horror's
summoning, with the same helper and tiles, for **5 Favour**
(`FAVOUR_SPENT` purpose `SUMMON_MASS`; `DAEMON_SUMMONED` role `MASS`, and
the two `STRAND_FORMED`), with Gibbering Masses.

**The Gibbering Mass** (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`): 30 HP, Attack 2, Defense 3,
Move 1, Range 1, Sight 1, worth 6, Control 1; its stored mechanical role is
`GUARD` (no rule of it reads the role: it is not the Human Guard, so no
Open to ranged; it may attack after its Move). A Fighter attacking it deals
4 and takes 8; a Knight deals 10 and takes 6. Its own rules:

- **Doorstep.** "On your doorstep it needs no strand." At the check a bound
  Mass short of its Control by its strands stays bound when it stands **on
  or beside an own city center** (a city, never a village) or **beside an
  own Idol Bearer whose idol stands**
  ([section 26.11](#2611-behold-anchor-and-boo)); elsewhere it needs 1
  strand like a Horror ([section 26.5](#265-the-channel-strands-and-the-check)).
- **Drag.** "Enemies beside it can move only one tile." A land-form unit of
  a player hostile to the Mass's owner (flyers included) that **begins a
  Move** on one of the eight tiles around a Gibbering Mass may move **one
  tile** in that Move: one step, no hop (`MASS_DRAG_TILES_V7`; a longer
  path is refused with the movement reason `DRAGGED`, and the offered Moves
  and the movement query honour it). As for Stuck, an ice slide is no step.
  It is no status and needs no state: it is read from the board when the
  Move begins, so it limits an Escape, an Overrun step, and a Bat Escape
  too, and never an advance after a kill, a shove, a swap, a pull, or a
  Boo!. An Unbound Mass drags every player's units.
- **Immovable.** Nothing shoves, swaps, pulls, bounces, Boos, or knocks it
  back (role mechanic `immovable`); a Crushing Shove crushes it, as damage,
  as it does the Herald. Statuses stick to it (it can be Frozen or Stuck),
  and no summon is a frog's target.
- **It never advances after a kill and never captures.** It may stand on
  an own center (a daemon fills no slot), its natural post; on a hostile
  center it besieges, as any unit does.

### 26.5 The Channel, strands, and the check

**Channel.** "A cultist channels a daemon within 3 tiles. At the start of
your turn each daemon needs as many unbroken strands as its Control, or it
is Unbound." A primary action of a robed cultist, which may follow its Move
(also for the Idol Bearer and the Stargazer, which may not attack after
one). The daemon is an own daemon within 3 tiles, or an Unbound one
([section 26.6](#266-unbound-the-rampage-furious-and-bind-again)). The
cultist holds a **strand** to it until the next check. A cultist holds one
strand a turn; a daemon may hold any number. A cultist that has channelled
cannot move afterwards.

**Control** is the number of strands a daemon needs: an Imp **1**, a
Horror **1**, a Gibbering Mass **1** (none on its Doorstep,
`pulp_wars-mch9.37`), the Herald **3**.

**Disrupted.** One rule decides when a strand breaks, a chanter leaves a
ritual, and a Thing's grip fails. After every command,
and inside a Start Turn after Plague, each such unit is compared with what
it was before. It is disrupted when:

- it **lost Hit Points**, from any source (an attack, a retaliation, a
  splash, a blast, a bomb, Plague, a crush, a star, a slap);
- it **stands on another tile** and the command was not its own (a Push, a
  Knockback, a Tractor Beam, a Bounce, a Boo!, a Switcheroo, a gate's
  shove, a reward unit taking its center);
- it has a **status it did not have**: Plagued, Bitten, Frozen, Stuck,
  Toothache, Splatted, a frog, or one of the marks a hit leaves (Terror,
  the hunted mark, the bombed mark, Cracked);
- it has **another owner**; or
- it is **no longer on the board in land form** (a death, a Sacrifice, a
  Seizure, a Swallow, an embarkation).

Who caused it does not matter: the Cult's own Boo!, its own Star-fall, and
its own daemon's kill of an exploding unit beside a channeller disrupt like
an enemy's act. A unit that gains Hit Points is not disrupted. A unit's own
states (a Shield, Cooling, Sugar Rush and the Crash, Berserk) are no
status. A disrupted cultist's strand breaks at once.

**Candlelit.** Every unit on a tile a player has explored is visible to
that player ([section 15](#15-fog-and-observation)), so a channeller, a
chanter, and a gripping Thing are seen, and can be targeted, by everyone who
has explored their tiles. The strands, the Control of every visible daemon
and the strands it holds, the grips, every standing idol, and the rituals
are public too: the counterplay is always on the board.

**The check** runs at the Cult seat's Start Turn, after Plague and its
chains ([section 26.13](#2613-resolution-order)). For each of the seat's
bound daemons, in unit-ID order, its **holding strands** are counted: the
strands whose cultist is still on the board as the seat's own robed
cultist, within 3 tiles of the daemon **now**. Each counts 1, or 3 under a
holding Anchor grip ([section 26.11](#2611-behold-anchor-and-boo)). With
at least its Control the daemon stays bound; an Imp short of it may be
held by a neighbour's **Brood** (below), and a Gibbering Mass short of it
by its **Doorstep** (below); otherwise it is **Unbound**
at once (`DAEMON_UNBOUND` reason `STRANDS`).

**Brood** (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`). An Imp short of its Control by its own
holding strands stays bound when an own bound Imp on one of the eight
tiles around it is held by **its own** holding strands and has held fewer
than **two** others this check (`IMP_BROOD_SIZE_V7`); among several such
neighbours the one with the lowest unit ID lends. The Imps are taken in
unit-ID order like every daemon, so a strand's two are the lowest IDs that
ask. An Imp held by its own strand counts that first and takes no Brood; a
held Imp never lends its Brood on (a Brood is one Imp and its neighbours,
not a chain); a Bind again takes one Imp per Channel (no Brood for a bind);
a grip on an Imp's channeller changes nothing. The channellers of the
lending Imp count as having held the Imp they held for it (the trickle).
The view names the lender of each Imp a Brood holds (`broodOf` of its
`cult.daemons` entry), so such an Imp is not short: no eye mark, no End
Turn question.

**Doorstep** (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`). A Gibbering Mass short of its Control
by its own holding strands stays bound when it stands on or beside an own
city center, or beside an own Idol Bearer whose idol stands, as the board
stands at its check (`massOnDoorstepV7`). Its strands count first: a
strand to a Mass on its Doorstep is legal and simply unneeded, and a
Summoner whose strand holds it there still pays the trickle; a Mass held
by its Doorstep alone has no holder and pays none. An Idol Bearer with a
status of the disruption rule has its idol down, so a frogged or Frozen
bearer holds nothing (a frog lasts until the end of its owner's next turn,
so one made in another seat's turn stands at the check). The view marks a
Mass on its Doorstep (`doorstep` of its `cult.daemons` entry), so it is not
short: no eye mark, no End Turn question. A fresh daemon is checked at
the first Start Turn after it appears, with the strands of its summoning.
What one break does is felt by the next: a rampage that hurts, moves, or
kills a channeller breaks that strand before the next daemon is checked.

**The trickle** (the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.32`). "A Summoner at
work on the channel pays 1 Favour." After every daemon is checked, each
own Summoner (a unit with Summon) whose strand **held** at its daemon's
check, for a daemon that is **still bound** now, and that is still on the
board as the seat's own, pays the seat **1 Favour**: one `FAVOUR_GAINED`
source `TRICKLE` for them all, up to the cap. One Summoner pays at most 1
a turn, whatever it held; a strand that did not hold, or held a daemon
that broke loose, pays nothing.

**Hunger** (`pulp_wars-mch9.32`). "The Herald hungers: 2 Favour each turn,
or it breaks loose." After the trickle, the seat pays **2 Favour** for each
of its still bound Heralds, in unit-ID order (`FAVOUR_SPENT` purpose
`HUNGER`). A Herald whose 2 cannot be paid (the seat has fewer than 2
left) is **Unbound** at once, as a daemon short of strands is
(`DAEMON_UNBOUND` reason `HUNGER`, with the strands it held): it rampages
at once and is Furious for the turn. Nothing is refunded. A Herald that
arrives at a Start Turn (its ritual completes after the check) first pays
at the next one. `heraldHungerDueV7` gives what a seat's Heralds will eat
at its next check.

Then every strand and grip of the seat is cleared, and the seat must
channel again this turn.

Ending a turn with a daemon short of its Control is legal. The interface
asks once ("The Horror will be Unbound.") and nothing stops the choice.

### 26.6 Unbound, the rampage, Furious, and Bind again

"An Unbound daemon belongs to nobody. It goes for a cultist within 2 first,
then anyone near it, friend or foe, at once and after every round."

**Unbound.** A daemon that fails its check belongs to the neutral owner,
like the Giant Spider ([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)), and is shown as
an "Unbound Imp", "Unbound Horror", "Unbound Gibbering Mass", or "Unbound
Herald" (an Unbound Imp is the neutral breed `IMP`, with no Brood and no
Swarm; an Unbound Mass the breed `MASS`, which still Drags every player's
units, never advances, and has no Doorstep). It keeps its Hit Points, its
numbers, and its kills, and loses every status and every strand. As a
neutral unit it only attacks: it never captures, besieges, Boos, or
Proclaims, it sees nothing, no status, shove, Mind Control, or Swallow
takes it, and it pays no bounty. **It never fades**: it stays until it is
killed or bound again. In the Score it is no Loss; it leaves its seat's
Army, and the seat's game is no longer flawless.

**The rampage** happens at the check that lets the daemon loose, and then
in every neutral turn after a round, in unit-ID order with the other
neutral units:

1. **The target** (the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.35`; the nearest unit
   of any player until `7r87`) is chosen by four steps, distances measured
   in tiles in any direction, its **reach** being its Move + 1 (Imp 4,
   Horror 3, Gibbering Mass 2, Herald 3). The candidates are units of any player (an Egg, and a daemon
   another seat commands, included); never a neutral unit, a ship or an
   embarked unit, or a burrowed unit.
   1. **A cultist within 2:** the nearest robed cultist of any Cult seat
      within 2 tiles.
   2. **Anyone in reach:** otherwise the nearest unit within its reach that
      is not a summon (no daemon of any seat).
   3. **A summon in reach:** otherwise the nearest bound daemon within its
      reach.
   4. **Walk on:** otherwise the nearest unit on the board that is not a
      summon (a summon only when there is no other), at any distance.
      A tie inside a step goes to a unit of **the seat that summoned it**,
      then to the fewest Hit Points, then to the lowest unit ID. It is chosen
      whether or not anyone sees it. So a daemon never walks past a soldier in
      its reach to bite a summon beside it, and never hunts a cultist across
      the map: beyond 2 tiles a cultist is just anyone.
2. **The walk.** The daemon walks up to its Move toward a tile next to the
   target by a shortest way over Grass, Forest, and Mountain, and stops as
   soon as it stands beside it. It never steps onto water, ice, a Rift, a
   settlement center, a curiosity tile, a treasure chest, or a tile with a
   unit, a mound, or a Barricade. **Zones of control, Roads, Snow, and
   terrain neither stop nor slow it.** With no way to the target it goes as
   near as it can.
3. **The attack.** If it ends beside its target it attacks it: an ordinary
   attack with retaliation. **After a kill it advances** onto the victim's
   tile (`pulp_wars-mch9.35`; never a Gibbering Mass), unless that tile is one its walk never
   enters (water, ice, a Rift, a settlement center, a curiosity tile, a
   treasure chest, a mound or a Barricade); then it stays. A Herald then
   attacks a second time, from where it stands, a unit beside it chosen by
   steps 1 to 3 among its neighbours (a cultist beside it first, then any
   non-summon, then a summon), by the same ties (which may be the same
   unit), and its attacks still ignore fortification. A daemon that does
   not end beside its target attacks nobody.

Its kills are credited to nobody and pay no Favour. A daemon Unbound while it stands on
a city center besieges nothing from that moment and leaves at its first
step. Killing an Unbound daemon is an ordinary kill at its value (Imp 2,
Horror 6, Gibbering Mass 6, Herald 24) with no bounty Coins, except that the seat that summoned it gets
no Kills in the Score for it.

**The eye mark.** Nothing about a rampage is random or hidden: the board
marks the unit each visible Unbound daemon will go for, and the unit each
bound daemon short of its Control would go for if it broke now
(`previewRampageV7`).

**Furious.** A daemon that broke loose in a Cult seat's Start Turn cannot
be channelled until that seat's turn ends. So it rampages twice, at the
check and after the round, before its seat can bind it again.

**Bind again.** "Channel an Unbound daemon with enough cultists in one turn
and it is yours again." A Channel may name an Unbound daemon the actor
sees, within 3 tiles, that is not Furious. The moment the acting seat's
strands on it this turn (each 1, or 3 under a grip) reach its Control, it
is bound to that seat: it cannot act until the seat's next turn, and those
strands count for the next check. Fewer strands change nothing. Any Cult
seat may bind any Unbound daemon. A player may also let a daemon go on
purpose, by not channelling it.

### 26.7 Rituals

"A leader and the cultists next to it chant. Everyone sees the countdown.
Disrupt the circle and nothing happens."

A ritual has a **leader** and **chanters**. The Great Summoning begins
with its circle: every own robed cultist on the eight tiles around the
leader that has not used its action (it may have moved) and is neither
Frozen nor a frog. Every such unit joins; a player who wants one left out
uses it first. **A Star-fall begins with no chanter** (the Cult redesign,
`pulp_wars-mch9.34`): cultists join it one by one afterwards with **Join
the chant** ([section 26.8](#268-star-fall)). Beginning a ritual spends
the action of the leader and of every chanter, marks a tile, and is
public: the circle, its mark, and its countdown are shown to every player
who sees a participant or has explored the mark.

A ritual **completes at the start of its seat's next turn**, after the
channel check, so the enemy has exactly one turn to answer. A participant
that is disrupted ([section 26.5](#265-the-channel-strands-and-the-check))
leaves the ritual. If the leader leaves, or
fewer chanters remain than the rite needs, the ritual **fizzles** at once
and nothing is refunded.

| Rite                | Technology                       | Leader                         | Chanters needed | Price     | Pay-off                                               |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------: | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Star-fall           | Stargazers (Sawmilling)          | a Stargazer that has not moved |               0 | none      | 6, plus 3 for each chanter, to nine tiles             |
| The Great Summoning | The Stars Are Right (Explosives) | a Summoner (it may have moved) |               3 | 18 Favour | the Herald, channelled by the leader and the chanters |

### 26.8 Star-fall

"Next turn a star lands 2 to 4 tiles away: 6 to everything around it, and
3 more for every cultist who joins the chant."

The Stargazer has no attack of its own and never strikes back. A Stargazer
that has not moved this turn marks any tile its seat has explored that is
2 to 4 tiles away, of any terrain, **alone**: nobody beside it is swept in
(the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.34`; until `7r85` it needed a chanter
and every unacted robed neighbour joined at the begin).

**Join the chant.** `JOIN_CHANT { unitId, leaderUnitId }` is a primary
action of an own robed cultist in land form (a mind-controlled one has
none) standing on one of the eight tiles around a Stargazer that leads a
pending Star-fall of its seat. The joiner has not used its primary action
(it may have moved this turn, and cannot move after joining), is neither
Frozen nor a frog, and is in no ritual already. It becomes a chanter of
that star: Candlelit, public, and **+3** to the star (`CHANT_JOINED`, with
the star's damage after the join). It pays no Favour. A star is pending
from its begin to its seat's next Start Turn, so joining happens in the
casting turn, in any order with the seat's other commands; a cultist may
move up beside the Stargazer and join in the same turn. A chanter beside
two pending stars of its seat names the one it joins.

**Disruption.** A disrupted chanter leaves the ritual (the star loses 3);
a disrupted Stargazer fizzles it (nothing lands, nothing is refunded). A
star **never fizzles for want of chanters**: it needs none.

When the ritual completes, **every unit on the marked tile and the eight
tiles around it**, of every seat and every form (the Cult's own units,
ships, embarked units, Eggs, daemons, giants, and neutral units included; a
burrowed unit is not on the board), takes **6 + 3 for each chanter still in
the ritual**. It is fixed damage: Defense, fortification, cover, Snow, and
the Blizzard do not count; Armoured, Plated, and a Shield apply as for
every fixed hit. Every Field Defense in the area is destroyed and every
Barricade removed. Nobody strikes back.

By chanters: 0 → 6, 1 → 9, 2 → 12, 3 → 15, 4 → 18, 8 → 30 (no cap beyond
the eight tiles around the Stargazer). A chanter that was disrupted before
the star fell makes it weaker by 3. The deaths are resolved like a Thunder
Stomp's: Graves, risings, Crumbs, and death blasts as for a splash death.
The Stargazer is credited with the hostile units it kills, and its seat
with their Score, Plunder, and bounty; an own unit the star kills is a
Loss. A star provokes the Giant
Spider for its Stargazer.

### 26.9 The Great Summoning and the Herald

A Summoner of a seat with **The Stars Are Right**, with three chanters or
more, pays **18 Favour** (20 before `pulp_wars-mch9.32`) and marks a tile next to itself where the Herald
could stand: land the seat has explored, never water, ice, or a settlement
center, with no mound, Barricade, treasure chest, or curiosity, and not in
an ally's territory. The mark may hold a unit.

When the ritual completes, with its leader and at least three chanters
still in it, the unit on the mark decides it:

- **Nobody:** the Herald arrives.
- **A legal victim is consumed**, and the Herald arrives: an own unit a
  Sacrifice could take (for its value), or a hostile unit that is living,
  one-slot, a player's, no reward giant, and at **5 HP or less** (for twice
  its value, as a kill of the leader). Nothing is left of it. A chanter that stands on the mark is
  consumed like any own unit. A frog above 5 HP is not consumed.
- **Any other unit blocks the arrival**, and so does a Barricade or a
  mound put on the mark: a healthy enemy, an ally's unit, a giant, a
  two-slot unit, an Undead or construct unit, a daemon, a neutral unit, an
  Egg, a Plagued or Bitten own unit. The ritual fizzles and the 18 Favour
  is gone. "Stand on the mark" is counterplay any sturdy unit can play. (A
  broken enemy that stands still recovers 2 HP at its own End Turn, so only
  one that walked onto the mark is still broken.)

The Herald stands on the mark at full HP and cannot act that turn. The
leader and every remaining chanter hold a strand to it at once, which is
their whole turn. Its first check is the seat's next Start Turn, so it
needs three of those strands unbroken. The enemy has two turns to answer:
the one after the ritual begins, and the one after the Herald arrives.

**The Herald:** 60 HP, Attack 7, Defense 4, Move 2, Sight 1, Control 3.

- **Ravage.** It makes **two attacks** in each of its seat's turns, after
  its Move or without one, at one target or two. **After a kill it
  advances** onto the victim's tile (the forced advance every unit makes;
  the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.35`: it never advanced before), and
  its second attack, if it has one left, is made from there. It cannot
  move after an attack (the advance is no Move). A Proclaim takes the
  place of one attack.
- **Unstoppable.** Its attacks ignore the defender's fortification (Walls,
  Field Defense, Dig In; cover still counts, and so do Armoured, Plated,
  and Shields) and destroy a Field Defense on the target's tile, bound or
  Unbound. No status sticks to it: it is never Frozen, Stuck, Splatted,
  Cracked, a frog, or given Toothache. Nothing moves it: no Push, Charge!
  push, Knockback, Tractor Beam, Bounce, Boo!, or Switcheroo, and a unit
  that would come through a Dimensional Gate onto it is blocked. A
  Crushing Shove it does not yield to crushes it, as damage. Damage of
  every kind hurts it.
- **Hunger** (`pulp_wars-mch9.32`): at each of its seat's checks after
  the one it arrived at, it eats 2 Favour, or it breaks loose
  ([section 26.5](#265-the-channel-strands-and-the-check)).
- It has none of the giants' signatures, and it is never Seized,
  mind-controlled, or Swallowed.

At full HP it kills a full-HP Fighter, Guard, Knight, Champion, or Captain
with one attack and takes nothing back, and it kills a Juggernaut in one
turn (20 and 20, taking 7). A Knight deals it 9 and takes 9, a Catapult 6,
a Marksman 3. The cheap answer is never the Herald: it is its channellers.

### 26.10 Proclaim and the Cowed city

"'KNEEL!' A hostile city within 3 hides in its cellars: no income and no
city action until its owner's turn ends."

Proclaim is one of the bound Herald's two attacks, before or after the
other and also after its Move. The city is a hostile player's city whose
center the Herald's seat has explored, within 3 tiles, that is not Cowed
already. It touches no unit.

A **Cowed** city pays no income at its owner's next Start Turn (like a
besieged city) and begins that turn with its city action spent: no
training, Egg, hire with the action, Land Grant, or Offering. Harvests and
buildings in its territory are not city actions and go on, and its rewards
still settle. It ends when its owner's turn ends, and at once when the city
changes hands. It may be Cowed again every turn.

### 26.11 Behold!, Anchor, and Boo!

**Behold! (the Idol Bearer, the warden).** "The idol is always raised.
Your units beside it take half from shots, and enemies beside it can attack
only the Idol Bearer." A lasting aura, with no command, no state, and no
event (the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.33`, its
[section 8.1](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md#81-behold-the-idol-bearer-the-warden);
until then a primary action that kept a hurt channeller's strand until its
seat's next check, which is gone, with the `BEHOLD` command, the `idols`
list, and the `IDOL_RAISED` and `IDOL_DROPPED` events).

- **The idol stands** while the Idol Bearer is on the board in land form
  as a player's unit with none of the statuses of the disruption rule
  (Frozen, Stuck, Toothache, Splatted, Plagued, Bitten, a frog, Terror,
  the hunted or bombed mark, Cracked). It needs no action and no
  technology beyond Warding Circles (the unit itself). A hit does not drop
  it; a status does, for as long as the status lasts. A mind-controlled
  Idol Bearer's idol stands for its controller (`idolStandsV7`,
  src/engine/v7/cult-warden.ts).
- **The shield wall.** An attack from **two or more tiles away**
  (`IDOL_SHIELD_MINIMUM_RANGE_V7`) on a unit of the Idol Bearer's seat that
  stands on one of the eight tiles around a standing idol is **halved,
  rounded up**, before Armoured, Plated, and Shields, as the Blizzard's
  halving is ([section 21](#21-ice-folk-faction-rules)); the combat
  preview says so (`idolHalved`). The Idol Bearer is not covered by its own
  idol (another bearer beside it covers it); two idols halve once, and a
  hit the Blizzard halves is not halved again. The retaliation, splash,
  and fixed damage (Star-fall, bombs, blasts, Plague, eruptions) are not
  halved. A Marksman's shot on an Initiate deals it 3 beside a standing
  idol, 6 elsewhere.
- **Awestruck.** A unit of a player hostile to the Idol Bearer's seat that
  stands on one of the eight tiles around a standing idol may make a
  targeted `ATTACK` **only on an Idol Bearer it stands beside** (any of
  them when several); another target is refused `ATTACK_AWESTRUCK` (with
  the bearer's ID) and withheld from the offered commands and the combat
  preview. Ranged units beside an idol are bound too; units two or more
  tiles away are free, and so are area effects, statuses, Mind Control,
  the Tractor Beam, and neutral units. (The retired Chosen's Pick Me! was
  its shouted forerunner.)

**Anchor (the Thing in the Cellar).** "The Thing grips the cultist beside
it: that cultist's strand counts three. Hit that cultist and all three
go." It is not a primary action: once a turn, before or after the Thing's
Move or attack, the Thing grips an own robed cultist next to it **that
holds a strand already**. One grip per Thing, one per cultist. At the check
(and when binding an Unbound daemon) the gripped strand counts **3** while
the Thing stands next to the cultist. The grip fails when the Thing is
moved by anything but its own command, gets a status (also one from its own
attack, such as Toothache from a Jawbreaker), is taken, or leaves the
board; the Thing's own loss of Hit Points never matters. It ends with its
cultist's strand: disrupt the cultist and all three are gone. A grip that
broke may be made again in the same turn. So one Initiate beside a Thing
holds a Herald, at the risk of losing it to one hit. Anchor is the Thing's
signature, and it is a Cult rule of its own
([section 11.1](#111-the-giants-signatures)).

**Boo! (the Horror).** "BOO! Every living unit beside it, friend or foe,
jumps one tile away." A primary action of a bound Horror in place of its
attack, which may follow its Move. Every **living** land-form unit on the
eight tiles around it, **of any owner**, that is not a reward giant, a
two-slot unit, or a neutral unit, jumps one tile directly away from the
Horror, one after the other, when that tile passes the Push conditions
([section 13.4](#134-after-combat)); otherwise it stays. No damage and no
retaliation. Undead units, constructs, daemons, and Eggs are not scared. It
needs somebody to scare. A scared cultist is moved, so it is disrupted (a
Horror never Boos beside its own channellers).

### 26.12 Hexes and tricks

Each is a primary action of its unit, in land form, that may follow its
Move.

**Ribbit (the Hexer).** "Turns an enemy within 2 into a frog until the end
of its next turn." In place of its attack, the Hexer turns a hostile unit
in land form that it sees, within 2 tiles, into a **frog**. Not a reward
giant, a two-slot unit, an Egg, a neutral unit, a summoned unit, or a unit
that is a frog already. The Hexer cannot Ribbit on its owner's next turn
(every second turn at most).

**A frog** lasts until the end of its owner's next turn:

- It may only Move (1 tile, whatever its role), Disembark, Promote,
  Disband, and Wait. It does not attack, capture, or use any ability, it
  helps no summoning, and it chants in no ritual.
- Against an attack it has **Defense 0.5**, no fortification (Walls, Field
  Defense, Dig In), no cover (terrain, Snow, ice), and **no strike back**.
  A Shield, Armoured, Plated, and a Blizzard's halving stay. Area hits and
  fixed damage are unchanged.
- It still blocks its tile and exerts its zone of control.
- A Summoner may **Seize** it at half its maximum HP or less.
- It may be frogged again as soon as it ends. **Tend Wounded** (and the
  Dwarf Repair) and the Candy **Top-Up** cure it, also at full HP, and a
  cured unit may act in that turn.
- A frog is a status: a frogged channeller's strand breaks, a frogged
  chanter leaves its circle, and a frogged Idol Bearer's idol is down.

An Initiate deals a frogged Fighter 5 (7 left) and a frogged Knight 5 (8
left) and takes nothing back (7 each before the Initiate's Attack 1.5 of
`7r85`).

**Switcheroo (the Familiar).** "The toad-cat and a unit within 4 swap
places. Never on a settlement center." With **Familiars** (the Cult's
Scouting; a Familiar from the Scouts reward or a chest swaps only once its
owner has it), the Familiar and one land-form unit of any player that it
sees, within **4** tiles (2 until the Cult redesign, `pulp_wars-mch9.34`;
nothing else changed), swap tiles. Not a reward giant, a two-slot unit, an
Egg, a neutral unit, a summoned unit, or a unit nothing moves (a
Jawbreaker). **Neither tile may be a settlement center**, each unit must be
able to stand where the other stood by the Push conditions, and neither is
put into territory allied to it. A swap is not a Move: it changes neither
unit's turn but for the Familiar's spent action, neither may capture where
it lands this turn, and nothing on either tile is picked up. A swapped
channeller or chanter, of either side, is disrupted. The Familiar cannot
swap on its owner's next turn.

**The Tentacle (the Summoner).** "Up comes a Tentacle within 3. It slaps
and grabs whoever is weakest beside it." With **Tentacles** (the Cult's
Chivalry, the capability `tentacles`; refused `TECHNOLOGY` without it) the
Summoner calls a Tentacle up on a
free tile its seat has explored, 1 to 3 tiles away: land, water, or ice,
never a settlement center or a Rift, with no unit, mound, Barricade,
treasure chest, or curiosity. One Tentacle per Summoner at a time; it
outlives its Summoner. (It was the retired Caller's until `7r85`; the
state still names the unit that called it `callerUnitId`.)

- **The Tentacle** belongs to nobody from birth: 8 HP, Attack 3, Defense 1,
  Move 0. Nothing moves it and it is no living thing. Anyone may attack it;
  killing it is worth nothing.
- **The slap.** At once when it rises, and in every neutral turn, it
  attacks the unit of a player on the eight tiles around it with the
  **fewest Hit Points** (a tie to the lowest unit ID), of any seat, its
  Summoner's own included, and of any form, ships included: an ordinary
  attack with retaliation. Its kills are credited to nobody and pay no
  Favour.
- **It sinks** at the end of the third neutral turn after it rose, so it
  slaps four times at most.
- **Grab.** "The unit it slapped cannot leave its side." After each slap
  the Tentacle holds the unit it slapped, while both live and the unit
  stands next to it. Every step of a held unit's Move must be a tile next
  to that Tentacle. Anything else that takes the unit from its side ends
  the grab (a shove, a swap, a Boo!, the advance after a kill), and so
  does the Tentacle's death, its sinking, or its next slap on another
  unit.

On arrival it kills a full-HP Catapult and a full-HP Initiate (7 HP since
`7r85`), and leaves a Marksman at 2 and a Fighter at 4 (taking 4).

**Pamphlets (the Initiate).** "Have you heard the good news about the
Ancient Ones? The village joins at once." An Initiate that ends its Move on
the center of a village nobody owns may capture it **in the same turn**.
Every other capture rule holds: a player's city still takes a turn, and a
frog does not preach.

### 26.13 Resolution order

**A Cult seat's Start Turn** adds these steps to
[section 3](#3-players-turns-and-victory):

1. With the Mind Control cooldowns, before the Shield recharge: the seat's
   Ribbit and Switcheroo cooldowns count down.
2. After Plague and its chains, the watched units are judged (a channeller
   Plague hurt is disrupted), and then **the channel check** runs for each
   bound daemon in unit-ID order (an Imp held by its own strands or by a
   neighbour's Brood, `pulp_wars-mch9.36`; a Gibbering Mass by its strands
   or its Doorstep, `pulp_wars-mch9.37`). Each daemon that breaks loose rampages at
   once, with its deaths and their consequences, and is Furious for the
   turn. Then (`pulp_wars-mch9.32`) **the trickle** (+1 for each own
   Summoner whose strand held, for a daemon still bound, up to the cap) and
   **Hunger** (2 for each still bound Herald, in unit-ID order; one that
   cannot be paid is Unbound at once, rampages, and is Furious). Then the
   seat's strands and grips are cleared.
3. **The rituals**, each completing or fizzling in leader unit-ID order:
   Star-fall's damage; the Great Summoning's consumption or block and the
   Herald's arrival. What one completion hurts is disrupted before the
   next: a star takes chanters out of the seat's second circle, and breaks,
   for the next check, the strand of a channeller of a Herald that arrived
   just before it.
4. Then the existing steps from Egg hatching on. A Cowed city pays no
   income.

So a Cult's own star that hurts its own channellers breaks those strands
for the **next** check, not for the one just made.

**End Turn.** A daemon stops being Furious when the seat in whose Start
Turn it broke loose ends its turn. A Cowed city stops being Cowed, and a
frog stops being a frog, when its owner's turn ends.

**The neutral turn** ([section 2.7](#27-map-curiosities)) runs every
neutral unit in unit-ID order: the Giant Spider, camp guards, Bigfoot,
Unbound daemons, and Tentacles. Each Tentacle's count goes down at the end
of the neutral turn. An Unbound daemon or a Tentacle on the board is enough
for a neutral turn, on a board with or without map curiosities.

**Elimination.** When a Cult seat is eliminated, its bound daemons are
Unbound in that moment (not Furious) and stay on the board, like its
Unbound ones; its other units are removed as for any seat, and its Favour
is gone. A Cult seat with a bound Herald and no city is eliminated like any
seat.

### 26.14 Interactions with other rules

| Other rule                                            | Ruling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Freeze                                                | A Frozen cultist is disrupted and cannot channel, help a summoning, or chant. A bound Horror can be Frozen; the Herald never; an Unbound daemon takes no status. A Cold Snap on a circle breaks every chanter it freezes. A Frozen Thing's grip fails.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Plague and Bitten                                     | Plague damage at the Cult's Start Turn comes before the check and breaks every plagued channeller, and a Plagued Idol Bearer's idol is down. A Plagued or Bitten own unit cannot be Sacrificed or consumed. A Bitten enemy can be Seized; it does not rise. No daemon is ever Plagued or bitten.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Graves and risings                                    | A Sacrifice, a Seizure, and a consumption leave no Grave and no rising; a daemon and a Tentacle leave none either. Every other death of a Cult unit, and the victims of a star, a rampage, and a Tentacle, leave Graves as any death.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Eggs                                                  | An Egg is never Sacrificed, Seized, frogged, swapped, scared, or consumed; one on the mark blocks the Herald's arrival. Star-fall, a rampage, and a Tentacle's slap hit Eggs as units.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Barricades and mounds                                 | No Horror, Herald, or Tentacle appears on one, and one on the Great Summoning's mark blocks the arrival. Star-fall removes every Barricade in its area. A rampage walks round them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Area hits (Whirl, Thump, Stomp, Sweep, blasts, bombs) | Each hit is a loss of Hit Points and disrupts every cultist it reaches.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Burrowed units                                        | A burrowed unit is not on the board: never a rampage's target, a star's victim, or a Seizure. A surfacing eruption disrupts the cultists it hurts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Kaboom and death blasts                               | A Sacrificed, Seized, or consumed exploding unit is removed and never explodes; one a daemon or a star kills explodes as usual. A frog cannot Kaboom.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Candy statuses, Crumbs, Bounce                        | Splat, Stuck, and Toothache disrupt a cultist. A Sacrifice, a Seizure, and a consumption leave no Crumbs. The Herald is never Stuck, Splatted, given Toothache, or bounced; a bound Horror may be. A Top-Up cures a frog. A Jawbreaker is never swapped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Mind Control and the Tractor Beam                     | A mind-controlled cultist has changed owner and a pulled one is moved: both are disrupted. No summoned unit is mind-controlled or pulled. A Brain may be Seized, and its controlled unit is released. A mind-controlled Cult unit keeps only its unit's tricks ([section 26.1](#261-roles-robed-cultists-and-labels)).                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Giants' signatures                                    | A swallowed cultist is off the board (disrupted); no daemon is Swallowed. A Thunder Stomp and a trample disrupt the cultists they hit. A Crushing Shove crushes a Herald or a Gibbering Mass (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`), which does not yield. A status from the Thing's own attack fails its grip.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Curiosities                                           | An Unbound daemon and a Tentacle act in the neutral turn and are monsters to every seat's previews (`previewMonsterV7`). A daemon never heals at a Fountain or a Wishing Well and is never promoted at a Shrine. A rampage never steps onto a curiosity tile or through a gate; a unit that would come through a gate onto the Herald is blocked. A bound daemon's kill of the Spider, a guard, or Bigfoot pays its bounty in Favour and in Coins.                                                   |
| Score and play modes                                  | Favour is not scored (nor what the cap or Hunger takes). A daemon counts in its seat's Army while commanded. A Sacrifice and a consumed own unit are no Loss and end a flawless game; so does a daemon that breaks loose. A Seizure and a consumed enemy are kills. The kills of an Unbound daemon and of a Tentacle are nobody's.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Achievements                                          | Slayer counts a Summoner's Seizures and a daemon's kills like any unit's. Muster counts the Cult's trained kinds; a daemon has no price and is not counted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Capture and siege                                     | Every Cult land unit and every bound daemon but the Imp and the Gibbering Mass captures (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`, `pulp_wars-mch9.37`: each besieges a hostile center it stands on and captures nothing); a city a daemon takes does not become its home. An Unbound daemon never besieges or captures. An Initiate captures a neutral village on arrival.                                                                                                                                               |
| Movement (Drag)                                       | A unit that begins a Move beside a hostile Gibbering Mass moves one tile (`DRAGGED`): an Overrun step, an Escape, a Charge!'s run-up, a Sugar Rush Move, and a Bat Escape included; an advance after a kill, a shove, a swap, a pull, and a Boo! are no Move. A burrowed unit is not beside a Mass, and surfacing is no Move (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`).                                                                                                                                                  |
| Boats and embarking                                   | The Cult's boats are the Human boats. An embarked cultist is no robed cultist: embarking breaks its strand, and it neither channels nor chants. Star-fall hits ships and embarked units; a Tentacle may rise on water and slaps ships; a rampage never goes for a unit afloat.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Missions                                              | A `MISSION` setup accepts a Cult seat, which may start with Favour, clamped to the cap of 30 ([section 2.6](#26-mission-setup)). The hidden lab `LAB_CULT_MID` (revision 2 since `7r85`) stages the roster with 12 Favour; it is built and has not been played. Campaign mission 10 (`FRONTIER_10`, revision 4, `pulp_wars-mch9.46`) seats the redesigned lodge with Gibbering Masses and 8 Favour ([campaign, section 11.17](CAMPAIGN.md#1117-mission-10-on-the-redesigned-cult-pulp_wars-mch946)). |
| Nine seats                                            | The Cult is the ninth faction, so a match has 2 to 9 players ([section 2.1](#21-match-setup)). With more seats there are more enemy turns between two checks: more chances to break a strand.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

### 26.15 Commands, events, errors, and queries

The exact shapes, the order of events, and who is shown each event are in
the six step notes of [section 1](#1-identity-and-compatibility) (the Cult
registration, Favour, the channel, Unbound, rituals and the Herald, hexes
and tricks). In summary:

- **Commands.** `SACRIFICE` and `SEIZE` (`unitId`, `victimUnitId`),
  `OFFERING` (`cityId`), `SUMMON` (`unitId`, `daemon` `IMP`, `HORROR`, or
  `MASS`, `helperUnitId` for a Horror or a Mass only, `at`; the `daemon`
  and the helperless Imp since `pulp_wars-mch9.36`, the Mass since
  `pulp_wars-mch9.37`; offered in tile, Summoner, daemon (the Imp first,
  then the Horror, then the Mass), then helper order),
  `CHANNEL` (`unitId`, `daemonUnitId`; also Bind again), `ANCHOR`
  (`unitId`, `cultistUnitId`), `BOO` (`unitId`),
  `BEGIN_RITUAL` (`ritual` `STARFALL` or `GREAT_SUMMONING`, `unitId`,
  `at`), `JOIN_CHANT` (`unitId`, `leaderUnitId`; `pulp_wars-mch9.34`),
  `PROCLAIM` (`unitId`, `cityId`), `RIBBIT` and `SWITCHEROO`
  (`unitId`, `targetUnitId`), and `TENTACLE` (`unitId`, `at`; the
  Summoner's). (`PICK_ME` was removed with the Chosen, `7r85`.) Pamphlets is the ordinary `CAPTURE`, and the Herald's two
  attacks the ordinary `ATTACK`.
- **State.** The `cult` block: `favour`, `strands`, `grips`, `rituals`,
  `cowed`, `frogs`, `hexCooldowns`, and `tentacles` (`taunts` was removed
  with Pick Me!, `7r85`, and `idols` with Behold!'s command,
  `pulp_wars-mch9.33`: the aura is read from the board).
  A summoned unit has the key `summoned` (`HORROR`, `HERALD`, `TENTACLE`,
  or, since `pulp_wars-mch9.36`, `IMP`, stored as a `RAIDER`, and, since
  `pulp_wars-mch9.37`, `MASS`, stored as a `GUARD`)
  and a stored mechanical role that no rule reads; an Unbound daemon and a
  Tentacle have an entry in the neutral registration (`monsters`). A city
  has `offeredPopulation` once it has made an Offering.
- **Events.** `FAVOUR_GAINED` (source `SACRIFICE`, `SEIZE`, `OFFERING`,
  `DAEMON_KILL`, `CONSUMPTION`, or, since `pulp_wars-mch9.32`, `TRICKLE`;
  `MARTYR` was removed at `7r85`; its `forfeited` is the part lost above
  the cap) and `FAVOUR_SPENT` (purpose `SUMMON_HORROR`, `GREAT_SUMMONING`,
  `HUNGER`, or, since `pulp_wars-mch9.36`, `SUMMON_IMP`, and, since
  `pulp_wars-mch9.37`, `SUMMON_MASS`), both shown to
  every player; `UNIT_SACRIFICED`, `UNIT_SEIZED`, `OFFERING_MADE`;
  `DAEMON_SUMMONED` (`role` `IMP`, `HORROR`, or `MASS`; an Imp's
  `helperUnitId` is null, and its one `STRAND_FORMED` follows), `STRAND_FORMED`,
  `STRAND_BROKEN`, `ANCHOR_GRIPPED`,
  `ANCHOR_BROKEN`, `UNITS_SCARED` (`IDOL_RAISED` and `IDOL_DROPPED` were
  removed with Behold!'s command, `pulp_wars-mch9.33`); the combat
  preview's `idolHalved` (the shield wall) and its `noRetaliationReason`
  `SWARMED` (an Imp's Swarm, `pulp_wars-mch9.36`);
  `DAEMON_UNBOUND` (reason `STRANDS`, `HUNGER`, or `ELIMINATED`),
  `DAEMON_BOUND`; `RITUAL_BEGUN`, `CHANT_JOINED`
  (`unitId`, `leaderUnitId`, the star's `damage` after the join; shown to
  its seat and to every viewer that sees the joiner or the Stargazer),
  `RITUAL_DISRUPTED`,
  `RITUAL_FIZZLED` (reason `LEADER`, `CHANTERS`, or `BLOCKED`),
  `STAR_FELL`, `UNIT_CONSUMED`, `HERALD_ARRIVED`, `CITY_COWED`;
  `UNIT_FROGGED`, `UNITS_SWAPPED`, `TENTACLE_ROSE`, `UNIT_GRABBED`,
  `TENTACLE_SANK` (`PICK_ME_SHOUTED` was removed at `7r85`).
  `UNIT_DIED.cause` gains
  `SACRIFICED`, `CONSUMED`, `STARFALL`, and `SANK`.
- **Errors.** `INSUFFICIENT_FAVOUR`; `SACRIFICE_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`,
  `VICTIM`, `DAEMON`, `CONTROLLED`, `PLAGUED`, `BITTEN`); `SEIZE_NOT_LEGAL`
  (`EMBARKED`, `VICTIM`, `IMMUNE`, `HEALTHY`, `NO_HOLDER`);
  `OFFERING_NOT_LEGAL` (`LEVEL`, `POPULATION`); `SUMMON_NOT_LEGAL`
  (`EMBARKED`, `TECHNOLOGY` (a Mass without Gibbering Masses,
  `pulp_wars-mch9.37`), `HELPER`, `TILE`); `CHANNEL_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`,
  `DAEMON`, `FURIOUS`, `RANGE`); `ANCHOR_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`,
  `GRIPPING`, `CULTIST`); `BOO_NOT_LEGAL`
  (`NOBODY`); `RITUAL_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `MOVED`, `CHANTERS` (the
  Great Summoning's only), `TILE`); `JOIN_CHANT_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`,
  `CHANTING`, `ACTED`, `STATUS`, `RITUAL`, `ADJACENT`);
  `PROCLAIM_NOT_LEGAL` (`CITY`, `RANGE`, `COWED`); `RIBBIT_NOT_LEGAL`
  (`EMBARKED`, `COOLDOWN`, `TARGET`, `IMMUNE`, `FROG`, `RANGE`);
  `SWITCHEROO_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`, `TECHNOLOGY`, `COOLDOWN`, `TARGET`,
  `IMMUNE`, `RANGE`, `CENTER`, `TILE`); `TENTACLE_NOT_LEGAL` (`EMBARKED`,
  `TECHNOLOGY`, `EXISTS`, `TILE`); `UNIT_FROGGED` (a frog's refused
  command; `PICK_ME_NOT_LEGAL` and `ATTACK_TAUNTED` were removed at
  `7r85`); `ATTACK_AWESTRUCK` (`unitId`, the Idol Bearer; an awestruck
  unit's attack on anybody else, `pulp_wars-mch9.33`, which also removed
  `BEHOLD_NOT_LEGAL`); the
  movement reasons `GRABBED` and (`pulp_wars-mch9.37`) `DRAGGED`, and
  `GATE_BLOCKED`. A Cowed city's refused
  action is `CITY_ACTION_SPENT`.
- **Queries and previews.** The public command query offers exactly the
  commands the reducer accepts. `previewSacrificeV7`, `previewSeizeV7`,
  `previewOfferingV7` (each with the Favour `forfeited` above the cap and
  the capped `favourAfter`), `previewSummonV7` (taking the daemon and the
  helper, null for an Imp: its price, HP, Control, and strands),
  `previewChannelV7` (the daemon's
  strands before and after, whether it binds, and, for an Imp, the `brood`
  its strand would hold, `pulp_wars-mch9.36`), `previewAnchorV7`,
  `previewBooV7`, `previewBeginRitualV7`,
  `previewJoinChantV7` (the star before and after the join, and the units
  it newly kills), `previewRitualV7` (a star's damage and hits, with its
  joiners; whether the Herald
  `ARRIVES`, `CONSUMES`, or is `BLOCKED`), `previewProclaimV7`,
  `previewRibbitV7`, `previewSwitcherooV7`, and `previewTentacleV7`
  describe an offered command and are null otherwise.
  `previewRampageV7` gives the unit a visible daemon goes for, the `step`
  of the target rule that chose it (1 to 4, `pulp_wars-mch9.35`), and its
  walk (`exact` is false when an unexplored tile could hold a nearer unit);
  `previewMonsterV7` answers for an Unbound daemon and a Tentacle;
  `attacksLeftV7` is a Herald's attacks left; `heraldHungerDueV7` is the
  Hunger a seat owes at its next check; `previewWardenV7` is what a visible
  Idol Bearer's aura does now (whether its idol stands, the own units it
  shields, the enemies it holds Awestruck) and `publicAwestruckBearersV7`
  the bearers that bind a unit (`previewBeholdV7` was removed,
  `pulp_wars-mch9.33`); `publicDraggingMassV7` is the Gibbering Mass that
  drags a visible unit, and `publicDaemonHeldV7` whether a daemon is held
  without strands of its own (Brood or Doorstep; `pulp_wars-mch9.37`). The combat preview of a
  frog is exact, and an attack a frog forbids has none.
- **Fog.** A view carries the Favour of every Cult seat; the strands,
  grips, frogs, cooldowns, and Tentacles of the units its
  viewer sees; every visible daemon's Control and holding strands (which
  count the strands of cultists the viewer does not see), and for an Imp a
  Brood holds the Imp that holds it (`broodOf`), and a Gibbering Mass on
  its Doorstep (`doorstep`); the rituals it
  knows of (it sees a participant or has explored the mark); and the Cowed
  cities it sees.
- **Text harness** ([text-mode play](../validation/TEXT_PLAY.md)): the
  commands `.sacrifice.u<id>`, `.seize.u<id>`, `c<id>.offering`,
  `.imp.<x>,<y>` (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`), `.summon.u<id>.<x>,<y>` (a
  Horror with its helper), `.mass.u<id>.<x>,<y>` (a Gibbering Mass with its
  helper, `pulp_wars-mch9.37`), `.channel.u<id>`, `.anchor.u<id>`,
  `.boo`, `.starfall.<x>,<y>`, `.join.u<stargazer>`,
  `.summoning.<x>,<y>`, `.proclaim.c<id>`,
  `.ribbit.u<id>`, `.switch.u<id>`, and `.tentacle.<x>,<y>` (`.pickme`
  was removed at `7r85` and `.behold` with `pulp_wars-mch9.33`),
  and lines for Favour (`favour 12/30`, with the Hunger due at the next
  check, and what a gain lost above the cap), strands and Control (an Imp
  `held by the Brood of u<id>`, and the Imps a strand's Brood holds; a Mass
  `DOORSTEP: needs no strand here`), a dragged unit (`DRAGGED by u<id>`),
  the unit codes `Im` of an Imp and `Gm` of a Gibbering Mass, grips,
  a standing idol (`IDOL STANDS`, or `idol down`), an awestruck unit
  (`AWESTRUCK by u<id>`), a halved shot (`HALVED by the Idol Bearer`),
  Unbound daemons and their targets (with the step's reason, "a cultist
  within 2"), circles, Cowed cities, frogs, and
  Tentacles. The headless tools take `cult` (alias `cultists`) in
  `--factions`.

### 26.16 Normal AI, presentation, and balance

- **Normal AI** (`pulp_wars-mch9.9` to `mch9.12` and `mch9.27`, rebuilt
  for the Cult redesign by `pulp_wars-mch9.38` to `mch9.41`; no rule and
  no identity change): the Cult seat's play and every seat's play against
  the Cult, in [section 16](#16-normal-ai-summary) and in
  [Normal AI, the Cult seat](../architecture/NORMAL_AI.md#the-cult-seat).
  It is a baseline made by judgement on hand-built positions: no match was
  played to set a number in it. The Cult seat fights with its summons and
  keeps its casters behind them: it summons all three daemons (a Gibbering
  Mass beside a watched city or a threatened circle's standing idol, a
  Horror at the front, an Imp beside an own Imp or with a body for its
  strand, and the best it can at the cap), channels one Imp of each Brood,
  gives a Mass on its Doorstep no channeller, plays Swarm, feeds or
  releases a hungry Herald, places its Idol Bearers to shield its casters,
  casts Star-fall alone and joins the chant, and scores the Herald's
  advance ([the redesign, sections 12.5 to 12.7](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md#125-as-built-a-r1-the-army-rules-and-favour-pulp_wars-mch938)).
  Every seat's play against the Cult reads an Imp a Brood holds, and a
  Mass on its Doorstep, as held, and minds the warden, Awestruck, Drag,
  Swarm, the chanters, a hungry Herald, and the engine's Unbound target
  rule ([section 12.8](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md#128-as-built-a-r4-every-seat-against-the-new-cult-pulp_wars-mch941)).
- **Presentation** (`pulp_wars-mch9.17` to `mch9.19`, with the art of
  `pulp_wars-mch9.13` to `mch9.16`, `mch9.22`, and `mch9.23`; for the
  redesign `pulp_wars-mch9.42` to `mch9.44`, with the art of
  `pulp_wars-mch9.45`). Every seat's faction
  select offers the Cultists (`pulp_wars-mch9.20`: the tribe picker has
  nine cards, and a game seats up to eight opponents;
  [the screen flow](../ui/SCREEN_FLOW.md#current-ruleset-7-many-players-overlay)).
  Their owner colour is eldritch green
  (`#00ff78`), and their units, portraits, cities, buildings, ships,
  ground, and forest have their own art
  ([the Cult's art direction](../art/factions/CULT.md)). Every number and
  legal choice the interface shows comes from the public view, the offered
  commands, and the public previews:
  - **Favour** is a candle and "n / 30" beside the Coins of a Cult player,
    and in the leaderboard row of every Cult seat for everyone; the chip
    turns amber at the cap, and previews and notices say what a gain loses
    above it. At the Start Turn a candle flies from each Summoner that paid
    the trickle, and a bound Herald's card shows its "Hunger 2"
    (`pulp_wars-mch9.42`).
  - **Sacrifice, Seize, Summon, Channel, Anchor, Star-fall, the Great
    Summoning, Proclaim, Ribbit, Switcheroo, and the Tentacle** have one
    button each, and what they aim at is picked on the board
    ([board targeting](../ui/BOARD_TARGETING.md)), labelled with what it
    pays or does; a rite's mark is previewed first and then begun. The
    Summon button opens a chooser of the three summons with their prices,
    greying what cannot be called with the reason, and each summon is also
    its own tile badge (`pulp_wars-mch9.44`). **Join the chant** is a badge
    on the casting Stargazer (a candle with a plus) and a dock button, and
    previews the star's new damage (`pulp_wars-mch9.43`). Boo! is cast by
    its button (Behold! had one until it became the warden's aura,
    `pulp_wars-mch9.33`), and the Offering is a button of the city panel.
  - **On the board, for every player who sees it:** a green chain for each
    strand (red and parted when its cultist is out of reach), a candle over
    each channeller and chanter, pips under a daemon for its strands
    against its Control, a short green link from the channelled Imp to
    each Imp its Brood holds, a small house for the lit pip of a Mass on
    its Doorstep, a thin teal ring round each Gibbering Mass's eight tiles
    (Drag), the eye mark on the unit a daemon would go for (the loose
    daemon's card says why), a chalk ring round a standing idol with a
    small idol on each unit it shields and a tether from each enemy it
    holds Awestruck, Switcheroo's reach of 4 outlined while armed, a
    tentacle from a gripping Thing, the circle of a ritual with its mark
    and countdown and what a star will deal to each unit, a banner over a
    Cowed city, a frogged unit drawn as a frog with a small badge of what
    it was, and a Tentacle's arm round the unit it holds. A halved shot
    reads "Idol: half damage", an unanswered Imp attack "Swarmed: no
    strike back", and a dragged unit "Dragged: only one tile".
  - **End Turn** with a daemon short of its Control, or with a bound
    Herald its next Start Turn cannot feed, asks once.
  - **The Imp** and **the Gibbering Mass** (`pulp_wars-mch9.36`,
    `pulp_wars-mch9.37`; art `pulp_wars-mch9.45`) are drawn with their own
    sprites, Unbound looks, and portraits; a daemon a Brood or its
    Doorstep holds has its pip lit and no eye mark. The glossary explains
    Brood, Swarm, Doorstep, Drag, that the Mass holds its ground, and that
    neither captures.
  - The unit glossary has one sentence for every ability and status. The
    cues use the game's existing sounds. The Cult has its own theme music
    (`theme.cultists`, `pulp_wars-mch9.25`;
    [Sound](../ui/SOUND.md#theme-music)): a Cult player hears it in a
    match and on New game, where the Undead theme stood in before
    (`STAND_IN_THEME_FACTIONS_V1`, now empty).

  The details and the decisions taken are in
  [the spec, section 14.3](RULESET_7_CULTISTS.md#143-how-it-reads-on-the-board-without-text),
  [the redesign, section 13](RULESET_7_CULT_REDESIGN.md#13-interface),
  [board targeting](../ui/BOARD_TARGETING.md#38-the-cultists-the-channel-bead-pulp_wars-mch918),
  and [the screen flow](../ui/SCREEN_FLOW.md).

- **Balance.** Every number is the design's first guess: none was tuned,
  and no simulation was run for the faction (the user's standing rule).
  The head-to-head results quoted in the spec and in the redesign were
  re-run through the engine's combat preview by the engine steps and
  match. The one hand-played game on the redesigned Cult is campaign
  mission 10's retune (`pulp_wars-mch9.46`, authorised for that bead: an
  autopilot that loses and a hand-played win in round 16;
  [campaign, section 11.17](CAMPAIGN.md#1117-mission-10-on-the-redesigned-cult-pulp_wars-mch946)),
  which set no faction number. A hand-played fairness check with
  `LAB_CULT_MID` runs only if the user asks for it; any later pass is
  bound by the variance rules above.
